items.title: As Texas embraces carbon storage, a Black community questions the risks
items.summary_raw: On a rural road outside Beaumont, a Texas energy giant is preparing to pump carbon dioxide underground to permanently store it and keep the gas from contributing to global warming. The project could be the first of its kind to start operating in the state . It’s a long-awaited milestone for the oil and gas industry, which has touted carbon capture and storage as an important tool for cleaning up industry emissions. Texas lawmakers threw their support behind the technology , while state regulators spent years seeking permitting authority from the federal government to try to clear projects faster. The Texas Railroad Commission , which oversees the oil and gas industry, won that authority late last year and approved this Exxon Mobil project in September. But the nearby community of Cheek has asked commissioners to reconsider the permit decision. The area close to the project is predominantly Black, and many residents are working-class or elderly. People there don’t trust the company’s assurances that it will keep residents and their groundwater safe. Only a small number of carbon storage wells have been permitted so far across the United States, and some CO2-related accidents have already happened. Experts and community advocates have warned of the risk for pipeline accidents and potential underground leaks. Leaders in Cheek are concerned the injected carbon dioxide could contaminate groundwater or get into the air and suffocate them. They worry emergency responders won’t be…

items.title: Reconstruction of extreme temperature events in medieval Poland (1001–1500 CE) from documentary evidence
items.summary_raw: Abstract Understanding the frequency, intensity, and societal impacts of extreme weather is essential for reconstructing past climate variability, yet systematic documentary-based reconstructions remain remarkably limited for medieval Poland. To address this gap in pre-instrumental data, this study reconstructs extreme temperature-related weather and climate events in Poland between 1001 and 1500 CE utilizing historical documentary evidence. A total of 299 extreme events were verified and synthesized from 452 primary weather notes. To mitigate duplication, overlapping accounts of the same anomaly were cross-referenced and merged. Validated events were categorized into severe frost; cold waves; river, lake, and sea ice events; snow and snowstorms; and heat and warm waves, with each classified by intensity, duration, and source reliability. The findings reveal a clear dominance of cold-related extremes, particularly severe frost and cold waves. A significant increase in the frequency and clustering of these events is observed during the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries, peaking specifically in the 1440s and 1450s. This pattern aligns with the broader Central European transition into the early phase of the Little Ice Age. Spatial analysis indicates a concentration of recorded events in the Baltic Coast, Pomerania, and Silesia, though this partly reflects uneven source preservation in prominent historical economic centers. items.summary_raw: Early on a Saturday morning in May, Ruben Juarez took the 45-minute flight from Oʻahu to Maui, just like he’d done dozens of times over the past three years. This one felt different. Juarez landed in Kahului Airport with his partner, Alika Maunakea, and drove on a long winding highway beside the piercing blue ocean until they reached the Lahaina Comprehensive Health Center. A cool breeze wafted in from the Pacific less than half a mile below as they set up stations for blood collection, lung function tests, and mental health check-ins, directing a team of Ph.D. students and local healthcare providers. Then they waited for the fire survivors to arrive. Ruben Juarez, left, and Alika Maunakea are professors at the University of Hawaiʻi and co-leads of the Maui Wildfire Exposure Study. Keerti Gopal On August 8, 2023, Maui was hit with the deadliest wildfires the U.S. has seen in over a century. They killed at least 102 people, displaced nearly 13,000 residents, and destroyed more than 2,200 buildings. Three years later, just 15 percent have been rebuilt. Juarez, an economist, and Maunakea, a biomedical scientist, never expected to focus on disaster recovery. But after the fires, they were thrust into the space by the overwhelming scale of need. The two University of Hawaiʻi professors dreamed up the Maui Wildfire Exposure Study, or MauiWES, as a form of rapid response: an effort to track the impacts of the fires on survivors’ health. items.title: Enhancing technical capacity for scaling climate smart agriculture in Ethiopia
items.summary_raw: Climate-smart agriculture (CSA) has emerged as a central strategy for enhancing food security, strengthening climate resilience, and reducing greenhouse gas emissions in Ethiopia’s predominantly agrarian economy. Substantial national policy commitment through the CRGE strategy and Nationally Determined Contributions and the availability of proven CSA technologies, but their adoption and sustained scaling remain limited, revealing a persistent efficiency gap between potential benefits and on-the-ground implementation. This narrative review uses a structured, transparent search strategy to synthesize evidence from over 180 peer-reviewed and grey literature sources from Google Scholar, Scopus, and PubMed published between 2000 and 2025. After thematic screening for relevance to technical capacity constraints, climate smart agriculture, and agricultural innovation systems in Ethiopia, 111 key sources were included in the final synthesis. The review analyzes limitations at the research and development, extension and advisory services, farmer-level capacities, policy and institutional frameworks, and digital and data infrastructure levels. Evidence indicates that inadequate human capital, weak research extension farmer linkages, limited access to knowledge, inputs and finance, fragmented institutional coordination, and limited rural digital infrastructure and weak agricultural data integration systems collectively hinder effective CSA scaling. Drawing on international experience…

items.title: A pilot study integrating environmental simulation for climate responsive architecture and planning curricula
items.summary_raw: Abstract This paper extends pedagogic research on the use of environmental digital simulation in higher education by examining how digital tools within an architecture and planning studio can impact knowledge, skills, practices and professional attitudes towards climate-responsive design. This study developed as part of Arts and Humanities Research Council (AHRC) Future Island Island (FII) project that applied wider cross-disciplinary, community and industry engaged research toward enhancing the green transition of sustainable design practices and education in Northern Ireland. This study presented centres on a series of teaching workshops through which third-year (final year) architecture and planning undergrade students engaged with Rhino, Grasshopper and Ladybug Tools to interrogate environmental analysis. Applying their learning both cohorts subsequently translated these analyses into decisions for urban planning and building design. Drawing on eight semi-structured interviews, the findings indicate: (1) participants perceived increased confidence and a developing ability to interpret environmental simulation outputs; (2) persistent barriers, including hardware limitations, software installation challenges and the cognitive demands of visual programming; and (3) a marked and seemingly durable enhancement in sustainability literacy, accompanied by a stated intention to integrate simulation into future design practice. items.title: Indigenous leaders at COP31 say it’s past time to turn promises into action
items.summary_raw: The annual United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change gathering drew historic levels of Indigenous attendance in Belém, Brazil last year, leading some to dub it “the Indigenous COP.” But the event was marked by frustration and protest , with many Indigenous leaders calling it little more than a continuation of a longstanding pattern of exclusion from international negotiations. This year’s gathering in Antalya, Turkey, is billed as an “implementation” conference focused less on sweeping new pledges than on the procedural work of turning previous agreements into action. For Indigenous advocates, that makes COP31, which started November 9, a test of whether the promises made last year translate into tangible changes, including greater authority over climate action. “It is still a struggle,” said Edward Porokwa, who is Maasai and a member of the United Nations Permanent Forum on Indigenous Issues. “I’m yet to really determine whether there will be any more progress that is made in terms of realization of the rights of Indigenous people.” Indigenous advocates are pressing governments to follow through on their commitments to secure and strengthen Indigenous land rights on 400 million acres in tropical forest countries, provide $1.8 billion in funding , and respect rights to free, prior, and informed consent in the energy transition. Two-phase NEUROD1 pioneer activity synchronizes sensory neuronal differentiation and subtype specification
items.summary_raw: Temporal control of neuronal differentiation is essential for establishing stable neuronal identities, yet the transcriptional and epigenetic mechanisms underlying this process remain poorly understood. Using auditory neurons as an in vivo model, we investigate the role of the proneural factor NEUROD1 in regulating neuronal differentiation timing and subtype specification. To bypass early neuronal loss in germline Neurod1 deletion mutants, we generated a delayed, self-terminating conditional knockout mouse ( Neurod1ST ) that permits analysis of later differentiation stages. Integration of NEUROD1 chromatin binding and histone profiling at embryonic day (E) 11.5 with transcriptomic analyses across E11.5, E14.5, and E18.5 reveals a two-phase regulatory program during auditory neuron development that parallels dynamic Neurod1 expression. In the first phase, coinciding with Neurod1 upregulation during early neuronal differentiation, NEUROD1 preferentially binds putative enhancers of neuronal differentiation genes and promotes their transition to active chromatin states, consistent with pioneer factor activity. Loss of Neurod1 disrupts these epigenomic transitions, resulting in persistence of progenitor-like states with premature activation of differentiation and axonogenesis programs. People know who to ask for favors despite underestimating compliance
items.summary_raw: Whether and how people approach social interactions hinges on how they expect others to respond. Extensive social psychology research suggests that people are inaccurate interpersonal perceivers, overestimating negative responses (e.g., discomfort) and underestimating positive responses (e.g., appreciation) across a variety of social situations. However, this conclusion is based almost exclusively on mean-level bias analyses that obscure the dyadic nature of interpersonal judgment and rely on a narrow conceptualization of interpersonal accuracy. Leveraging research on favor-asking and anticipated compliance as an exemplar, we demonstrate that interpersonal accuracy takes multiple theoretically distinct forms, and that the prevailing conclusion that people misunderstand their influence over others—because they tend to underestimate compliance—is likely overgeneralized. Across four studies (13,196 directed dyadic ratings), we show that people accurately differentiate between who will comply with their favor requests (dyadic meta-accuracy) despite the average tendency to underestimate compliance (mean-level bias). This pattern emerged for specific and general favor requests, among well- and newly-acquainted individuals, and beyond what could be expected due to self-projection. Through this dyadic lens, people are highly adept judges of their influence over others, as they are able to target their requests toward individuals who are uniquely likely to acquiesce to them—and can…

items.title: ChREBP drives diabetic kidney disease, and its inhibition confers renal protection
items.summary_raw: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) represents a major medical burden. Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is a leading cause of CKD, but intracellular pathways that can be pharmacologically targeted are poorly defined. Using transcriptome screening of DKD model mice we found that a carbohydrate-responsive element–binding protein (ChREBP)-dependent transcriptional cascade is markedly up-regulated in diabetic kidneys. Genetic ablation of ChREBP in diabetic mice ameliorated DKD, establishing ChREBP as a potential causal driver. A chemical screen based on ChREBP transcriptional activity identified D-532 as a small-molecule inhibitor that is effective in human and rodent cells. Oral administration of D-532 protected multiple diabetic mouse models from DKD progression and suppressed ChREBP and its downstream targets, including genes associated with excessive reactive oxygen species production. These findings position ChREBP as a pharmacologically targetable transcriptional driver of DKD and provide proof of concept that ChREBP inhibition can confer renal protection.

items.title: Selectively disrupting lysine acetyltransferase p300 and ZEB1 interaction prevents tumor progression while enhancing antitumor immunity
items.summary_raw: Both p300 acetyltransferase inhibitors and bromodomain inhibitors show therapeutic promise in cancer, but they mostly exhibit limited efficacy and may elicit severe adverse effects due to their lack of targeting selectivity. Thus, selectively disrupting p300 interactions with specific pro-oncogenic targets that are specifically expressed in neoplastic cells could serve as a safe and effective strategy for cancer treatment. Here, we demonstrate that p300 interacts with the pro-oncogenic transcription factor, ZEB1, and catalyzes its acetylation at an evolutionarily conserved K80 residue, stabilizing its expression in aggressive cancer cells. Ectopic expression of wild-type ZEB1 (mostly in acetylated status) but not the acetylation-deficient ZEB1 mutant modulates cytokinome of cancer cells, creating an immune-suppressive tumor microenvironment to support cancer progression. Underlining the importance of ZEB1 posttranslational processing, the K80-acetylated transcription factor is highly expressed in human cancers where its high-level expression is associated with poor prognosis. Importantly, we identify a small molecule compound, WY6, that undergoes high-affinity binding to p300 TAZ2 domain (a domain critical for ZEB1 binding) and consequently disrupts ZEB1 binding to p300, thereby suppressing K80 acetylation. WY6 treatment of tumor cells effectively represses p300-mediated ZEB1 acetylation, promoting its ubiquitination and subsequent degradation. Moreover, in vivo, WY6…

items.title: Physical distancing to prevent influenza-like illness on a college campus: The eX-FLU trial
items.summary_raw: Public health recommendations often advise people to isolate when infected with influenza-like illness (ILI) with the goal of promoting physical distancing and limiting face-to-face interactions when risk of transmission is highest. Because isolation may have negative consequences, it is important to carefully assess whether encouragement to physically distance actually prevents cases of ILI. College campuses can be especially vulnerable to outbreaks of ILI and are ideal environments for assessing the impact of encouragement-to-physically-distance interventions. The eX-FLU cluster-randomized trial followed 579 students on a college campus over a ten-week period during flu season to evaluate such an intervention. Students in the trial were randomized to receive the intervention—encouragement to isolate in their dorm room when symptomatic for ILI—or control. Evaluating the effect of this intervention is challenging because of dependence between students in the trial and an anticipated spillover effect of the intervention. Moreover, while the intervention was designed to affect both face-to-face interactions and ILI infections, the effect on ILI infections is of primary public health interest. In this paper, a randomization-based testing procedure is proposed to assess the intervention effect specifically on ILI infections in the presence of dependent data and spillover effects. The testing procedure is shown theoretically and empirically to control the type I error rate and…

items.title: Emergent long-tailed dynamics in spin ice
items.summary_raw: In this study, we reveal long-tail dynamics spontaneously arising from a magnetic system. Specifically, we consider a classical spin system and demonstrate the emergence of a spin-ice physics when drive-induced heating is well suppressed. We show that at high driving frequencies, magnetic monopole excitations exhibit nonergodic stochastic dynamics characterized by power-law-distributed trapping times with long tails—a behavior that persists even in the absence of driving. At intermediate driving frequencies, the system eventually heats up to an infinite-temperature state. However, contrary to conventional wisdom of Floquet heating, the heating time in our model is extremely sensitive to different initial-state realizations and also follows a long-tailed power-law distribution, which arise specifically due to periodic driving. We show that an effective short-range attractive interaction between monopoles is responsible for the long-tailed distributions observed in both monopole and heating dynamics.

items.title: Elastic interactions of mechanically polarizable cells
items.summary_raw: Cells mechanically interact through the deformations they generate in their surrounding extracellular matrix. We present an analytical theory of the elastic interactions between cells that actively adapt their forces in response to local deformations of their environment. Cells are represented as localized contractile force generators, modeled as polarizable point force dipoles, whose adaptive forces are determined self-consistently with those of surrounding cells. Analysis of the associated elastic interaction energy identifies a generic short-ranged interaction arising from the mutual adaptation of cellular forces. This induced-dipole interaction is analogous to the van der Waals interaction between molecules and likewise is shown to be generally attractive for cells that enhance contractility in response to stretch. Furthermore, unlike the long-ranged elastic interaction between nonpolarizable force-dipoles, that peaks at intermediate matrix stiffness and then weakens as the matrix softens, the induced-dipole interaction strengthens monotonically as the matrix softens and can reverse the interaction from being repulsive at long cell distances to being attractive at short separations. Analytical calculations are presented to illustrate the mutual polarization of forces in pairs of interacting cells on a substrate. The identification of a generic, short-range cohesive elastic interaction between cells is important for understanding cell behavior at short separations and…

items.title: Dynamical geometric modes in non-Euclidean plates
items.summary_raw: Continuum elastic shells with residual stresses can exhibit complex motions that require vanishing elastic energy to excite, also called geometric zero modes, enabling them to be driven by weak and generic energy inputs. Despite recent interest in these modes, we understand very little about their dynamical properties. Plates with a curved, rather than flat, in-plane geometry, also called non-Euclidean plates, are one example in which residual stresses and geometry combine to produce a continuum of ground states. The plate can explore these states through a geometric zero mode when it has the shape of a minimal surface—a surface with zero mean curvature. We demonstrate that a non-Euclidean plate with the shape of a saddle minimal surface exhibits the predicted continuous stability, but this degeneracy is ultimately lifted by aging. Despite developing a preferred configuration, the zero mode remains the softest mode. Using a combination of analytical theory and experiments, we show that the elastodynamics of this soft mode is captured by the dynamics of a damped pendulum. A periodic driving uncovers resonance phenomena in this pendulum mode, such as small oscillations and steady rotations, but mixes with an additional flapping mode at high frequencies.

items.title: The affordability election delivered billions for public transit
items.summary_raw: In an election dominated by concerns about affordability, voters across the country overwhelmingly agreed to raise taxes to preserve or expand public transit. Out of 27 ballot measures supporting transit, 22 passed on November 3 , representing $27.4 billion in funding to rescue faltering systems and expand or build new ones. Some of the biggest wins of the night included voters in the San Francisco Bay Area staving off enormous cuts to Bay Area Rapid Transit and other regional systems, Coloradans backing new regional rail, and residents of Seattle and nearby Pierce County favoring expanded bus service. “It’s an indication that the public is willing to pay for these public transit improvements,” said Sohail Husain, a policy analyst at the Eno Center for Transportation. “That’s very telling –– especially in a world like today where people are concerned about affordability. I think people are still also concerned about mobility and having options to move.” Public transit has now fared well in the red wave of 2024 — when 19 out of 25 measures supporting transit passed — and this year’s blue wave. Although few candidates campaigned on the issue, the results could significantly alter policy. At the state level, transit advocates see opportunities to advance projects or simply get the government out of the way. Meanwhile, a Democratic majority in Congress will shape a major transportation infrastructure law that is up for renewal. Together, the results could remake how Americans…

items.title: The cozy radicalism of repair cafés
items.summary_raw: On an unusually cool and rainy Saturday morning in Decatur, Georgia, dozens of people filed into a warehouse at the back of a church parking lot, their arms full of what a less hopeful group might call junk. Some carried broken lamps, glitching electronics, or cracked furniture. Others walked in with tool boxes, multimeters for testing electric currents, and cans of WD-40. Beneath extension cords dangling from the rafters, they sorted themselves into smaller groups: the volunteer electricians, tailors, luthiers, carpenters, and at least one cutler (knife sharpener), commandeering nearby worktables and passersby as needed. That’s how Lilly Pettus ended up shoulder to shoulder with three strangers, their hands all pressing together the pieces of her family’s cracked dining room chair as wood glue hardened and a volunteer tightened a clamp. “This is so interesting,” a giddy Pettus said, inspecting for the first time the joints, one of them broken, that held together the chair she’d owned for decades. “You never even know how furniture is put together.” Lilly Pettus’s broken chair gets a hand from attendees at the Decatur repair café​. Nearby, a sign tracks repair progress during the event. Johnny Kauffman / Grist This is Decatur’s semi-regular repair café, one of a few hundred meetings like it across the United States. items.title: Editorial Board
Building the hydrogen future: Why announced projects fail to reach investment
A AMAZÔNIA NO TELEGRAM: UM DASHBOARD BASEADO EM MODELAGEM DE TÓPICOS BERT
items.summary_raw: The Amazon occupies a central position in contemporary disputes over climate, sovereignty, conservation, and development, which makes it fertile ground for disinformation narratives. This study presents a methodological strategy for exploring large volumes of text, applied to messages about the Amazon posted by public Telegram channels in a multilingual corpus (Portuguese, Spanish, and English). Building on a previous study, the research advances the application of BERT-based topic modeling, coupled with the construction of an interactive dashboard. The aim is to discuss how semantic representations, thematic clusters, and exploratory visualizations can support the interpretation of extensive and heterogeneous textual data. The dashboard makes it possible to observe topic evolution over time, hierarchical structures, inter-topic distances, and distribution across channels. We argue that combining machine learning, visualization, and qualitative analysis contributes to research in Information Science and climate disinformation, taking the Amazon as an empirical case study and offering a replicable workflow for other thematic corpora.

items.title: Ukraine–US university partnership: a unique humanitarian commitment in wartime
items.source_name: International Journal of Leadership in Education
items.summary_raw: Uniting as international collaborators, we examine a Ukraine–US university partnership advancing international study and humanitarian commitment amid wartime. This practice article analyses the development of this collaboration in conditions of war and globalization, asking: What early experiences and understandings of this interinstitutional partnership are associated with faculty contributions, development, and initial outcomes? Six faculty collaborators describe partnership building, research contributions, and joint programming within a crisis leadership context. As partners from Virginia Tech, US, and National Technical University, Ukraine, we reflect on the initiative’s emerging 4-year trajectory, drawing on scholarship in crisis leadership, international partnerships, and education in conflict zones. Grounded in shared leadership and dialogic practice, we present four illustrative snapshots from six faculty insiders, including the Ukrainian author’s perspective on contractual and programmatic development. The narrative is framed through lenses of partnership development, crisis leadership, motivational climate, and resilience. We conclude with challenges, limitations, and implications for sustaining international collaborations in conflict contexts.

items.title: Analysis of Attitude Toward Green Financing in Support Net Zero Emission by 2060 Based on the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB): A Perspective from MSMEs
items.summary_raw: Net Zero Emission (NZE) 2060 has become Indonesia’s national aspiration to achieve a carbon-neutral economy by 2060 that the banking sector has reinforced its role as a key catalyst in promoting environmentally sustainable economic activities, particularly through the provision of green credit, financing, and investment. This study examines the behavior of green MSMEs toward Green Financing in supporting NZE 2060 based on the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB). The research focuses on green MSMEs located in four districts/cities in the Special Region of Yogyakarta (DIY), aiming to analyze the determinants of their behavioral intention to access Green Financing. The study applies the 10-times rule sampling technique and collects primary data from 62 respondents using a Likert scale (1–5) questionnaire distributed via Google Forms. Data were analyzed using SmartPLS 4.0. The findings reveal that Attitude does not significantly influence Behavioral Intention among green MSMEs actors in accessing Green Financing.

items.title: Predicting termite risk to North Korean wooden architectural heritage using climate data
items.summary_raw: Termite damage to wooden architectural heritage is a growing concern under climate change, yet no assessment exists for North Korea, where field survey is currently impractical. Framed within the hazard-exposure-vulnerability paradigm of heritage risk assessment, we integrated climate data, GIS-based spatial analysis, a biological model of termite-driven wood decay, and regression analysis to assess risk to 67 heritage sites. Termites can potentially inhabit 62.1% of the land area, and 64 sites (95.5%) fall within this range, with an estimated above-ground activity period of 195.2 days. Using the Relative Termite Damage Potential Index and Jenks natural breaks, habitable sites were classified as 15 low-, 32 moderate- and 17 high-risk, and every World Heritage component in the country fell in the high-risk class. Regression on location explained 86.4% of the variance, risk increasing toward lower latitudes. This first assessment offers a transferable risk-assessment framework for heritage in regions with poor access.

items.title: Development of Distributed Energy Resource Control Technology to Alleviate Congestion in Power Grids
items.source_name: IEEJ Transactions on Electrical and Electronic Engineering
items.summary_raw: This paper provides an overview of the ‘Development of Flexible and Distributed Energy Resources Control Technology to Mitigate Congestion in Power Systems’ (FLEX DER Project), a demonstration project conducted by the New Energy and Industrial Technology Development Organization (NEDO) from 2022 to 2024. With the expected further advancement of photovoltaic systems into distribution systems, it is inevitable that local supply systems and distribution substations will experience periods of overload (grid congestion) due to reverse power flow. This project aims to alleviate grid congestion by utilizing distributed energy resources (DERs) as an alternative to facility reinforcement. It includes advanced use of DER, necessitating sophisticated information sharing between power system operators and aggregators. Considering existing DER utilization already in practical use, the requirements for the business flow, information sharing, and operational management systems necessary for realizing grid congestion mitigation were comprehensively investigated. Furthermore, field‐based demonstration tests were conducted to verify these elements. This paper describes the entire project, focusing on the considerations behind each part, the implications for practical application derived from the results, and outlines future prospects for maximizing the value of DERs based on a report prepared by NEDO and comparisons of the initiatives of other countries. © 2026 Institute of Electrical…

items.title: Cheap talkers or hard hitters? Political parties’ climate policy proposals
items.summary_raw: Parties are central to climate politics, yet we have little knowledge of their climate policy preferences beyond salience or ‘pro’ or ‘anti’ positions. This study develops a new measure of parties’ climate policy preferences based on whether they advance policy proposals, and the ‘soft’ and ‘hard’ quality of those proposals. It is argued that policy proposals are more ‘substantial’ than general climate-related content in political texts, and that ‘hard’ policies are more substantial than ‘soft’ policies as the former are less popular and therefore associated with higher political risks. The analysis of original data from 502 manifestos in 20 industrial democracies over four elections (2002–2022) finds that climate policy proposals – both pro- and anti-climate, and soft and hard – have become less prevalent. The study’s analysis of parties’ climate policy preferences shows that party ideology, size and incumbency help to explain variation in the prevalence of climate proposals.

items.title: ONDAS DE CONSPIRAÇÃO: DESINFORMAÇÃO CLIMÁTICA DURANTE AS ENCHENTES DE 2024
items.summary_raw: In 2024, devastating floods struck Rio Grande do Sul and, during the tragedy, online content circulated attributing the rains to a research program allegedly operated as a climate weapon. Conspiracy narratives recurrently associate the program with the manipulation of natural disasters. Climate Disinformation prevents climate action and collective mobilization while, in general, incorporates ideological repertoires, cultural values, and local beliefs. Drawing on contributions from Information Science to the study of climate disinformation, this study investigates the construction and dissemination of this narrative on social media. The corpus comprises data collected from Telegram, YouTube, and Instagram, and the analysis methodology combines thematic classification and timeline mapping. Results indicate the cross-platform activation of a global conspiratorial repertoire, thematic co-occurrences suggesting the employment of technopolitical explanation for the catastrophe, and distinct circulation patterns across platforms. The study contributes to the understanding of informational disputes surrounding extreme climate events and the epistemic displacement produced by conspiratorial narratives.

items.title: Sustainability as Emergent Outcome: How Entrepreneurs Navigate Constraint in British Columbia
items.summary_raw: Sustainable entrepreneurship scholarship treats environmental orientation as a strategic input that founders pursue and that ecosystems support. A computational analysis of a corpus assembled from 125 long-form transcript files featuring entrepreneurs in British Columbia produces a different finding. The methodology conveyed grounded coding with sentence-embedding representation, code co-occurrence networks, Markov sequence modelling, and bootstrap-validated regression. Therefore, within the analysis, the researchers identified a consistent discursive pattern in which constraint is the upstream condition that organises decision narratives, navigation is the variable response that distinguishes founder accounts, and sustainability appears as one contingent outcome framing among several others. The corpus comprises all eligible entrepreneur interviews available in the Innovation Fuel podcast archive at corpus lock, and the episodes were not selected for sustainability or climate content. Explicit climate-urgency language is absent from more than 90% of episodes, while substantive sustainability work appears through discourse on efficiency, circularity, and community stewardship. This asymmetry is theorised as sustainability as an emergent outcome, a complementary discursive mechanism that extends, rather than displaces, Sustainable Innovation Theory and the Triple Bottom Line for ventures whose narratives do not lead with a declared mission. The study identifies pivot framing…

items.title: Transition from fossil fuels to nuclear and renewable energy: Evidence from Japan
items.summary_raw: Japan has pledged carbon neutrality by 2050, yet energy production still accounts for 84% of its greenhouse-gas emissions, and only 33.4% (328.48 TWh) of its 2023 electricity generation came from nuclear and renewable sources. This paper asks how Japan's electricity generation can complete the transition from fossil fuels to nuclear and renewable energy. Using annual data for 1980-2023 from the World Bank, IMF, and the Statistics Bureau of Japan, we estimate an autoregressive log-growth model of electricity consumption driven by GDP per capita, median age, and population change, and project Japan's 2050 electricity consumption at approximately 1,000 TWh (999 TWh; range 900-1,000 TWh across specifications, sample horizons, and population paths). Closing the resulting clean-energy gap of roughly 469 TWh would require the equivalent of about 56 additional nuclear reactors of average current capability (8.41 TWh each), rising to about 67 at the capacity factors Japan has realized since Fukushima. Applying machine-learning facility-location methods (genetic and NSGA-II algorithms) to a benchmark 21-plant configuration, we show that siting new plants on Japan's least-populated coastlines reduces the population inside their emergency planning zones by roughly two orders of magnitude relative to naive placement, at an additional transmission cost of a few hundred million US dollars per year. Public acceptance, rather than engineering capacity, is the binding constraint on Japan's…

items.title: Exploring Canadian beef farmers' perceptions of participation in climate change mitigation: Insights from Prince Edward Island.
items.summary_raw: Beef farmers can play a significant role in reducing and sequestering greenhouse gas emissions through specific farm management practices. Understanding how farmers perceive this role is essential for effective knowledge exchange and communication strategies that promote climate change mitigation. This study investigates how beef farmers in Prince Edward Island (PEI), Canada, perceive their involvement in farm-level mitigation efforts. Using identity theory as a framework, the study conducted a framing analysis to examine how participating farmers communicated their actions through four identity lenses: productivist, conservationist, hero, and scientist. Through purposive sampling, nine in-depth interviews were conducted with PEI beef farmers actively engaged in mitigative practices. Findings reveal that farmers often drew on multiple identities, with the productivist frame emerging most prominently. To foster broader engagement in climate mitigation, communication strategies should reflect the range of identities farmers associate with. Future research should explore perceptions among those not currently participating in mitigative practices.

items.title: Climate Change Adaptation Governance in Chad: Institutional Challenges and Pathways toward Environmental Sustainability
items.source_name: Journal of Geography Environment and Earth Science International
items.summary_raw: Chad combines extreme exposure to climate variability with some of the weakest adaptive capacity in the world, yet the governance arrangements through which adaptation is planned, financed and delivered in the country have rarely been examined as an integrated whole. Existing scholarship is concentrated on the hydrology of Lake Chad, on the security crisis in the Lake Chad Basin or on the Sahel as a generic region, leaving the national and subnational institutions of adaptation comparatively neglected. This critical narrative review synthesises peer-reviewed literature, scholarly book chapters and authoritative institutional documents published between 2001 and 5 September 2026, identified through multidisciplinary, francophone and institutional sources and appraised for relevance, methodological transparency, contextual specificity and credibility. The evidence is organised around six analytical themes: the contested climate-risk evidence base; the national policy and institutional architecture; adaptation finance; sectoral arenas including pastoralism, land restoration, wetlands, urban flood risk, health and gender; the climate–security nexus; and pathways toward sustainability. Four findings emerge with reasonable confidence. First, Chad has accumulated a layered set of adaptation instruments, including a national adaptation programme of action, an updated nationally determined contribution and a first national adaptation plan, but implementation remains weak because…

items.title: RenovaBio, environmental efficiency scores, and the cost of debt: evidence from Brazilian biofuel firms
items.summary_raw: Purpose This study aims to investigate whether the environmental efficiency scores assigned to Brazilian biofuel firms under the RenovaBio program affect their cost of debt. Specifically, it examines whether a regulated, standardized and externally verified environmental-performance metric can influence creditors’ risk assessments and borrowing conditions in an emerging economy, with particular emphasis on the highly leveraged Brazilian sugar-energy sector. Design/methodology/approach This study uses panel data from Brazilian biofuel-producing firms participating in RenovaBio, covering the 2020/2021, 2021/2022 and 2022/2023 crop years. Financial data were obtained from Balanços Patrimoniais and Valor Pró, while environmental efficiency scores and biofuel information came from the ANP. The relationship between RenovaBio efficiency scores and the cost of debt was estimated using panel regressions, with a random-effects specification as the main model, robust standard errors clustered at the firm level and additional robustness checks using lagged RenovaBio scores. Findings The results show that RenovaBio environmental efficiency scores are negatively associated with the cost of debt, but the relationship is not statistically significant. This suggests that creditors in the Brazilian sugar-energy sector do not yet systematically incorporate these environmental performance signals into lending conditions. Firm size and asset tangibility are associated with lower borrowing costs…

items.title: Research on the Coordinated Development of Urban Green Infrastructure Construction and Carbon Neutrality
items.source_name: Transactions on Environment Energy and Earth Sciences
items.summary_raw: This study systematically explores the intrinsic mechanism and implementation path of the coordinated development of urban green infrastructure (UGI) and carbon neutrality. Based on the four-dimensional analysis framework of input carbon effect synergy institutional guarantee, the contribution characteristics of UGI to carbon neutrality were revealed through remote sensing inversion, model simulation, and multiple case comparisons. Indirect carbon reduction is significantly higher than direct carbon sequestration, becoming the dominant path; In the landscape pattern, compact clustered patches have both carbon fixation and emission reduction advantages, while their shape complexity offsets their carbon fixation gains due to the increase in carbon emissions; The configuration of institutional tools is closely related to carbon performance, and the combination of mandatory greening indicators and incentive policies can enhance synergistic benefits. Research shows that incremental expansion cities should prioritize accumulating carbon fixed scale, while stock optimization cities should focus on spatial pattern adjustment to amplify indirect emission reduction benefits.

items.title: From Narratives That No Longer Persuade to Those That Enchant Again: An Analysis of Narratives of Fury in Polarized Contexts in the United States, Brazil, El Salvador, and Argentina
items.summary_raw: ABSTRACT The main objective is to analyze the variation in the resonance and echo of outrage narratives within agenda setting, consensus building, and policy institutionalization in Argentina, Brazil, the United States, and El Salvador 2017–2025. The article employs a mixed‐methods design grounded in the Narrative Policy Framework. This methodology combines qualitative content analysis—to identify narrative structure and strategy—with quantitative content analysis that codes resonance (the alignment of narrative structure with core beliefs) and echo (the propagation and polarization based on the frequency of narrative strategies in the analyzed speeches) on an ordinal scale. The main findings indicate that while these narratives are initially effective in mobilizing support and shifting the policy agenda, they tend to exacerbate polarization and hinder the construction of sustainable consensus, ultimately affecting the institutionalization of public policies.

items.title: Solar Energy Landscape of Pakistan: Resource Potential, Deployment, Policy Framework, and Future Directions
items.source_name: Journal of Energy and Power Technology
items.summary_raw: Pakistan encounters complex issues in its electric infrastructure, as demand increases with growing reliance on foreign oil and gas, while abundant solar potential remains underutilized across the country, and tariff instability, coupled with subsistence concerns, intensifies systemic stresses. Potential far exceeds practical application, as resources are left underutilized. Starting with an overview, this paper explores solar energy development in Pakistan from various perspectives: resource abundance, technological routes, adoption trends, economics of technology choices, policy frameworks, and barriers to implementation. Out of the 923 works retrieved from the IEEE Xplore and Scopus databases over the period 2015-2026, 105 peer-reviewed papers were identified through systematic screening and snowballing for final analysis. This review makes three contributions. First, it compiles the techno-economic indicators (cost of energy, payback period, and performance ratio) reported by a subset of the reviewed studies across residential, institutional, and utility-scale applications. These values are reported as published in each study, under differing system configurations, currencies, cost years, and assumptions; they are not normalised and should not be interpreted as results of a single standardised comparison. Second, it demonstrates that interdependent feedback loops of import reliance, financial instability, political uncertainty, and grid constraints determine barriers to…

items.title: Houses of pain: Paying the energy poverty premium for energy inefficiency and inequity in Hungary
items.summary_raw: This article utilizes the energy affordability ratio and the energy equity threshold to quantify the energy poverty premium in the Hungarian household sector. The focus on equity meets a call to tailor policy solutions to individual needs, in a similar manner to other sectors, such as health, education, and the environment. The novel arrangement of these quantitative methods enables the identification of households that do and do not pay an equitable amount for energy services. The calculations are based on required energy expenditures according to the energy rating of the buildings, instead of the actual energy expenditures. It can be stated that despite regulated and highly subsidized energy prices in Hungary, which are applied uniformly across all households, they generate unequal financial burdens due to the poor energy efficiency of the building stock and low disposable income. There is persistent and onerous energy inequity for almost all Hungarian households. While the median energy affordability ratio is 4.33%, the ratio varies widely across households, with a maximum of 107.27%. The energy equity threshold is 270 kWh/m 2 a, above which energy poverty is significantly present. Five particularly vulnerable social groups were identified in our study: 1) single person households with at least one dependent child, 2) other single person, 3) pensioner, 4) unemployed, and 5) other economically inactive households. We can conclude that assessing differences in energy…

items.title: Declining environmental predictability erodes reproduction in a tropical seabird
items.summary_raw: Seasonal breeders often depend on predictable resource pulses, yet climate change may alter reliability without shifting average timing. Here, using satellite chlorophyll records and two decades of individual breeding data for a tropical seabird, we show that weakened breeding synchrony and declining and less consistent reproductive success were associated with increasingly variable bloom timing without a consistent directional shift. Focusing on average timing alone could mean that climate impacts on species are overlooked. The authors show that, for a tropical seabird model species, winter–spring phytoplankton blooms kept a stable mean timing but became more variable between years. Breeding synchrony weakened and reproductive success declined and became less consistent over the same two decades.

items.title: Research on the Impact of Environmental Protection Tax Incentives on Enterprises' Green and Low-Carbon Transformation
items.source_name: Transactions on Environment Energy and Earth Sciences
items.summary_raw: As a major tax-collecting nation and one of the key contributors to global environmental governance, China's tax policies have attracted worldwide attention, whilst its environmental governance efforts have also come under scrutiny. To date, in the process of promoting sustainable and green development, China has introduced a range of tax measures, including the replacement of pollution discharge fees with an environmental protection tax, the establishment of a systematic framework comprising 56 green tax incentives to support green development, and the passage of the 'Ecological and Environmental Code of the People's Republic of China' in 2026. The introduction of environmental tax incentive policies is intended to facilitate a comprehensive green and low-carbon transition in economic and social development and to implement a sustainable development strategy. This paper delves further into the relationship between these two aspects and examines the mechanisms through which environmental tax incentives directly or indirectly influence enterprises' green and low-carbon transition. The study employs empirical analysis using listed data on environmental tax incentives for companies from 2008 to 2024, alongside data on green patents applied for by these companies. The study found that environmental tax incentives significantly promote enterprises' green and low-carbon transition, while internal factors—including cash levels and operating costs—as well as macro-level external…

items.title: Between hope and exhaustion: the emotional impacts of COP participation on young climate delegates
items.summary_raw: Abstract Given the increasing recognition of the vitality of youth inclusion to keep international climate negotiations progressive and accountable, there has been much recent attention focused on improving formal access for young people in the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC). However, what should be considered as meaningful inclusion must extend beyond physical presence to encompass the conditions under which individuals are able to engage, contribute, and feel heard. Very little has been published on the actual experiences of youth delegates to the UNFCCC – an experience that is often exhausting and can be highly demoralising. Thus this paper seeks to explore the emotional experience of attending a UNFCCC Conference of the Parties (COP). We document the multifaceted, intersectional, and long term forms of emotional labour young people, like ourselves, do to participate in COP and posit ways to promote sustainable communities of young delegates.

items.title: “All these teachers is my sons”: a teacher educator’s narrative on Black language, Black authority, and lesson planning for Black LGBTQ+ youth in ELA classrooms
items.summary_raw: Purpose This study aims to explore the challenges to assuming authority as a Black teacher educator and what this means for helping teachers design culturally sustaining ELA lessons for Black LGBTQ+ youth. Design/methodology/approach As a reflective narrative, this paper is grounded in the author’s experiential knowledge as a teacher educator and researcher committed to improving the schooling experiences of Black LGBTQ+ youth. The author uses research on Black language and queer of color critique as a way to frame this reflective exploration. Findings Black language shapes the work of Black teacher educators, especially with regard to perspectives on exercising authority with K-12 teachers. Research limitations/implications As a teacher educator’s narrative centered around one personal experience, this paper offers specific insight rather than broad, generalizable implications. This articicle illuminates the need for more teacher educator narratives and scholarly explorations of how teacher educators’ positionalities inform their work. Practical implications This piece helps ELA teachers understand the kind of preparation, intentions, and rituals needed for effective lesson planning for LGBTQ+ students of color. Social implications Language matters, even at the level of teacher education, as it shapes the ways in which teacher educators write, research and engage with other teachers. Originality/value Operationalizing a queer of color critique theoretical approach to…

items.title: How Online Discussions Triggered by Documentaries Shape Young Adults' Cultural Product Preferences: A Case Study of Exploring the Unknown with Wang YIBO
items.source_name: International Journal of Social Science Studies
items.summary_raw: The pervasive integration of digital platforms has transformed how cultural products influence consumer preferences, with online discourse serving as a critical mediator. However, international scholarship lacks a precise, theory-driven model linking the quantitative metrics of this online buzz to subsequent behavioral intentions, particularly in non-Western entertainment contexts. This study addresses this gap by investigating how online buzz generated by the documentary Exploring the Unknown With Wang YIBO is associated with young Chinese viewers' preferences for related cultural products. Grounded in the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), the research employs a quantitative design integrating secondary social media data with a cross-sectional survey (N = 372). Structural equation modeling analysis indicates that the association between buzz metrics (discussion volume, sentiment polarity) and behavioral intention is consistent with full mediation by TPB constructs. Discussion volume was positively associated with subjective norm and perceived behavioral control, while sentiment polarity was most closely associated with attitude. The study provides actionable insights for global content creators and cultural policymakers, emphasizing the need to strategically nurture both the volume and sentiment of organic online discourse.

items.title: Moral Imagination in Climate Communication
items.source_name: Etikk i praksis - Nordic Journal of Applied Ethics
items.summary_raw: There is an urgent need for climate action by people in the richer parts of the world, for example, politicians and producers, but also ordinary citizens. Many people are concerned about climate change but remain mainly inactive, many are disengaged and some continue to dismiss climate change. The present study investigates how moral imagination can be used in communication at various societal levels to overcome obstacles to climate action. Communication is not sufficient to solve the problem of inaction. Binding political agreements at a global level are of key importance. However, communication improved by moral imagination is necessary in undertaking such coercive measures by democratic means. A three-step model for attaining this goal is proposed. The first step is to use moral imagination to discern what is morally relevant in the specific communicative situation. The second step is to use moral imagination to put oneself as communicator empathetically in the place of the recipient to understand the recipient’s specific obstacles to climate action. The third step is to use moral imagination to envision the full range of possible responses to the specific obstacles and to determine which response could be the most effective. It is explored how moral imagination in a concrete way can be used in responding to obstacles by applying the imaginative tools of framing, narrative, metaphor and prototype structure. Keywords: climate change; cognitive science; communication…

items.title: An expert-derived content blueprint for ocean, climate, and biodiversity education in Mexico
items.summary_raw: Ocean literacy is central to sustainable ocean stewardship, yet existing frameworks are often too general for context-specific curriculum design. Here, we contribute specifically to the content dimension of ocean literacy by identifying candidate priority topics for basic education in Mexico from the perspective of an expert panel. We conducted a three-round Delphi with 45 national experts. Round 1 yielded 186 statements, which were consolidated into ~100 coded concepts. In Round 2, participants grouped concepts by affinity, and we used network-based clustering and threshold analysis to identify stable groupings. Round 3 refined and validated cluster descriptions. The result is a set of 10 thematic clusters across Marine Science, Biodiversity, and Climate that link ocean processes, biodiversity dynamics, and climate drivers in a Mexico-specific context. This work provides a structured, expert-derived content blueprint to support curriculum design and the adaptation of ocean literacy frameworks to national contexts.

items.title: Smallholder livestock farmers' willingness to adopt biogas technology to meet the energy crisis in rural Bangladesh
items.summary_raw: Despite gains in national electrification, rural Bangladesh continues to experience persistent energy insecurity, while livestock-based livelihoods generate large volumes of organic waste that remain underutilized as locally available renewable energy resources. This study investigates smallholder livestock farmers’ willingness to adopt biogas technology as a decentralized clean-energy solution for reducing rural energy shortages and advancing SDG-oriented outcomes related to clean energy, climate resilience, and sustainable livelihoods. A semi-structured household survey was conducted among 480 livestock-farming households selected from 12 Upazilas in four northern districts of Bangladesh, where livestock dependence, rural poverty, and recurrent electricity interruptions make household-scale biogas particularly relevant. Descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, exploratory factor analysis to construct an awareness index, and a maximum-likelihood probit regression model were employed to identify the determinants of adoption willingness. The model demonstrates strong explanatory performance, with an LR chi-square value of 92.67 and a pseudo R² of 0.5457. The findings reveal that daily electricity shortage (coefficient = 0.3361), awareness of biogas benefits (1.0406), surplus homestead space (0.4826), women’s work-related energy burden (0.0835), electricity-related disruption to children’s education (-0.5707), and educational attainment are statistically associated with…

items.title: Global insights and feasibility evaluation of incineration approach for sustainable waste-to-energy conversion
items.summary_raw: The generation of municipal solid waste (MSW) is expected to rise from 2.01 billion tons in 2016–3.40 billion tons by 2050, mostly due to population expansion, urbanization, and industrialization in low- and middle-income nations. The technical, economic, environmental, and social viability of incineration-based waste-to-energy (WTE) is still heavily reliant on local waste characteristics and institutional conditions. WTE offers simultaneous waste-volume reduction, energy recovery, and partial displacement of fossil-based electricity. Using literature in Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar for the years 2015–2026, this study presents a comprehensive evaluation of incineration-based WTE development; 118 studies are kept after PRISMA-based screening. Successful WTE deployment depends not only on technological maturity but also on source segregation, regulatory enforcement, emission-control infrastructure, financial capacity, and public acceptance. Large-scale incineration is restricted in developing-city contexts due to high-moisture trash, low technical capacity, poor governance, and reliance on unofficial waste-recovery systems. These limitations and the promise of an integrated treatment pathway are further demonstrated by a case study of Gazipur, Bangladesh. Diverting the organic portion (∼2220 t day⁻¹) to anaerobic digestion results in a dry combustible residue of about 627 t day⁻¹ with a corrected net calorific value of 14.79 MJ kg⁻¹ from around…

items.title: Climate-smart dairy technology adoption profiles and multidimensional food security among smallholder dairy households in Northwest Ethiopia
items.summary_raw: This study examines associations between climate-smart dairy technologies and practices (CSDTPs) adoption profiles and multidimensional food security (MDFS) among 734 smallholder dairy households in Northwest Ethiopia using cross-sectional survey design. Latent class analysis (LCA) identified three profiles: selective (19.5%), intermediate (45.9%), and intensive-diversified adoption (34.6%). Augmented-inverse probability weighting (AIPW) estimated the adjusted counterfactual contrast, with inverse-probability weighting regression adjustment (IPWRA) and inverse-probability weighting (IPW) estimators as a robustness checks. Compared with selective adoption, both adoption profiles had lower food insecurity deprivation scores across the four MDFS dimensions. The intensive-diversified adoption generally showed larger estimated differences relative to the selective profile mean: 23.46% for quantity, 10.35% for quantity, 27.22% for acceptability, and 16.62% for stability. Sensitivity analysis broadly supported the findings, although the quality contrast of intermediate profile was not robust to kebele-clustered standard errors. For binary MDFS, compared to selective adoption, intermediate and intensive-diversified adoption profiles were associated with 11.70% and 12.20% lower probabilities of food insecurity, respectively; their difference however, was not statistically significant. These findings highlight the relevance of context-specific combinations of CSDTPs in relation to…

items.title: Visual climate communication in coastal India: A social-media engagement analysis
items.summary_raw: Climate-induced coastal erosion is increasingly affecting India’s 7,500-kilometre coastline, of which nearly 45% experiences erosion and approximately 7% is categorized as highly eroding. These changes are contributing to relocations, livelihood loss and socio-economic vulnerability across coastal regions. Despite increasing climate communication efforts, limited evidence exists on how visual climate communication performs among coastal digital audiences. This study analyses visual climate communication shared by non-governmental organizations (NGOs) and climate communication influencers working in southern Indian coastal regions. The study examines how visual materials are used in digital climate communication and evaluates their performance using social-media engagement metrics, including interaction patterns, reach and audience response trends. Using a mixed analytical approach combining content analysis and digital media engagement analysis, the study identifies visual characteristics associated with higher audience engagement. The findings also highlight gaps between standard scientific climate messaging and locally contextualized communication approaches used in practice. The study provides evidence-based directions towards the development of context-sensitive visual climate communication frameworks for coastal regions. These suggestions are intended to support climate communicators in designing more locally relevant and effective climate action messaging for…

items.title: The p38α MAPK–MK2 axis drives chemotherapy-mediated nuclear actin remodeling to promote ovarian cancer progression
items.summary_raw: Nuclear F-actin facilitates DNA damage repair and contributes to cancer chemoresistance. However, the regulatory mechanisms controlling its dynamic polymerization in response to genotoxic stress remain poorly defined. A major barrier in nuclear actin research is the lack of tools for precise, high-throughput analysis. To systematically investigate nuclear F-actin assembly in DNA damage response, we developed a deep learning pipeline, named nFANet, for high-throughput detection and analysis of nuclear F-actin. Here, using ovarian cancer—a malignancy where chemoresistance is a major clinical obstacle—as a model, we showed that platinum-based chemotherapy robustly induces nuclear F-actin assembly. A subsequent kinome screening, in combination with the application of nFANet, identified the kinase p38α MAPK as a critical upstream regulator of platinum-induced nuclear F-actin assembly. Mechanistically, the p38α MAPK–MK2 signaling pathway promotes formin-mediated nuclear F-actin assembly in response to chemotherapy. Importantly, pharmacological inhibition or genetic knockout of the p38α MAPK–MK2 pathway sensitized ovarian cancer cells to platinum-based therapy. Our work uncovers a key mechanism governing nuclear actin remodeling under genotoxic stress and lays the foundation for identifying a patient subgroup likely to benefit from therapeutic targeting of this pathway.

items.title: Quantifying the hierarchical topological decay of fluid knots
items.summary_raw: In this paper we analyze the hierarchical topological cascade of knotted and linked filaments associated with the natural decay of superfluid vortex tangles. This is done by using an algebraic reformulation of knot polynomial invariants to quantify the topological states of the cascade process. By interpreting the evolutionary paths associated with vortex knot dynamics as geodesic flows in an appropriate knot polynomial space defined by adapted Jones polynomials [X. Liu, R. L. Ricca, J. Phys. A Math. Theor. 45 , 205501 (2012).], we introduce an entanglement index to quantify the probability density of occurrence of each topological state. By this method we analyze all prime knots, links, and composites up to 8 crossings, and show that this measure detects accurately the decreasing topological complexity observed in simulations and laboratory experiments. By a comparative analysis carried out with data based on an alternative measure (complexity degree), we show that this entanglement index proves to be a more robust and reliable quantifier. The theoretical framework proposed here can be applied to other types of physical systems, where networks of filamentary structures are subject to continuous topological change and reorganization.

items.title: Diffusional depth profiling using electrochemiluminescence microscopy
items.summary_raw: Electrochemiluminescence (ECL) microscopy has emerged as a powerful 2D imaging technique with exceptional spatial resolution, enabling visualization of biological entities, nanomaterials, and multiphase systems. Conventional ECL experiments rely on coreactant concentrations in large excess of the luminophore to generate a bright signal in the vicinity of the electrode. While effective for surface interrogation, this confinement limits resolution in the z-dimension, making 3D imaging challenging. Here, we show that introducing an excess of luminophore enables access to 3D information through diffusion of the emission layer away from the electrode. By tuning the concentration ratio of tris(2,2’-bipyridine)ruthenium(II) ([Ru(bpy) 3 ] 2+ ) to tri-n-propylamine (TPrA), we control emission layer diffusivity. Initially, ECL arises from heterogeneous oxidation of both species at the electrode. As TPrA is depleted, the mechanism shifts to chemiluminescence, where [Ru(bpy) 3 ] 3+ oxidizes TPrA, generating a diffusing emissive layer that extends in the z-direction over time. Simulations and scanning electrochemical microscopy capture these diffusion profiles and highlight the role of concentration ratios. We apply this “diffusional depth profiling” to spirulina algae and spheroid cell models, insulating bodies that block light coming from the evolving emissive layer, revealing 3D morphology. This work uncovers the important influence of time and concentration on ECL emission layer…

items.title: The quantum agreement theorem
items.summary_raw: Intersubjective consistency asks when different observers of a physical system, reasoning from a shared theory, will agree on their probability assessments. Classical probability theory provides a benchmark in the form of the Agreement Theorem [R. J. Aumann, Ann. Stat. 4 , 1236–1239 (1976)]. We study the quantum mechanics (QM) analog to the classical Agreement Theorem in a finite-dimensional tripartite setting in which two observers obtain information via local projective measurements. We represent their mutual awareness by common certainty, which is formally an infinite hierarchy of certainty operators concerning the probability of an event of interest. We first prove that if the observers’ measurements commute with one another and with the property of interest, common certainty forces their probability assessments to coincide, thereby recovering a QM analog to the classical Agreement Theorem. We then construct a one-parameter family of qutrit–qubit–qubit models in which one observer’s measurement does not commute with the property and common certainty of disagreement occurs—a distinctively QM phenomenon. The mechanism is coherence between branches distinguished by one but not the other observer’s measurement. When measurement outcomes are stored in a classical register, the resulting dephasing removes this coherence and restores agreement. Finally, we prove that QM does not permit the extreme 0 - 1 configuration in which Alice is certain of a property and is also certain…

items.title: Synergy between Gq and Gi proteins for the antipsychotic-like effects of mGlu2 receptors
items.summary_raw: The capacity of one G protein–coupled receptor (GPCR) to modulate signaling outputs of another is a phenomenon with potential implications for neuron function and therapeutic action. Notably, Gi/o-coupled receptors have been shown to generate calcium signals after costimulation of Gq-coupled receptors, an effect resulting from a crosstalk between signaling cascades. But the relevance for brain function and for therapeutic applications remains largely unclear. Here we show that Gi/o-coupled metabotropic glutamate 2 (mGlu2) receptors can generate calcium signals in neurons. It results from either agonist activation or constitutive activity of a Gq-coupled receptor endogenously coexpressed with mGlu2, independently of dimerization. Specifically, the constitutively active platelet-activating factor receptor (PAFR) plays an essential role in mGlu2-calcium signaling in hippocampal neurons, an effect largely inhibited by PAFR inverse agonists and genetic variants. This mGlu2-PAFR crosstalk is required for the cognitive and behavioral rescue produced by mGlu2 agonists in a mouse model of NMDA receptor hypofunction. These data highlight the complexity of GPCR signaling and provide key insights on therapeutic strategies for psychiatric disorders.

items.title: This surprise cost could derail your heat pump or EV charger installation. Here’s how to avoid it.
items.summary_raw: “Electrify everything” has become a mantra in the fight against climate change. Switching a home’s heating, cooling, and other energy-intensive loads from fossil fuels to electricity could drastically reduce planet-warming emissions. But electrification has often run into a major, and expensive, hurdle: upgrading a home’s electric capacity. A home’s connection to the grid is rated by amperage, or amps, which caps the amount of current it can safely draw at once. The standard for houses built in the last few decades is generally 200 amps. Many older residences, however, have a lower limit because they were constructed when electricity powered little more than the lights, refrigerator, microwave, and perhaps the dryer. Research from Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory found that roughly a third of homes in the United States have panel capacity of 100 amps or less. In the Northeast, that share rises to closer to half. As people install heat pumps, induction stoves, and EV chargers, they can run into a couple of potential issues. Their electric panel may simply run out of slots to install more circuit breakers, in which case the relatively easy fix of adding a subpanel often does the trick. But sometimes homeowners run into a bigger problem, where an electrician says all the new loads will push them past their home’s peak power limits. items.title: Climate progressives won the midterms without saying ‘climate’
items.summary_raw: On October 20, the two candidates running to represent Michigan in the U.S. Senate, Abdul El-Sayed and Mike Rogers, took questions for an hour at the Detroit Economic Club. El-Sayed, the Democrat who had previously run for governor, made a name for himself years ago by connecting public health to the climate crisis. He published a fierce defense of the Green New Deal at the time, touting its economic, health, and planetary benefits . But last month at the Detroit Economic Club, El-Sayed didn’t mention the Green New Deal at all. Instead, the only mentions of such a plan came from his opponent, who used it as an attack on El-Sayed and the Democratic party as a whole. “We need to make sure we don’t have the largest tax increase in the history of the country,” Rogers said, “which is, that’s what the other team is talking about doing.” A vote for El-Sayed would ring in an era of “big government, government control, more rules, more regulation, another Green New Deal,” Rogers continued. It’s become a common refrain since President Donald Trump’s effort to rebrand the climate movement’s push for widescale public investment in renewable energy as a “Green New Scam.” Two weeks later, El-Sayed handily won the race. Even though many of the newly elected Democrats did not talk about the Green New Deal by name, the think tank Climate and Community Institute describes El-Sayed as belonging to a new class of green economic populists who are running for public office (and winning) by…

items.title: Climate change is coming for the cactus. Yes, the cactus.
items.summary_raw: The humble cactus is an icon of resiliency. Stuck in a desert with little rain and abundant searing sun, these plants don’t just survive — they thrive and in turn provide habitat for owls and other birds, and flowers for bats and other pollinators. Yet cacti are in serious trouble , due to habitat loss and the poaching of species for private collections. Now we can add worsening droughts to those woes, according to a new study in the journal Nature. Researchers modeled not just a future of relentlessly rising temperatures, but the attendant dry spells, finding that the majority of nearly 1,000 cactus species will lose habitat as the climate radically changes. More than a quarter of those species could lose at least 80 percent of that habitat by 2100. “The public perception of cacti tends to be of these organisms that are extremely drought-adapted and are just resilient, can handle anything that you can throw at them,” said Michiel Pillet, a conservation ecologist at the University of South Florida and lead author of the paper. “In reality, cacti are absolutely amazing — and they’re my favorite plant group, clearly — but they’re not that different from other plants.” That means cacti need water. In the deserts of the southwestern United States, for example, they rely on seasonal monsoon rains which tend to make July or August the wettest month in a given year . Because this is still a desert, cacti have evolved a range of adaptations to survive , like a waxy skin that helps…

items.title: Pohled české veřejnosti na fungování demokracie se rok po volbách do PS mírně zhoršil
items.summary_raw: Podle posledního výzkumu STEM, realizovaného v září 2026, spokojenost veřejnosti s fungováním demokracie za poslední rok mírně klesla, zůstává ale nad předvolební úrovní z roku 2024. Aktuálně vyjadřuje spokojenost 43 % občanů. „Pokles pravděpodobně souvisí se změnou vlády po loňských volbách. U voličů současné opozice výrazně vzrostla nespokojenost, zatímco u voličů vládních stran ANO a SPD spokojenost posílila jen mírně, což tento rozdíl nevyrovnalo a promítlo se i do mírného poklesu na celospolečenské úrovni. Výrazná nespokojenost opozičních voličů přitom zřejmě neplyne jen z toho, že jejich strana není u moci, ale odráží nejspíše i nesouhlas s kroky vládní koalice, které podle nich nemusí být v souladu s demokratickými principy,“ uvádí analytička STEM Eliška Votavová. Z časové řady je patrné, že převažující nespokojenost s fungováním demokracie je trvalým jevem. „Nespokojenost nemusíme nutně vnímat pouze jako negativní jev – může sloužit také jako impuls k větší aktivitě občanské společnosti a růstu volební účasti,” dodává Eliška Votavová. Kriticky lidé hodnotí i to, zda vedoucí představitelé dodržují demokratické principy (nevěří tomu 54 %) a zda je umí v běžném životě uplatňovat veřejnost sama (59 % říká, že ne). Naopak občanské svobody považuje za dostatečně zajištěné 60 % lidí. Polistopadový vývoj hodnotí smíšeně 55 % a dlouhodobě přetrvává názor, že politické strany demokratickou politiku dostatečně nezaručují.

items.summary_raw: Integrating passive energy strategies in built projects improve the performance of buildings, especially in warmer and more humid urban environments. However, having an intention of integrating climate responsive designs does not guarantee passive energy strategies are systematically integrated within the construction project management process. This research investigated how passive energy strategies are currently being integrated in construction project management processes in Lagos, Nigeria. A convergent mixed methods approach was used. The questionnaire section employed a cross-sectional survey and the interview section comprised semi-structured interviews. Quantitative data was collected from 200 valid respondents in the construction industry. Ten interviews were conducted with experienced professionals. Data analysis involved frequencies, percentages and weighted mean scores of the questionnaire responses. Thematic analysis was undertaken for the interview data. The results show that there is moderate uneven integration of passive energy strategies. There was a higher frequency of high and very high integration at the design stage (70.0%), project planning (65.0%) and project initiation (59.0%). A lower frequency of integration was reported at monitoring stage (56.0%), contractor compliance with passive design requirements (53.0%), project completion (50.0%) and project performance indicators (energy efficiency) (47.0%).
