items.title: Swedish teachers’ perceived professional action competence in sustainability and climate change education
items.summary_raw: This study aims to explore how in-service school teachers in Sweden perceive their professional action competence (PAC) in Sustainability and Climate Change Education (SCCE). Drawing on data from an exploratory survey involving 202 primary and secondary school teachers in Sweden, the study examines three core dimensions of PAC in SCCE: professional knowledge, self-efficacy, and willingness to teach. Descriptive and frequency analyses were employed to identify teachers’ self-perceptions across these dimensions. The study reveals that teachers generally perceive their professional action competence in SCCE as well-prepared, particularly regarding content knowledge and teaching approaches, and they report high levels of intrinsic motivation for teaching SCCE. However, the results also show several areas across these dimensions in which teachers felt less prepared: (1) to facilitate collective action-taking by students, (2) to engage with community partners beyond school in the teaching and learning process, (3) to support students in dealing with difficult emotions, and (4) to assess students’ sustainability-related competences. The study provides valuable insights into the conditions that support or constrain the implementation of SCCE in schools and aims to inform the design of future professional development initiatives and contribute to ongoing efforts to strengthen teachers’ preparedness for transformative SCCE.

items.summary_raw: This article evaluates the Ecobudget for Łódź, Poland, as an innovative instrument for the city’s participatory climate change adaptation, and identifies the benefits and limitations in its design and implementation. The article’s theoretical framework is based on three integrally linked themes: public participation in environmental protection, deliberative democracy (mini-public), and participatory climate change adaptation instruments. The empirical research was conducted as a qualitative case study of the first edition of the Ecobudget. It included participant observations, a focus group interview with representatives of institutions involved in the implementation, and six individual in-depth interviews with project applicants. The results indicate that the Ecobudget effectively mobilised residents around specific green spaces, drawing on their attachment to the place and their concern for its future. At the same time, it fostered cooperation between residents, experts, and the public administration. Its main strengths include its strong local roots, its educational function, and its tripartite cooperation model. The most significant limitation lay in the implementation phase of the selected projects and the communication issues that accompanied it. The case study of the Ecobudget for Łódź may serve as a source of inspiration for cities seeking new participatory tools. items.summary_raw: Purpose The purpose of the current study is to assess the relationship between employees' perceptions of inclusivity policies and employee well-being (i.e. life satisfaction, job satisfaction, turnover intentions and work–life balance). Moreover, we also examine diversity climate as a potential mediator of this relationship. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on the model of inclusive organizations and the signaling theory, we hypothesized that positive perceptions of inclusivity policies would relate to better employee well-being through a more favorable perception of diversity climate. The sample consisted of 361 faculty and staff from a large Southeastern university. A single-level path-analytic mediation model was used to test hypothesized relationships due to the negligible between-college variance. Findings The results revealed that positive perceptions of inclusivity policies were associated with a more positive diversity climate which, in turn, enhanced certain well-being outcomes – life satisfaction, job satisfaction, turnover intentions and work–life balance. Further, diversity climate mediated the relationship between employees' perceptions of inclusivity policies and employee well-being. Our results highlight the importance of not only implementing inclusive policies but, also ensuring that employees perceive them as fair and effective. items.summary_raw: This study aimed to determine the effects of school climate on the work performance of public secondary school teachers in Pililla District, Division of Rizal, during School Year 2024–2025. Specifically, it examined the teachers’ perceptions of school climate in relation to their teaching methodologies, ability to handle diverse students, task accomplishment, and interpersonal relationships. It also determined whether significant differences existed in their perceptions when grouped according to selected demographic and professional profiles and whether these perceptions were significantly related to their work performance based on their Individual Performance Commitment and Review (IPCR) ratings. The study employed a descriptive survey research design involving the total population of 263 public secondary school teachers from five secondary schools in the district. Data were gathered using a researcher-made questionnaire-checklist and documentary analysis of the respondents’ latest IPCR ratings. The findings revealed that school climate often affected teachers’ work performance across the four dimensions. No significant differences were found when respondents were grouped according to age, sex, civil status, position title, length of service, and educational attainment. However, significant differences were observed in task accomplishment and interpersonal relationships when grouped according to in-service trainings attended. items.title: Transitioning to low-carbon agriculture: Institutional misalignment and constraints in South Africa’s extension systems
items.summary_raw: Despite climate-mitigation commitments in the global South, an implementation gap constrains sustainable agricultural development in South Africa. This study examines government extension practitioners' perceptions of climate-aligned practices to identify the institutional factors driving this divide. A qualitative content analysis of 1775 thematic segments from focus groups with 52 extension officers across eight provinces in 2025 reveals deep institutional misalignment. Only 10.7% of coded segments explicitly framed agriculture as a mitigation strategy, while 35.8% prioritize economic optimization and livelihood conservation. Provincial focus on climate mitigation ranges from 20.3% in Mpumalanga to 4.7% in Gauteng. Crucially, land tenure insecurity emerges as a foundational structural constraint that contributes to this misalignment by discouraging long-term climate investment. While national mandates conceptualize mitigation through global carbon accounting, local extension systems prioritize immediate economic survival. Therefore, achieving national targets requires reforming communal land governance alongside extension mandates, rather than merely introducing technical solutions. The study demonstrates that land governance reform is a prerequisite, rather than a complementary measure, for effective climate policy implementation. It advances frameworks that leverage smart technologies for carbon measurement, youth-led data management, and carbon credits, reframing…

items.title: Responding to Overshoot: From “Inconvenient Truth” to “Inconvenient Ignorance”
items.summary_raw: Between co-creating the Ecological Footprint in the early 1990s and cofounding Global Footprint Network, I have spent over three decades arguing that humanity’s central predicament is ecological overshoot: a resource metabolism larger than what the biosphere can renew. I have tried to make it measurable. I have argued that biocapacity is the economy’s binding physical constraint, and therefore the most meaningful measure of ecological overshoot. More recently, I have come to recognize that meaningful responses to overshoot are unlikely unless responding is perceived to be advantageous rather than merely noble. If people perceive overshoot merely as a predicament or a moral burden, rather than an inescapable context for which it is essential to prepare, overshoot is more likely to end by disaster than by design. This framing also helps to show that preparing well turns out to be far more aligned with self-interest than commonly assumed: The most effective responses to overshoot are also the most effective ways to reduce it. This perspective helps to redirect the dominant but misguided “free-rider” framing of climate action, which in my view is strategically self-defeating. For cities, companies, countries, and households alike, the incentives to prepare for an inevitable resource-constrained future are far better aligned than the prevailing narrative admits, a claim I consider crucial, and one that is fiercely resisted.

items.title: Climate change awareness and environmental attitudes among undergraduate students in Hargeisa, Somaliland
items.summary_raw: Climate change awareness is often assumed to translate directly into positive environmental attitudes; however, this relationship remains under-theorized in sub-Saharan African higher education contexts. This study examined climate change awareness and environmental attitudes among 178 final-year (“senior”) undergraduate students at the University of Hargeisa, Somaliland, using a stratified random sample drawn from six academic colleges. Guided by the Theory of Planned Behavior and Value-Belief-Norm theory, a structured questionnaire assessed awareness and attitudes via composite indices, analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple linear regression. Students reported moderate climate change awareness and generally positive environmental attitudes, with a statistically significant positive correlation between the two constructs ( r = .244, p = .001). Disaggregating the composite awareness index into its constituent components showed that self-rated awareness was positively associated with environmental attitudes, whereas course completion, organizational membership, information-seeking, and family discussion were not independently associated at the conventional significance level. Lack of information and limited curriculum integration were the most commonly reported barriers to climate awareness. These findings suggest that students’ perceived level of climate awareness may be more closely related to environmental attitudes than specific forms of…

items.title: Seeing the Heat: How a Communication Tool Transformed Experiences into Evidence for New York City’s Climate Response
items.summary_raw: As climate change intensifies heat, New York City faces mounting health risks. While quantitative data like temperature trends and mortality rates are essential, they cannot capture the lived experience of the climate crisis. Your Heat Story, a partnership between South Bronx Unite, Columbia University, and the NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene, addresses this gap by collecting and visualizing firsthand narratives from New Yorkers alongside public health data. By integrating stories with environmental health data, this project demonstrates how qualitative and quantitative approaches together strengthen climate communication. These narratives illuminate the cumulative toll of heat on physical, emotional, and mental health and community life, particularly in under-resourced neighborhoods. This initiative models a new form of government communication that uses public platforms for storytelling and relationship-building. In doing so, it advances awareness, informs policy, and offers a replicable framework for integrating narrative into climate-health resilience work.

items.title: Climate Change and Multisystem Disruption of Diabetes Care: A Climate-Health System
items.source_name: Journal of Health Science and Medical Research
items.summary_raw: Climate change increases the need for health systems to prepare for extreme weather events that threaten continuity of chronic disease care. This narrative review examines the clinical and health system implications of flooding for diabetes care in Southeast Asia, using the November 2025 Hat Yai floods in southern Thailand as a case study. We synthesized evidence from disaster medicine literature, regional epidemiological studies, and current diabetes guidance. Floods interrupt safe water, food, electricity, transport, and health services, while dehydration, infection, and preexisting cardiovascular and kidney disease increase susceptibility to acute multisystem decompensation. Modern cardiometabolic therapies add context-dependent hazards, including euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis with sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors and metformin-associated lactic acidosis during acute kidney injury, and loss of insulin refrigeration and medicine supplies threatens glycemic stability. We propose a climate-health system framework that links these hazards, with practical sick-day rules, insulin-storage measures, and roles for patients, health-care teams, and health systems across the disaster cycle. Integrating these measures into routine diabetes care and national health adaptation strategies may reduce preventable complications, although flood-specific intervention evidence remains limited.

items.title: Ultra-high voltage transmission and corporate ESG performance: evidence from Chinese A-share listed firms
items.summary_raw: Whether large-scale clean-energy infrastructure can alleviate the trade-off between economic growth and environmental degradation is central to environmental regulation under China's dual-carbon goals. This study examines the relationship between ultra-high voltage (UHV) transmission access and corporate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance using firm-year observations of Chinese A-share listed companies with valid Sino-Securities ESG ratings from 2009 to 2022. We estimate a two-way fixed-effects difference-in-differences model with firm and year fixed effects, complemented by the Callaway–Sant’Anna staggered DID estimator. Firms gaining UHV access exhibit higher ESG scores, with the largest point estimate observed for the environmental dimension and smaller positive estimates for the social and governance dimensions. The positive UHV-ESG association persists after accounting for local carbon-market exposure and is also observed under alternative ESG specifications and propensity-score-matched DID estimation. Mechanism estimates are consistent with production resilience, including liquidity buffers, and reduced transition risk as two potential channels. Subgroup estimates are larger for smaller firms and firms in other classified industries, with formal coefficient-difference tests indicating cross-group variation, while positive relationships are observed in both ownership groups. These findings suggest that clean-energy infrastructure may be relevant to…

items.title: Associations between types of screen use and bedtimes among a large sample of adolescents: age and typical bedtime variations from the COMPASS study
items.summary_raw: Abstract Background Recreational screen time is linked to poorer sleep among adolescents. However, most evidence focuses on total recreational screen time rather than on time spent on different screen-based activities. Also, few studies have specifically examined bedtime, an actionable determinant of adolescent sleep hygiene. To date, it is not clear how age and typical bedtime influence this relationship. The objective of this study was to examine the associations between time spent on different screen-based activities and adolescents’ bedtimes. We also aimed to examine how these associations vary based on age and typical bedtime. Methods Using a cross-sectional design, we analyzed data collected from 67,710 adolescents aged 11 to 19 (age: 14.4 (± 1.5) ; females: 51.2%) attending 154 Quebec schools in 2025 as part of the COMPASS study. Quantile regressions were conducted to assess associations between the time adolescents spent on different screen-based activities (i.e., browsing/scrolling social media, playing video games, sending messages, surfing the Internet, watching/streaming television shows or movies) and their bedtimes. The analyses were stratified by age and typical bedtime and adjusted for the adolescents’ sex and family-level material affluence. A difference-in-difference analysis was also conducted. items.title: Creating “PEACH Clips: Empowering Sustainable Health Care Through Knowledge and Action”: A Case for the Use of Digital Story Telling in Climate Action Communication Strategies
items.summary_raw: Health care systems significantly contribute to environmental degradation, yet clinicians often lack clear and actionable guidance on how to implement sustainable practices. PEACH Health Ontario (Partnerships for Environmental Action by Communities within Healthcare systems) develops tailored educational tools, including specialty-specific guidebooks, to support health care climate action. In 2023, PEACH adopted Digital Storytelling (DST) as a novel knowledge translation strategy to communicate its mission, highlight its guidebook development process, and showcase how to navigate PEACH guidebooks. DST, an art-based method using multimedia narratives, enables complex concepts to be conveyed through personal, engaging, and memorable formats. The research team followed the general steps of DST content development and worked with a consultant to create three short videos. Using the Knowledge-to-Action framework, facilitators captured and thematically analyzed detailed field notes from participant reflections on PEACH's identity, legacy, and guidebook utility. A consultant specializing in health care-climate communication then refined these ideas, identified priority content, guided script and media development, and created a communication dissemination plan to maximize audience engagement. Iterative review cycles ensured videos accurately represented participant perspectives and aligned with PEACH's goals. Our findings suggest that DST, when combined with strategic…

items.title: Fintech adoption and its impact on climate smart agriculture technology adoption and agricultural productivity in rice and maize farming
items.summary_raw: Farmers have an increasing need for financial resources, which has led to the development and adoption of Fintech. This research aims to identify the determinants of Fintech adoption and productivity of rice and maize cultivation, and to examine how Fintech affects farmers’ intensity of climate-smart agricultural (CSA) technologies in transforming the agro-economy. Fintech and CSA technologies may contribute to climate adaptation and sustainable agricultural development, contributing to Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 2 and 13 by improving agricultural productivity and climate resilience. To evaluate the effect of Fintech on rice and maize production, the study was conducted with 240 rural households through a cross-sectional survey in Kaliganj and Kaliakair Upazilas of Gazipur District, Bangladesh. A fractional regression model, an instrumental variable fractional regression model, and a Cobb–Douglas production function were employed. bKash, Rocket, and Nagad were among the preferred Fintech technologies. Education, remittances, number of mobile phones, Fintech adoption, and family size significantly influenced CSA adoption intensity, although remittance was significant only for rice and family size was not significant in the instrumental variable fractional regression model. Rice and maize yields were significantly influenced by family size, number of mobile phones, remittance receipt, and Fintech adoption, while fertilizer and hybrid variety use significantly…

items.title: Associations between mitigation-oriented and adaptive behaviors and climate change anxiety: a cross-sectional study among college undergraduates
items.summary_raw: Abstract Background: Mental and physical health effects stemming from climate change are increasingly prevalent while adaptation to protect health has not kept pace. Climate change anxiety (CCA) is an area of research that may inform behavioral responses to climate hazards. We examined whether CCA was associated with pro-environmental behaviors or the adoption of health-protective adaptive measures, such as accessing air cleaners for wildfires or cooling systems (e.g. heat pump, air conditioning) for extreme heat. Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional study with an online survey of 451 college students for CCA using a validated scale and asked students about their mitigating pro-environmental behavior and if they had taken any adaptive measures. We assessed four subscales representing distinct dimensions of climate-related responses. Quasi-Poisson and binomial logistic regression models were used to analyze behavioral outcomes related to mitigation (pro-environmental behaviors) and adaptation measures (e.g., access to air cleaners; cooling). Results: All four subscales were significantly associated with the number of pro-environmental behaviors (p-values 2x10-16 to 0.007) and all subscales except functional impairment were significantly associated with the binary outcome of the adoption of adaptive health behaviors (p-values 0.008 to 0.020). Conclusions: These findings suggest that certain dimensions of climate-related psychological responses are associated with both…

items.title: Climate Change Education through AI-Powered Simulations among Rural Learners: A Framework for Developing Climate Literacy
items.summary_raw: Climate change education helps students understand environmental changes and develop responsible attitudes towards the environment. The National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 emphasises experiential, inquiry-based, and technology-supported learning, providing an important educational context for innovative approaches to climate change education. However, many climate processes are difficult to observe directly and explain through classroom teaching alone. Rural learners may benefit from learning experiences that connect scientific concepts with their local environment. This conceptual study proposes a framework for developing climate literacy among rural learners through artificial intelligence-powered simulations. It draws on published literature on climate change education, simulation-based learning, and educational technology. The review informs a framework linking local environmental experiences, interactive simulations, teacher guidance, reflective learning, and evidence-based decision-making. The proposed framework identifies these elements as potential contributors to climate literacy, including scientific understanding, systems thinking, critical evaluation, and environmental responsibility. The paper also highlights the importance of teacher preparedness, access to digital resources, language accessibility, scientific accuracy, and responsible use of artificial intelligence. The framework may help teachers in designing relevant climate learning experiences and provide…

items.title: Echoes of Dissent: Intermedia Frame-Setting Between Social Media and Legacy Media in the Debate Over Climate Protesters in Germany
items.summary_raw: This study examines how polarized attributes and frames of climate protesters diffuse across social and legacy media. It shows that polarization is driven less by ideologically segregated media environments than by a discursive backlash that amplifies antagonistic frames across ideological divides. Climate protest provides a particularly instructive case, as protest tactics frequently spark debates over legitimacy and legality that can become problematic when shaped by ideologically motivated framing. Focusing on the climate protest group the Last Generation in Germany, this study analyzes how polarized attributes and frames diffused between Twitter/X and legacy media in 2022 and 2023. Using a mixed-methods approach, we identify six polarized frames across approximately 1.5 million tweets and 2500 news articles. Combining (semi-)automated content analysis with time-series analysis, we trace the dynamics of attribute and frame diffusion. Our findings show that polarization emerged less from isolated ideological camps than from contentious dynamics across media spheres. Following a traffic accident involving protesters, conservative-right-wing actors from social and legacy media introduced and intensified antagonistic frames, which diffused into liberal-left-wing media largely through critical engagement. Although intended to challenge these frames, such coverage amplified them, enabling right-wing actors to shape the interpretive boundaries of the debate.

items.title: Production Constraints and Genetic Diversity of Coffea arabica (L.) in Ethiopia: A Review
items.summary_raw: Ethiopia is the center of origin and genetic diversity of Coffea arabica and plays a central role in global coffee production. Coffee contributes significantly to national export earnings, rural livelihoods and ecosystem services. However, coffee productivity in the country remains constrained by a combination of biotic, abiotic and socioeconomic factors. This review examines the major production constraints, including pests and diseases, climate variability, soil fertility decline and limited access to improved management practices. In parallel, it explores the rich genetic diversity of Ethiopian Arabica coffee, which represents a valuable resource for breeding, adaptation and long-term sustainability. The review synthesizes findings from previous studies to assess the current status of genetic variation across different coffee-growing regions and production systems, including forest, semi-forest, garden and plantation systems. However, deforestation, land-use changes and genetic erosion threaten long-term sustainability. Emphasis is placed on the importance of conserving both in situ and ex situ genetic resources to support climate resilience and productivity improvement. Overall, this paper highlights the need for integrated strategies that address production constraints while promoting the conservation and utilization of genetic diversity. Strengthening research, extension services and policy support is essential to ensure the sustainability and global competitiveness of…

items.title: Predictors of climate anxiety and climate policy support in a British public
items.summary_raw: The current study investigates the existence of climate anxiety amongst a British public. Given the threat presented to human wellbeing from a changing climate, this study adds to a growing research body that seeks to understand and improve efforts to help deal with the mental health challenge climate change is increasingly presenting to the public. Using an online sample, 898 participants were asked to complete various survey measures including climate anxiety, storm fear, existential thinking, compassion, risk perceptions, policy support and various demographics. Participants were also asked to provide top-of-mind image associations with climate change. Results revealed that although prevalence of climate anxiety is low, the strongest predictors of this construct included age, storm fear, risk perception and existential thinking with younger participants, those who are fearful of severe weather, those who perceive climate change as a serious threat and those who engage in existential thinking behaviours reporting higher levels of climate anxiety. Additionally, ‘alarm’ based image associations were the most frequent top-of-mind thoughts participants associated with climate change with phrases including ‘destruction of our planet’, ‘emergency’ and ‘existential climate disaster’ being provided. Climate anxiety was also a strong predictor in a regression analysis of climate policy support alongside risk perception, political ideology and compassion. The results demonstrate the…

items.title: Assessing learners’ attitudes toward meme-based learning through the technology acceptance model
items.summary_raw: Introduction In an era when learners are immersed in a fast-evolving digital culture, education should adopt practices that resonate with learners' characteristics. There is a growing need to examine how emerging tools can support the current generation's learning styles. In this context, internet memes offer a potentially engaging resource for language learning. This study investigates learners' acceptance of meme-based learning in English language education by applying an extended Technology Acceptance Model (TAM). Methods A quantitative research design was employed, with data collected from 238 undergraduate ESL learners through a structured questionnaire. The instrument assessed five constructs: perceived ease of use, perceived usefulness, attitude towards use, behavioural intention, and positive learning experience. Reliability and regression analyses were performed using SPSS version 25 to examine the proposed relationships among these constructs. Results The findings indicate that all hypothesised relationships are statistically significant. Perceived ease of use and perceived usefulness emerge as significant predictors of learners' attitudes towards meme-based learning. Attitude is significantly associated with behavioural intention, which, in turn, significantly predicts positive learning experience. The findings further indicate that learners perceive memes as meaningful learning resources that facilitate engagement and interaction while requiring relatively less…

Participation, procedural fairness and policy acceptability: A quasi-experimental field study of workplace travel planning
items.source_name: Transportation Research Part A Policy and Practice
items.summary_raw: Parking restrictions are among the most effective tools available to organisations and local authorities seeking to manage transport demand and reduce commuting emissions. Yet their implementation often fails when commuters question their legitimacy, highlighting the need to better understand the conditions under which such measures gain acceptability during the development stage. This study examines whether involving commuters in the development of restrictive travel measures increases their acceptability, applying policy acceptance and deliberative democracy literatures to an organisational transport context for the first time. Using a quasi-experimental field design embedded in a travel plan development process at a UK university (N = 486, data collected between 15/09/2025 and 05/12/2025), we compare standard consultation via a travel survey with enhanced involvement via deliberative workshops. Mediation analysis shows that workshop participation increased perceived procedural fairness, which in turn increased policy acceptability, replicating and extending Liu et al.’s (2020) participation–fairness–acceptability pathway to an organisational setting. A significant negative direct effect indicates that deliberation simultaneously raised critical scrutiny, producing inconsistent mediation. Trust in the organisation emerged as a precondition of participation: deliberative engagement increased acceptability among those who already trusted the institution. For local…

items.title: Nationalist parties and the transnational cleavage
items.summary_raw: European party politics has been realigning around a transnational dimension of competition that pits cosmopolitan parties — favouring immigration, European integration, and climate policy — against radical right parties that oppose these. Radical right parties are sometimes equated with nationalist parties. However, nationalism is highly diverse in Europe’s multinational democracies. Multinational democracies are characterised by a salient centre-periphery conflict, in which majority nationalist parties confront minority nationalists representing peripheral nations. While majority nationalists can be expected to converge on the particularist pole of the transnational cleavage, minority nationalists have strategic reasons to adopt more cosmopolitan stances: they need international allies and seek to differentiate themselves from majority nationalists, their main domestic opponents. The analysis draws on the 2023 edition of an expert survey designed to measure nationalist ideology separately from cultural values, and to differentiate majority from minority nationalism. Analysing 89 nationalist parties in 21 countries confirms that while majority nationalists position themselves on the particularist pole of the transnational cleavage, minority nationalists are more pro-European and more in favour of climate policy — but not more in favour of immigration — than majority nationalists. Interestingly, cosmopolitanism appears also among majority nationalists in smaller peripheral…

items.title: Technology pathway choices and lifecycle costs of chinese power battery firms under carbon constraints: An empirical analysis of managerial decision-making
items.summary_raw: China's power battery industry has grown into the world's largest by volume, yet firms now face mounting pressure from carbon pricing mechanisms and evolving emissions trading scheme (ETS) regulations. Strategic technology pathway choices among lithium iron phosphate (LFP), nickel manganese cobalt (NMC), and emerging solid-state chemistries carry material consequences for long-run manufacturing cost structures. This study investigates how carbon constraint intensity and carbon price volatility shape firm-level technology pathway decisions in listed Chinese battery manufacturers, and how managerial characteristics moderate these effects. Using an unbalanced panel of 68 listed Chinese battery firms over 2013–2022 (N = 680 firm-year observations) drawn from CSMAR, Wind, CNIPA, MIIT, and MEEB databases, we construct a Technology Pathway Index (TPI) and a Solid-State Investment Index (SSII). Carbon Constraint Intensity (CCI) combines ETS provincial coverage with prevailing carbon prices. We estimate dynamic panel models with firm and year fixed effects, supplementing OLS estimates with two-stage least squares (2SLS) using provincial energy-sector ETS coverage as an instrument. A one standard deviation increase in CCI raises TPI by 4.19 points under OLS and 5.87 points under 2SLS, confirming a robust positive effect. Carbon price volatility independently elevates solid-state investment. TMT educational diversity amplifies the CCI-TPI relationship (interaction coefficient +2.03, p…

items.title: Co-Creating Disaster Alert Messages with Communities for Climate Adaptation and Public Health
items.summary_raw: This study examines how to improve the effectiveness of climate-related disaster alert messages. Using a living lab methodology-based co-creation approach, it conducts a case study in Seoul, South Korea, exploring how citizens and experts can collaboratively enhance disaster alert messages. Findings showed that citizens perceive current disaster alert messages as lacking relevance, causing desensitization to alerts, and providing insufficient information. Moreover, citizens indicated that credibility, information specificity, and noticeability need to be improved to enhance message effectiveness.

items.title: The primary energy fallacy in energy transitions
items.summary_raw: Abstract The global energy system remains dominated by fossil fuels, often cited as evidence that replacing them with renewables is unrealistic. Here we show that this view rests on a systematic misinterpretation of energy system size - the primary energy fallacy - that arises when energy systems are compared using primary energy inputs rather than delivered energy services. Using global energy flow analysis grounded in the Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory World Energy Flow framework and IEA energy balances, we compare today’s fossil-fuel-based system with a stylised highly electrified scenario delivering the same level of useful energy services. We find that system-wide losses (rejected energy) fall by 61%, while the contribution of ambient environmental heat captured by heat pumps rises approximately twentyfold; under conventional energy-balance conventions this corresponds to a fall in primary energy inputs of nearly half. Our results show that primary energy metrics increasingly misrepresent system scale as electrification advances, with important implications for energy system analysis and policy. We recommend that energy-system analysis and policy lead with system-loss and useful-energy indicators while continuing to report primary energy as a translation for readers anchored in conventional accounting.

items.title: THE ROLE OF THE GREEN ECONOMY IN THE GLOBAL ECONOMY
items.summary_raw: This article analyzes the role of the green economy in the global economy and its impact on energy security, investment, employment, international trade, and climate policy. Drawing on reports from the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), the International Energy Agency (IEA), international renewable energy statistics, and official information from Uzbekistan, the article examines recent trends in the transition toward a green economy. In addition to the economic opportunities offered by the green transition, the article considers challenges related to financing, grid infrastructure, raw material supply, and social equity.

items.title: DEVELOPING A CLIMATE-RESILIENT INDUSTRIAL LEADERSHIP MODEL FOR RENEWABLE ENERGY ADOPTION
items.summary_raw: The increasing effects of climate change and the need for sustainable industrial operations have highlighted the importance of effective leadership and renewable energy adoption. Industrial organizations face financial, technical, organizational, and workforce-related challenges in implementing renewable energy technologies and climate-resilient practices. This study aimed to assess industrial leadership practices, employee engagement, and organizational readiness for renewable energy adoption; identify implementation challenges; and develop a climate-resilient industrial leadership model for sustainable industrial operations. The study employed a descriptive-developmental research design involving 50 respondents from selected industrial establishments in Pinamungajan, Toledo City, and Balamban, Cebu, Philippines. The respondents consisted of industrial managers, supervisors, technical personnel, and industrial employees. A researcher-developed questionnaire was used to gather data on leadership practices, employee engagement, organizational readiness, renewable energy adoption, and climate-resilient industrial practices. Frequency, percentage, weighted mean, and standard deviation were identified as the statistical tools for analyzing the collected data. The findings were intended to serve as the basis for developing the proposed leadership model. The illustrative assessment results indicated an overall mean of 3.97, interpreted as highly adopted. Leadership support for…

items.title: Failing great expectations: Systemic assessment of the technological and economic viability of commercial fusion undertakings
items.summary_raw: Start-ups and governments have great expectations about the future of energy from fusion, like imminent roll-out at scale, abundance, low cost and negligible environmental impact. Most start-ups claim to be in the final stages of building a fully functional fusion power plant. The aim of this study is to assess these narratives and the communicated expectations around fusion energy. These clear narratives are compared with the state of knowledge, the low technical maturity of essential processes, and the pending integration of interacting and parallel processes into an extremely complex fusion energy system. Narratives of a benign or sustainable technology are related to immense resource and energy needs. Promises of abundance at low cost are placed in perspective of inherent complexity and resource demand. This study is unable to support the great expectations set forth by these start-ups and governments. Meeting the technical needs of a reliable and cost-effective power plant with fusion seems exceptionally unlikely, as research still does not provide basic answers for essential engineering. A fusion energy system will not be clean, carbon-neutral or benign. Cost of fusion power will in view of the immense resource demand substantially exceed the cost of renewable or fission power. Metal availability constrains any energy system and would severely limit fusion power capacity, well below abundance. As these factors impede the economic viability of fusion power, this study…

FEMA’s disaster buyout program is working — but there’s a catch
items.summary_raw: For nearly four decades, the federal government has funded a program that buys out homeowners who live in disaster-prone areas as a way of encouraging them to relocate to safer ground. The Federal Emergency Management Agency has spent over $6 billion on more than 53,000 properties nationwide through its Hazard Mitigation Grant Program. But the question has long been: To what extent does this approach work? A study published today in Science Advances is the latest to offer an answer. Author Rachel Young, an environmental economist at the University of Minnesota, found that the buyout program has largely succeeded in its objective of relocating people and has mostly paid for itself by avoiding future damages. But it isn’t helping everyone equally. “The program is extremely effective at helping people not only move but also move to lower-risk places,” said Young, whose paper makes clear that the “benefits are not evenly distributed.” FEMA started doing buyouts in 1988 with the aim of encouraging people to move out of harm’s way. The idea was to avoid repeatedly paying federal disaster aid or insurance claims at the same location. ProPublica reported , for example, that in one extreme case, a single home in northeast Houston received 18 federal flood insurance payments totalling $1.8 million — roughly 15 times its market value. Residents apply through their local or state government, which requests federal funding that typically covers 75 percent of the property’s cost. If…

items.title: Intermittent Cauchy walks enable optimal 3D search across target shapes and sizes
items.summary_raw: Efficiently locating rare targets requires balancing the exploration of novel space with the exploitation of local vicinities. While this tradeoff is well documented in simplified environments, its behavior in realistic three-dimensional environments remains unclear. Here, we analyze intermittent Lévy walks in three dimensions and show that search efficiency becomes strongly dependent on target geometry, with volume, surface area, and elongation governing performance across the Lévy spectrum. Against this geometric complexity, the Cauchy walk ( μ = 2 ) emerges as a robust, near-optimal solution across a wide range of target geometries. Specifically, we prove that for convex targets of surface area Δ in a domain of volume n , the optimal expected detection time scales as n / Δ , and that the Cauchy walk achieves this scaling up to polylogarithmic factors, while other Lévy strategies are suboptimal in different geometric regimes. Our findings provide a theoretical framework for biological movement patterns, including marine predator foraging and immune surveillance, and inform the design of efficient search algorithms for engineered systems such as autonomous nanoscale explorers.

items.title: Multi-omics characterization of white matter free water reveals genetic and vascular determinants of neurological disorders
items.summary_raw: White matter free water (FW-WM), quantified using diffusion MRI, reflects extracellular water content and microstructural alterations within water matter, but its genetic architecture and clinical relevance remain largely uncharted. We conducted a multi-omics study integrating 42,039 individuals from the UK Biobank and Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative cohorts to characterize tract-specific FW-WM across genetic, phenotypic, and proteomic dimensions. Genome-wide association analyses identified 27 independent loci and prioritized 88 genes, which were enriched in the genomic functional elements of vascular endothelial cells, pericytes, and astrocytes. Notably, 20 loci (74%) were novel compared to conventional white matter metrics. Both genetic predisposition to higher FW-WM and imaging-derived FW-WM were associated with a spectrum of neurological disorders. Specifically, imaging-derived FW-WM showed strong associations with stroke (OR = 3.14) and dementia (OR = 4.15), while higher baseline FW-WM predicted progression from MCI to AD (HR = 2.58). Bidirectional Mendelian randomization analyses further supported genetically predicted associations between hypertension and FW-WM, which were together associated with increased risks of stroke and cognitive impairment. Integrative proteomic analyses further nominated PEAR1 and ANGL3 as candidate proteins potentially linking hypertension-related vascular processes to FW-WM variation. Together, these findings provide a…

items.title: Principles of use of tensile J-curve materials in antagonistic arrangements
items.summary_raw: Natural ligaments are soft connective tissues that provide high stretchability for dexterous flexibility but switch to high stiffness to protect the musculoskeletal system from excessive deformation. These two functions cannot be independently tuned in conventional engineering materials with linear or hyperelasticity. Biological materials achieve this tailored behavior through a highly nonlinear tensile response characterized by a J-shaped curve, featuring an extended “toe region” of low force up to intermediate strains followed by an inflection, called the “heel region” which marks the onset of nonlinear stiffening. Here, we aim to study the characteristics of J-curves to establish principles for their use in robotic mechanisms. We define and measure the J-curve features responsible for protectiveness and mobility, describe the effective stiffness and the level of nonlinearity as a function of pre-stretch, and elucidate how the J-curve decouples flexibility from damage protection. Experimental measurements reveal the performance advantages of twisted and coiled elastomeric J-curve materials in engineered antagonistic arrangements and highlight their unique design space compared with linear elastic systems. Furthermore, we present a conceptual analysis of exploiting J-curve materials in energy-efficient running as an outlook toward their use in bioinspired robots.

items.title: How Antoni Gaudí used math to make his basilica soar
Phase transition in a dryland shrub–grass ecosystem: Emergence through local trade-offs
items.summary_raw: Ecosystems are complex adaptive systems in which local interactions among individuals shape macroscopic phenomena such as pattern formation, multistability, and critical transitions. However, how such bottom-up interactions govern emergent behaviors and system-level complexity remains a central challenge in ecology. Phase transition theory, a classic paradigm in physics, links local interaction rules to emergent changes in macroscopic system states, offering a formal language for understanding cross-scale dynamics. Here we unite this theory with empirical evidence from dryland shrub–grass ecosystems and show that these systems exhibit three hallmarks of phase transitions. First, abrupt shifts separate different phases of deserts, shrublands, and grasslands. Second, shrublands and grasslands self-organize into Turing-like phase patterns, contrasting with homogeneous deserts. Third, special phenomena emerge near-transition threshold, including patch enlargement and abrupt decline at desert–vegetation interface, and fairy circles within the shrub–grass transition zone. Using a cellular automaton model built on a fundamental trade-off between extensive and intensive resource foraging strategies (EI trade-off), we show how kernels encoding local trade-offs integrate these seemingly disparate phenomena within a unified phase transition framework. Moreover, this EI trade-off was empirically validated through analyses of plant functional traits and spatial patterns of plant patches…

items.title: Phylogenetic profiling reveals evolutionary coupling between methyltransferases and the cytoskeleton
items.summary_raw: Methylation is a fundamental post-translational modification best understood as regulating chromatin structure and gene expression, yet there is emerging evidence that methylation also shapes cytoskeletal organization, regulating key processes such as mitosis and cell migration. Proteomic studies have revealed cytoskeletal protein methylation is widespread, however little is known about the enzymes responsible for these modifications, or their evolutionary relationship to other, better known substrates for methylation, such as chromatin. To address this question, we applied phylogenetic profiling across the complete repertoire of human methyltransferases to identify conserved functional relationships extending beyond chromatin. Unbiased clustering revealed extensive coevolution between methyltransferases and many components of the cytoskeleton, uncovering a previously unrecognized evolutionary network linking canonical chromatin regulatory enzymes to cellular structural systems. Evolutionary Trace analysis of the H3K36 methyltransferase family recovered known catalytic and regulatory domains while identifying additional evolutionarily constrained residues, suggesting previously unappreciated functional interfaces. Comparative analyses further distinguished deeply conserved methyltransferase–cytoskeletal relationships from those that emerged later during eukaryotic evolution, indicating that cytoskeletal methylation comprises both ancient and lineage-expanded regulatory…

items.title: Correction for Ge et al., Empirical validation of race-neutral normative brain morphometry models across ethnoracially diverse populations
Dormancy stabilizes structured food webs
items.summary_raw: Theory predicts that strong species interactions drive instability in large ecosystems, but strong interactions are common in nature while strong instability appears rare. This discrepancy motivates enduring interest in ecological mechanisms that limit or counteract instability. Dormancy—reversible metabolic suppression—may be one. Dormancy is a ubiquitous life history trait found in organisms ranging from bacteria to trees. Dormant individuals form “seed banks” that are temporarily disengaged from demographic processes and species interactions, creating a memory of past ecological dynamics. Seed banks can stabilize predator–prey interactions, but whether, when, and how they affect the stability of larger ecological networks is uncertain. We show that dormancy stabilizes oscillatory dynamics in a minimal mathematical model and illustrate how dormancy converts high oscillation frequency into strong restoring force. We find that dormancy can have qualitative stabilizing effects in structured food webs that undergo Hopf bifurcations and exhibit oscillatory instability, but rarely in unstructured networks or networks with symmetric (competitive or mutualistic) interactions. This classification remains accurate when only some species go dormant and drive stabilization. Our results clarify when dormancy can promote stability, indicating that it may be an important but overlooked stabilizing factor in food webs.

items.title: RE1 silencing transcription factor is reduced in endometriosis, and uterine deletion in mice alters progesterone responsiveness
items.summary_raw: Endometriosis is a steroid-dependent gynecologic disease characterized by progesterone (P4) resistance, subfertility/infertility, and pelvic pain; however, the molecular mechanisms underlying impaired P4 responsiveness in endometriosis tissue are not fully understood. RE1 silencing transcription factor (REST), a transcriptional regulator implicated in steroid hormone signaling, has emerged as a potential mediator of P4 responsiveness. Here, we investigated the role of REST in endometriosis using human tissues and a uterine-specific Rest conditional knockout mouse model. Immunohistochemical analysis of eutopic endometrium and ectopic lesions from patients with endometriosis revealed significantly reduced nuclear REST expression compared with control endometrium, suggesting loss of functional REST in disease. To assess the physiological consequences of REST deficiency, uterine-specific Rest knockout (Rest d/d ) mice were generated. Rest d/d females exhibited progressive subfertility and hyperestrogenic uterine tissue characteristics that displayed a blunted responsiveness to P4 treatment. Loss of Rest selectively altered expression of P4-responsive genes associated with endometriosis pathology, despite preserved P4 receptor expression. Following induction of experimental endometriosis, female mice that developed endometriotic-like lesions using Rest-deficient donor tissue developed significantly larger lesions that were less responsive to P4 treatment compared to lesions…

items.title: Phosphatases regulating ERK activation and ERK-dependent cell migration
items.summary_raw: Extracellular signal-regulated kinases (ERKs) have essential roles in development and are implicated in numerous diseases. ERKs are activated by phosphorylation and are regulated by dephosphorylation. To study the ERK phosphatases, we adapted a method to monitor ERK activity in live, unfixed preparations that accommodates the highly dynamic temporal and spatial features of ERK activation. We evaluated 140 human phosphatases using an in vivo reporter (ERK-SPARK) for high-throughput screening in human cells, and we used an in vivo Drosophila model for functional validation of their phosphatase homologs. We found that EYA family phosphatases are critical regulators of ERK signaling both in Drosophila and in mammalian cells and found that inhibition of human EYA4, a homolog of Drosophila Eyes Absent phosphatase, enhances migration of ERK-responsive tumor cells. These findings have important implications for the development of therapeutics.

items.title: Modest loss of sleep increases susceptibility to cybersecurity threats
items.summary_raw: Sleep restriction leads to impaired cognitive processing across domains. I examined whether the transition to daylight saving time (DST), typically accompanied by compromised sleep, would lead to an increase in the probability of falling prey to a simulated phishing attack using a fully naturalistic experiment with random assignment and blinding. A predatory email was sent to employees at the University of California, Irvine (N = 11,218) either on the morning of Monday following the transition to DST or one week earlier. The transition led to a ~13% increase in the probability of clicking a suspicious link, without affecting the probability of opening the email or reporting it as spam. These results demonstrate that even modest, mundane, and acute loss of sleep has real-life, potentially hazardous, implications for cognitive function.

items.title: Structural insights into the evolution of mitochondrial protein import from the trypanosome ATOM complex
items.summary_raw: The translocase of the outer membrane (TOM) mediates the import of most mitochondrial preproteins. In the protozoan parasite Trypanosoma brucei , this machinery is replaced by the atypical translocase of the outer membrane (ATOM), whose composition differs substantially from the canonical TOM complexes of fungi and metazoans. Here, we report the cryoelectron microscopy structure of the T. brucei ATOM complex at 2.8 Å resolution. The structure resolves all previously identified components together with an additional, previously uncharacterized subunit. Despite its divergent composition, ATOM retains a conserved dimeric channel architecture and a protein-conducting pathway closely resembling those of opisthokont TOM complexes, indicating that the core mechanism of mitochondrial protein translocation was established early in eukaryotic evolution. In contrast, the receptor and intermembrane-space regions exhibit distinct architectures, revealing extensive evolutionary diversification and multiple examples of convergent evolution. Together, these findings provide a near-atomic view of the ATOM translocase and offer insights into the origin, conservation, and diversification of the mitochondrial protein import machinery across eukaryotes.

items.title: Chromatin dynamics secondary to dexamethasone exposure identifies 67 genes linked to elevated IOP and primary open-angle glaucoma
items.summary_raw: Primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) is a chronic neurodegenerative disorder, and elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) represents its only modifiable risk factor. We modeled increased IOP by treating three primary human trabecular meshwork cell strains with dexamethasone and generated a high-resolution map of promoter-centered chromatin contacts and regulatory modules. We identify dynamic changes in chromatin compartments and looping, cis-regulatory elements, and transcription factor hubs corresponding to altered expression profile. By integrating Genomewide association studies associated variants with dexamethasone induced chromatin landscape, we ascertain 29 target genes linked to 23 lead IOP variants and 57 genes for 46 POAG variants, with 19 shared between the two. Pathway analysis of 67 IOP- and POAG-associated genes reveals enrichment in vesicle transport, TLR, MAPK, and hippo-YAP signaling pathways. We also uncover transcriptional regulatory role of 103 noncoding lead variants. Our studies provide a mechanistic framework of genetic complexity accompanying steroid-induced IOP and related POAG pathology.

items.title: Recurrent hybridization between highly divergent paramecium species
items.summary_raw: The process of speciation, through which two reproductively isolated species emerge from an ancestral population, is often gradual, including a period during which gene flow still occurs, and hence speciation remains reversible. However, if isolation persists, the progressive accumulation of genetic incompatibilities ultimately locks the speciation process, reaching the point where hybrid offspring are inviable or sterile. In plants and animals, the establishment of species barriers is quite rapid: Beyond a net genetic divergence of 0.02 substitutions per synonymous site, interspecific introgressions become extremely rare. Here we report that in ciliates, species barriers can be broken despite huge genetic divergence. We show that the genome of Paramecium sonneborni contains hundreds of DNA segments that were acquired by recurrent horizontal transfers from multiple very distant lineages (synonymous divergence ~1 substitution/site). These segments approach the size of full-length chromosomes, which indicates that they were introgressed by interspecific mating. These data show that in the ancestry of P. sonneborni , hybridization events with highly divergent species occurred repeatedly and led to viable and fertile offspring. We propose that this unexpected promiscuous sexual behavior is made possible by the fact that paramecia separate somatic and germline functions in two types of nuclei: The elimination of non-self-DNA fragments during the development of the somatic genome…

items.title: Correction for Santos et al., Treating language contact as normal: Coalescent-theoretic modeling of the prehistory of the Bantu language family
Lipid droplets buffer hydrogen sulfide–induced redox imbalance
items.summary_raw: The electron transport chain is a signaling hub for hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S) that serves both as a respiratory substrate and an inhibitor. While acute sulfide toxicity is well characterized, cellular adaptations to chronic H 2 S, particularly microbially-derived sulfide exposure in colon, is poorly understood. We report that chronic, low-level H 2 S exposure (4 to 20 µM) drives robust carbon sequestration in lipid droplets (LD) across several human cell lines, driven by a coordinated remodeling of redox and nucleotide metabolism. Specifically, H 2 S-induced reductive shifts in nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD) and coenzyme Q (CoQ) pools are accompanied by glycerol-3-phosphate accumulation and cytidine triphosphate (CTP) depletion. Lipidomic analysis reveals increased neutral lipid synthesis and triacylglyceride accumulation concomitant with decreased CTP-dependent synthesis of membrane phospholipids. Mitochondrial expression of a water-generating NADH oxidase attenuates LD accumulation and spatially confines the origin of H 2 S-induced reductive stress signaling to this compartment. Interestingly, LD abundance increases even after H 2 S withdrawal, continuing over 48 h, during which time the reductively-shifted NAD and CoQ pools slowly reoxidize. Inhibition of fatty acid synthesis during sulfide exposure impairs cellular recovery of respiration. These findings establish an active role for LDs in stress response and reveal that lipid biogenesis is a strategy for…

items.title: PPP1R1B differentially modulates alcohol intake and emotional comorbidity through distinct prefrontal circuits
items.summary_raw: Excessive alcohol consumption frequently co-occurs with anxiety and depression in alcohol use disorder (AUD), yet the specific neural circuits and molecular mechanisms coordinating these comorbid conditions remain poorly defined. The medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), particularly its prelimbic (PL) and infralimbic (IL) subregions, projects to key reward and emotion centers like the nucleus accumbens (Nac) and basolateral amygdala (BLA), but the functional heterogeneity of these projections is unclear. Using chemogenetics, retrograde tracing, electrophysiology, spatial proteomics, and cell-type-specific gene editing in mice subjected to a 4-wk intermittent access to alcohol (IAA) paradigm, we selectively manipulated glutamatergic projections from the PL and IL to the Nac core, Nac shell, and BLA and assessed alcohol intake, anxiety-like, and depression-like behaviors. Chemogenetic activation of PL-Nac core projections reduced short-term alcohol intake, anxiety-, and depression-like behaviors, while IL-BLA activation decreased alcohol consumption and anxiety-like behaviors only. Retrograde tracing revealed mirror-image anatomical segregation of projection-defined neuronal subpopulations within PL/IL linking spatial organization to functional divergence. IAA induced pathway-specific synaptic adaptations. Spatial proteomics nominated protein phosphatase 1 regulatory subunit 1B (PPP1R1B) as a candidate molecule in PL-Nac core neurons. items.title: Linear scaling reveals low-dimensional structure in observable microbial dynamics
items.summary_raw: Microbial communities often exhibit apparently complex dynamics driven by myriad interactions among community members and with their environments. Yet, practical modeling and control are often based on a limited number of observables, raising fundamental questions: are these observed dynamics low-dimensional? If so, how does the low dimensionality enable predictions with limited information? Here, we report an emergent simplicity that the temporal dynamics of observable microbial populations can be captured by low-dimensional representations. Using variational autoencoders, we define a critical latent dimension ( E c ) that operationally quantifies the smallest latent dimension required for high-fidelity reconstruction of observable microbial dynamics under a specified criterion. Despite the complexity of unobserved background dynamics, we find E c to be drastically lower than the community’s apparent degrees of freedom. E c scales linearly with the number of observables, providing an empirical principle for determining representation complexity. This principle holds across simulations of pairwise interacting communities, consumer–resource dynamics, spatially distributed microbial patches, and plasmid transfer, experiments with engineered and environment-derived communities, and human microbiomes. Our findings establish a scaling law for microbial community dynamics and demonstrate that low-dimensional representations of observable dynamics retain information useful for…

items.title: Physiologic and pharmacologic role of the glucocorticoid receptor in germinal center B cells and plasmacytic differentiation
items.summary_raw: In diffuse large B cell lymphoma (DLBCL), a malignancy derived from germinal center (GC) B cells, somatic hypermutation aberrantly targets glucocorticoid receptor (GR) binding sequences in the super-enhancer (SE) of multiple oncogenes. These events abrogate GR binding and deregulate the expression of the SE-linked gene, suggesting an important role of GR in normal and transformed GC B cells. Using a GC-specific Nr3c1 knockout mouse model and multi-omics analyses in murine and human GC B cells, here we show that, under physiological conditions, GR constitutively localizes to the nucleus, where it transcriptionally modulates signaling pathways implicated in GC homeostasis and plasmablast differentiation in part by antagonizing the repressive function of BCL6 on the plasma cell master regulators IRF4 and PRDM1. While loss of baseline GR activity led to mild GC hyperplasia and impaired plasmacytic differentiation, pharmacologic doses of glucocorticoids, a key component of DLBCL chemo-immunotherapy, were preferentially toxic to GC in a GC B cell–autonomous manner. These findings uncover a physiological role for GR in the GC reaction as well as in promoting plasmablast/plasma cell formation and provide insights into the specific activity of glucocorticoids in the treatment of DLBCL.

items.title: Dynamic supercoiling sponsors transcription amplification by MYC
items.summary_raw: Dysregulated MYC provokes profound changes in cancer gene expression. Although usually considered an E-box-dependent transcription activator, an alternate model is that MYC is a universal amplifier of transcription. Although MYC participates in pause release, its full role in the transcription cycle remains poorly illuminated. MYC also stimulates topoisomerases to resolve DNA topological issues complicating its transactions; how this stimulation is coordinated with its transcriptional role has not been examined. We have developed a system that discriminates between MYC-driven activation versus amplification in any cell. This system enables the interrogation of genes, cofactors, and compounds that execute or modulate MYC activity. Using a combination of biochemical and cellular assays, we reveal dynamic interplay between MYC-driven transcription amplification and DNA supercoiling. Because the early stages of transcription are sensitive to DNA supercoiling, Reducing TOP1 activity 1 either through genetic knockdown or low-dose inhibition, potentiates transcription amplification by MYC. By increasing promoter melting and RNA polymerase loading, negative supercoiling provides the early transcription complexes upon which MYC acts to increase output.

items.title: Wearable interstitial fluid sensing of time-resolved uric acid for early prediction of flare-associated pain in an induced mouse model
items.summary_raw: Gout flare is driven by hyperuricemia (HUA) and inflammatory responses to monosodium urate (MSU) crystals, yet single time-point serum uric acid (UA) measurements cannot capture the biochemical dynamics preceding flare onset or explain the timing of severe pain manifestation. Here, we present a skin-attachable interstitial fluid (ISF)-based electrochemical sensing platform for time-resolved, minimally invasive UA monitoring in a controlled, induced mouse model of gout flare-associated inflammation and pain. The platform integrates an enzyme-based UA sensor, a thin insertion electrode, and battery-free near-field communication (NFC), enabling time-resolved in vivo tracking of ISF UA dynamics. By establishing disease-stage-specific models comprising HUA, MSU-only inflammation, and gouty arthritis flare (GA flare) conditions, we separately examined metabolic and inflammatory contributions to flare-associated UA dynamics. Time-resolved ISF monitoring revealed that the GA flare group exhibited pronounced UA fluctuation patterns that were not reproduced by either condition alone. The peak timing of UA dynamics was temporally decoupled from pain-related behavioral responses, indicating that flare-associated pain onset cannot be explained by a single UA concentration. A machine learning framework using ISF UA time-series features identified predictive information preceding peak pain, whereas analyses using earlier events defined by sustained decreases in paw withdrawal threshold…

items.title: PHYTOCHROME INTERACTING FACTOR 7 moderates the activity of phytochrome A in persistent canopy shade conditions
items.summary_raw: In nature, plants perceive and respond to complex vegetative environments through the phytochrome (phy) photoreceptor-signaling system. The Canopy Adaptation Strategy, elicited by phyA, together with the Shade Avoidance Syndrome, regulated by phyB, enables plants to adapt to diverse forms of vegetation shade. The phyA High Irradiance Response mode, which involves photocycle-coupled nuclear shuttling, is essential for sensing sustained far-red-rich conditions typical of canopy or occlusive shade. Our research identifies PHYTOCHROME INTERACTING FACTOR 7 (PIF7) as a key regulator of phyA function. We show that PIF7 overexpression (PIF7ox) effectively suppresses phyA action. Under persistent shade, PIF7 and phyA both accumulate and associate within nuclear photobodies, with this interaction mediated by the C-terminal domain of PIF7 and the PAS-PAS domain of phyA. PIF7 also interacts with FAR-RED ELONGATED HYPOCOTYL 1 (FHY1) and FHY1-LIKE transport facilitators, thereby interfering with phyA cytosolic-nuclear shuttling. This coordinated molecular targeting by PIF7 constitutes an effective strategy for modulating phyA function under persistent shade conditions.

items.title: How Trump plans to fast-track mining in Montana
items.summary_raw: Over the past 20 months, the Trump administration has rolled back regulations and issued executive orders aimed at unilaterally speeding up industrial development projects. In true bureaucratic fashion, even attempts to cut red tape come with a litany of acronyms you may have never heard of. Take, for instance, “FAST-41.” Title 41 of FAST-41, or the Fixing America’s Surface Transportation Act, was originally passed under former President Barack Obama in 2015. It was created as a mechanism to streamline federal review for approval of large-scale infrastructure projects, and improve the public’s access to any permits and documents produced as part of federal review. Infrastructure projects can only be added to the FAST-41 list if they fall under federal review with the National Environmental Policy Act and meet certain size requirements. In a July 2025 executive order, Trump expanded the definition of critical infrastructure projects eligible to be covered under the FAST-41 process to include artificial intelligence data centers. “My Administration will utilize federally owned land and resources for the expeditious and orderly development of data centers,” the directive reads. “This usage will be done in a manner consistent with the land’s intended purpose — to be used in service of the prosperity and security of the American people.” FAST-41 shares similarities with the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, or BAAJA, the permitting bill that passed the Senate this…
