items.title: An organic semiconductor-based photocatalyst sheet for overall solar-driven water splitting
items.summary_raw: Abstract Splitting water into hydrogen and oxygen using sunlight offers a route to renewable fuel, but translating this reaction into systems suitable for industrial implementation remains difficult. Photocatalyst sheets can overcome key limitations of common direct water-splitting approaches (photoelectrochemical devices and photocatalyst dispersions), but existing photocatalyst sheets rely on inorganic semiconductor nanoparticles and processing techniques that can be difficult to scale. Here we show that solution-processed organic semiconductors can form water-splitting photocatalyst sheets by simply tailoring the charge extraction layer beneath the light-absorbing film. A single organic semiconductor active layer (deposited as a bulk heterojunction blend) drives either hydrogen or oxygen evolution depending on its underlying molecular contact, yielding photocathode and photoanode half-cells with well-matched photocurrents. Combining both reactions on one substrate using a microdomain-patterned molecular underlayer affords a photocatalyst sheet that achieves unassisted water splitting under simulated sunlight for over 2 h and generates hydrogen at a stabilized rate of 1.3 µmol h −1 cm −2 , which corresponds to a solar-to-hydrogen conversion efficiency of 0.1%.

items.title: Enabling factors for modular construction methods in developing economies: towards broader adoption in the Global South
items.summary_raw: Purpose Modular construction methods (MCM) have achieved global acknowledgement as a sustainable and effective substitute for conventional construction techniques. Although advanced economies have experienced a rise in adoption, numerous developing nations, especially in the Global South, continue to face challenges with insufficient implementation. This gap highlights the necessity to examine the enabling variables that can promote broader adoption. This study analyses the principal enablers of MCM implementation within the construction industries of Ghana, Nigeria and South Africa to promote the wider integration of modular systems. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative study design was employed, utilising a standardised questionnaire disseminated to construction experts in three countries. The data analysis encompassed mean-score ranking, factor analysis and fuzzy synthetic evaluation (FSE), offering a multidimensional viewpoint on the prioritisation of enablers. Findings The findings highlighted essential enablers, including research, development and innovation; the creation of a supportive industrial environment; policy incentives to attract skilled experts; and improved communication across the AEC industry. Further analysis yielded five principal enabler groupings: strategic policy support, capacity building and knowledge sharing, infrastructure integration, economic flexibility and stakeholder benchmarking. Practical implications These categories provide a…

items.title: Endogenous Determinants of IFRS S2-Based Climate Disclosure in Indonesian State-Owned Enterprises
items.source_name: MAR-Ekonomi Jurnal Manajemen Akuntansi Dan Rumpun Ilmu Ekonomi
items.summary_raw: Climate change creates substantial risks for corporate operations and financial prospects, increasing the need for transparent and comparable climate-related disclosure. This study examines the endogenous determinants of IFRS S2-based climate disclosure among Indonesian listed State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs) and SOE-affiliated companies. The endogenous factors include board size, independent commissioners, audit committee size, independent audit committee members, institutional ownership, government ownership, firm size, profitability, leverage, and the COVID-19 period. A quantitative approach was applied to 22 companies selected through purposive sampling during 2020–2023, resulting in 88 firm-year observations. IFRS S2-based disclosure was measured using content analysis covering 57 items across governance, strategy, risk management, and metrics and targets. Panel-data regression was performed using the Random Effect Model. The results demonstrate that profitability has a positive and significant effect on IFRS S2-based disclosure, whereas the COVID-19 period has a negative and significant effect. Meanwhile, corporate governance mechanisms, ownership structure, firm size, and leverage have no significant effects. These findings indicate that economic resources and crisis conditions are more influential in determining climate-disclosure quality than formal governance structures. Therefore, Indonesian SOEs should strengthen climate-governance competence, sustainability…

items.title: Co-creating Taita-Taveta County energy demand projections for integrated national energy planning in Kenya through a mixed methods modelling approach
items.summary_raw: Energy devolution in Kenya has progressed unevenly, with many counties yet to complete their County Energy Plans (CEPs), posing challenges for integration into the forthcoming Integrated National Energy Plan (INEP). A key gap lies in translating qualitative, needs-based insights from county planning documents into quantitative inputs for energy demand modelling. This study applies a mixed-methods approach to address this gap. Building on existing Model for the Analysis of Energy Demand (MAED)-based datasets and multi-scale modelling frameworks, we develop a structured process to translate qualitative planning narratives into quantitative scenario assumptions. Using Taita Taveta County (TTC) as a case study, we construct four demand scenarios (baseline, ambitious, reserved, and a county priorities scenario). The latter is co-developed through interviews, a workshop, and analysis of CEP and County Integrated Development Plan (CIDP) documents with 26 county and national stakeholders. The county priorities scenario is operationalised by systematically mapping qualitative insights, such as electrification ambitions, cooking transitions, and sectoral development priorities, onto model parameters, including electrification rates, fuel shares, sectoral composition, and technical coefficients. The resulting scenarios illustrate how aligning modelling assumptions with county planning narratives produces different demand trajectories and sectoral structures compared to nationally…

items.title: Multimodal misinformation: from climate conspiracy to climate obstruction on TikTok
items.summary_raw: This article examines how conspiratorial climate claims on TikTok are constructed through multimodality, meaning made through visuals, sound, and text, and function as climate obstruction. While conspiratorial and audiovisual climate misinformation are increasingly prominent, research has largely focused on text-based analyses of mainstream platforms, overlooking how meaning, affect, and attention are organized through multimodal communication on visual-first, sound-on platforms. The study asks: what thematic patterns emerge from a large corpus of TikTok videos on climate and weather modification; how are conspiratorial narratives constructed by integrating visual, sonic, and textual cues to mobilize emotional engagement, with what implications for climate obstruction? The analysis combines computational multimodal topic modeling of 7,658 TikTok videos with theory-informed qualitative multimodal framing analysis on 27 topics (1,220 posts), drawing on framing theory, social semiotics, and sociology of emotions. It shows how conspiratorial meaning is assembled distributively across posts and modes. Findings identify a distinct conspiracy variant that affirms anthropogenic climate change while redefining its cause as covert technological intervention by powerful actors, falling outside established climate misinformation typologies. Conspiratorial framing mobilizes an interplay between fear and epistemic emotions such as curiosity, redirecting attention from climate toward…

items.title: Between social democracy and neoliberalism in a world in crisis: putting the Albanese Labor Government in context
items.summary_raw: This special issue explores social democracy, labourism, and neoliberalism through investigations of the Albanese Labor Government’s first-term. Bringing together political science, political economy, and public policy, the contributions examine the Albanese Government’s ideological commitments and how it has governed policy domains in crisis, such as housing, climate, and higher education. This introduction discusses the context for the rise of the Albanese Government, including the global ‘polycrisis’, widespread discontent with politics, and Labor’s electoral strategy. We frame the contributions of the special issue as examining the space between two poles. On one side, conceptualising Labor as attempting to address crises while hamstrung by decades of neoliberalism. On the other, understanding Labor as hewing to the neoliberal status quo and possessing a limited appetite for social democratic change. We position the special issue to contribute to wider debates on the challenges of social democratic policymaking in an era of global crisis.

items.title: LEXICAL-SEMANTIC AND ETHNOLINGUISTIC FEATURES OF CLIMATE- RELATED GEOGRAPHICAL TERMS IN THE AZERBAIJANI LANGUAGE
items.summary_raw: In the geographical terminology of the Azerbaijani language, lexical units denoting climate and atmospheric phenomena constitute a distinct system. Some of the terms belonging to this system entered Azerbaijani under the influence of international scientific terminology, whereas others developed as linguistic reflections of the centuries-long observations made by the people concerning natural phenomena. The article examines the origin, structural and semantic features of climate-related terms in Azerbaijani, as well as the relationship between scientific terminology and folk geographical vocabulary. Particular attention is paid to the rich nomenclature of winds, rain and snow and it is demonstrated that these units are lexicalised on the basis of the intensity, duration, direction and seasonality of natural phenomena, their effects on agriculture, and their regional characteristics. Alongside internationally used terms such as advection, aerology, bora, boreal climate, arid climate, trade wind, monsoon, and breeze, the semantics of national and regional units such as ağ yel, qara yel, elqovan, keçiqıran, vәdә külәyi, qurd yağışı, gәzәngi, kәpәk qar, quşbaşı qar, and heyvagülü qar are analysed. The role of colour-denoting words, especially the components ağ “white” and qara “black”, in the formation of meteorological terms is also considered separately. The evidence shows that in folk terminology climatic phenomena are named not only according to their physical…

items.title: Street Fights and Court Battles: Incumbent mobilization and the timing of regulatory bans against platform entrants
items.summary_raw: In this paper, we examine how incumbent-led mobilization against Uber’s platform entry in Europe relates to regulatory bans, public attention, and consumer-side uptake. Combining hand-coded data on taxi-sector tactics and frames with first regulatory bans, Uber app downloads, and Google search interest across 22 European countries from 2012 to 2020, we identify a differentiated temporal pattern. Private tactics are strongly associated with first-ban hazard in the short window following mobilization, whereas lawsuits are positively associated over a longer window. The frames incumbents deploy also matter: legitimacy-challenge frames portraying UberPop as incompatible with lawful and fair competition are more consistently associated with bans than compliance-dispute frames focused on tax or labor obligations. At the same time, private tactics and lawsuits coincide with immediate increases in app downloads and Google search interest, indicating an attention spillover from incumbent contestation. Lawsuit-related download elevations display marginally greater persistence than those associated with private tactics, although this difference is not stronger early after entry. Taken together, the findings show that incumbent mobilization in platform markets can be associated with regulatory bans and consumer-side uptake of the entrants they seek to exclude at the same time. The results establish temporal association, although the direction of influence within this process cannot be…

items.title: How and When Incivility Unfolds in Online Heatwave Communication: Characterizing Public Discussions on Reddit
items.summary_raw: The increasing frequency of heatwaves has sparked widespread concern and emotionally charged, often uncivil, discussions on social media. Drawing on heatwave communication and online incivility research, this study investigates how incivility manifests, arises, and spreads in Reddit discussions about heatwaves between 2023 and 2024. Specifically, it examines the forms of incivility expressed, contexts in which incivility is more likely to occur, and how incivility spreads across comment layers. Using natural language processing (i.e. topic modeling and emotion analysis) as well as a large language model-assisted incivility detection approach, we analyzed 1,369 posts, 10,800 first-layer comments, and 7,297 second-layer comments from eight climate- and country-related subreddits. Results revealed that incivility was more prevalent in comments than in posts, with first-layer incivility significantly predicting second-layer instances, suggesting a contagion effect that persisted across comment layers. Comments expressing anger, disgust, and sadness were more likely to be uncivil, and controversial topics like climate change attribution, geopolitical conflicts, and regional impacts correlated with higher incivility. Theoretical and practical implications were discussed.

items.title: Climate Change and Crisis of Multilateralism: Why do States Struggle to Cooperate on Shared Global Threats?
items.summary_raw: Climate change is a shared global threat that requires coordinated action among states, yet international cooperation remains slow, fragmented, and insufficient. This paper examines the crisis of multilateralism in global climate governance by asking why states struggle to cooperate despite the growing severity of climate impacts. Drawing on collective-action theory and the concept of global commons, the study argues that sovereignty, competing national interests, free-riding, and unequal power relations undermine effective climate cooperation. It analyzes the evolution of the UNFCCC, Kyoto Protocol, and Paris Agreement, showing that broader participation has often come at the cost of weaker enforcement and lower ambition. The paper further examines how geopolitical rivalry, climate finance disputes, and the North–South divide deepen mistrust between developed and developing countries. It concludes that reviving climate multilateralism requires stronger accountability, predictable finance, equitable burden-sharing, sectoral cooperation, and renewed leadership by major emitters. Keywords: Climate Change; Multilateralism; Global Commons; Collective Action; North–South Divide

items.title: Molluscs in a Changing Amazon: Ecological Importance, Climate-Crisis Vulnerability, and Taxonomic and Funding Constraints in Brazil
items.summary_raw: Molluscs contribute to food webs, nutrient cycling, food production and environmental reconstruction across Amazonian forests, inland waters and coastal habitats. This critical narrative review examines climate-impact pathways and the limits of regional evidence, while distinguishing biological vulnerability from the institutional capacity to assess and manage it. A targeted literature update links regional case studies with explicitly identified evidence from other Neotropical and extra-regional systems. Studies from the Caeté basin, the Amazon mangrove coast and a floodplain lake near Iquitos document habitat associations, reproductive seasonality and shell-isotope signals, respectively; they do not establish basin-wide climate-driven declines. Drought-associated mortality outside Amazonia and marine physiological experiments identify plausible mechanisms requiring regional tests. National catalogue and specialist assessments indicate knowledge gaps but cannot quantify transboundary Amazonian richness or climate risk. Priorities include voucher-based inventories, monitoring of recruitment and adult survival, habitat-specific experiments, and protection of hydrological connectivity and moist refugia. A staged ten-year programme is proposed, with conservation outcomes assessed separately from research outputs. Sustained taxonomic and institutional capacity can reduce identification uncertainty and delays in management; its effects should not be conflated with a population’s…

items.title: Missed Opportunities Forgo One-Third of Mass Timber’s Carbon Storage Potential
items.summary_raw: Abstract Building materials are increasingly positioned as a scalable option for carbon dioxide removal (CDR). Carbon-storing engineered wood products, such as structural mass timber, will be instrumental for CDR. However, system-level perspectives can overlook operational choices that forfeit storage potential. Using stage-resolved life-cycle inventories, scenario-aware uncertainty analysis, and dynamic carbon accounting, we trace carbon flows across mass timber supply chains in the United States, from harvest slash and mill residue to wood products through end-of-life. Across modeled deployment scenarios, we show that management decisions, not technical limits, cut 1.4–2.6 gigatons (Gt) of CO2e storage by 2120, corresponding to roughly one-third of mass timber’s storage potential. Globally, storage losses from these choices could reach 3.8–12 Gt CO2e. We outline a storage-first pathway including slash pyrolysis, diversion of mill residue from bioenergy to wood panel markets, and reuse or pyrolysis at end-of-life. Together, these strategies redirect carbon into value-added, long-lived pools rather than short-lived fates, showing that release timing and supply chain routing choices can matter more than production decarbonization in shaping warming outcomes under mass timber deployment. If implemented, these choices recover forgone storage and aid in developing the built environment as a durable carbon reservoir.

items.title: A Bayesian network analysis of survey climate and response intention in official statistics
items.summary_raw: Declining response rates and growing concerns about nonresponse bias threaten the quality of official statistics. Although prior studies have identified various factors associated with survey cooperation, such as privacy concerns, response burden, and political trust, most have examined these determinants independently without modeling the dependency structure among them. This study applied Bayesian networks to data from a web-based survey conducted in Japan to explore the probabilistic dependency structure linking broader social orientations, survey attitudes and perceptions, and response intention in official statistical surveys. The analysis identified relationships in which perceived social fairness was associated with trust in official statistics, which, in turn, was associated with survey response intention. Perceptions of others’ honesty in answering sensitive income questions were linked to individuals’ willingness to respond to such items, which was in turn associated with overall participation intention. Community participation was associated with opinions on social issues, which were in turn linked to response intention toward official statistical surveys. These findings suggest that intention to cooperate with official statistical surveys is embedded in broader social orientations. Understanding these dependency structures may help generate hypotheses about variables that could be examined in future studies of actual nonresponse and nonresponse adjustment.

items.title: Youth Voices in Times of Climate Change: Strengthening Young People’s Political Agency Through Participatory Workshops
Climate regulation and civil society activism
items.summary_raw: This paper examines how climate public regulation shapes NGO activism against firms. We develop a private-politics framework where regulation alters campaign incentives through two opposing mechanisms: a cost-reducing channel lowering monitoring costs, and a value-diminishing channel where state compliance substitutes for private pressure. When the cost-reducing channel dominates, public regulation crowds in civil-society activism. Testing these predictions on a novel monthly panel of NGOs across 76 countries (2010–2023) within an event-study design, we show that executive regulations trigger a persistent increase in firm-targeted activism without pre-trend anticipation. Textual evidence shows that NGOs explicitly invoke regulatory benchmarks in their campaigns and that their use around enactment is not confined to campaigns already underway. Mobilization is strongest in weaker regulatory environments and concentrated among national NGOs targeting domestic firms. Together, these findings demonstrate that public regulation mobilizes civil society as an informal enforcement layer, extending climate governance beyond formal state action.

items.title: “Life” as Biofoundry in the Technocene: Politics of Extraction and Resistance in Saad Z. Hossain’s Speculative Narratives
items.summary_raw: The paper examines Saad Z. Hossain’s The Gurkha and the Lord of Tuesday (2019) and “Bring Your Own Spoon” (2021) as speculative imaginings of the Technocene, where technology becomes an epochal subject and constructs hierarchical structures through its influence on the human and the nonhuman natural world. Drawing on Agostino Cera’s feralization of man, Anna Tsing et al.’s concept of feral patches, and Elizabeth Povinelli’s distinction between Life and Nonlife, the paper argues that geoengineering and bioengineering procedures become interlocked extractive apparatuses that operate as state- or corporate-funded solutions to climate crisis. While geoengineering manages carbon-as-Nonlife, bioengineering manages carbon-as-Life. Both extractive infrastructures turn the bodies of the environmentally poor into biofoundries. Using Ramachandra Guha’s Structural-Organizational and Political-Cultural paradigms of protest, the paper examines Hossain’s literary representations of how the environmentally poor refuse the imposed condition of surviving as developmental refugees in a poor environment, and ultimately resist the biotechnical extraction of their labor.

items.title: The Opportunity to Learn Mathematics in Contrasting School Climates
items.source_name: The International Journal of Science Mathematics and Technology Learning
items.summary_raw: This study examines how school climate conditions are associated with Grade 5 learners’ opportunities to learn mathematics in Norway, South Africa, and Türkiye, drawing on data from the Trends in International Mathematics and Science Study (TIMSS) 2023. Guided by an ecological–opportunity-to-learn (OTL) comparative framework, the analysis focuses on bullying, safety, discipline, and classroom order as learning-relevant conditions. A comparative descriptive design with effect size estimation was applied to nationally representative samples (Norway: n = 5,301; South Africa: n = 10,424; Türkiye: n = 4,541). The results indicate that positive school climate conditions are associated with higher mathematics achievement and that the strength of these associations varies across contexts. Bullying shows the strongest negative association with mathematics achievement in South Africa (d = 0.51), while discipline and safety exhibit substantial positive associations in Norway and moderate associations in Türkiye. The results suggest that school climate indicators are patterned alongside variation in mathematics outcomes, with broader systemic conditions, including equity policies, structural inequality, and governance arrangements, providing important contextual framing. The study demonstrates how international large-scale assessments can be used diagnostically to illuminate context-sensitive learning conditions rather than as instruments for causal attribution, thereby supporting more…

items.title: Climate Change Familiarity and Travel Intention: The Parallel Mediating Roles of Environmental and Social Sustainability Perceptions
items.summary_raw: This study examines whether environmental and social sustainability perceptions of a destination mediate the association between climate change familiarity and travel intention. Drawing on the knowledge–attitude–behavior approach and the theory of planned behavior, climate change familiarity was conceptualized as a second-order construct comprising media climate news, personal environmental experience, and perceived climate knowledge. Survey data from 409 residents of Mersin, Türkiye, who had previously visited Istanbul were analyzed using bootstrap-based structural equation modeling. Climate change familiarity was positively associated with both sustainability perceptions but showed no significant direct association with travel intention. Social sustainability perception was positively associated with travel intention and transmitted a positive indirect association that held across all model specifications. Environmental sustainability perception was negatively associated with travel intention only when social sustainability was controlled for; this pattern reflected statistical suppression and did not hold in a single-mediator model. The findings show that aggregated sustainability measures may mask dimension-specific mechanisms. Given the cross-sectional design, the results represent associations; for destinations facing climate-related risks, they suggest that the social dimension of sustainability deserves attention in sustainability communication.

items.title: Cross-vector flexibility in sector-coupled low-carbon energy systems
items.summary_raw: This paper holistically assesses the current literature by examining how cross-vector flexibility is observed, coordinated, and verified in low-carbon energy systems based on sector coupling. To this end, the interplay between cross-vector flexibility, digital twins and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled observability, predictive control approaches, local coordination mechanisms, and flexibility markets is addressed within a common analytical framework. This review shows that cross-vector flexibility is more than an energy conversion technology problem; it is also a coordination problem. Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) framework, a systematic Scopus search and screening process yielded an analytical core of 107 studies. Within this core, only 19 studies (17.8%) progress beyond synthetic simulation: thirteen use real or case-based data, six provide co-simulation, hardware-in-the-loop or closed-loop field evidence, and none verifies delivered flexibility against a baseline. Observability is addressed as a primary concern in only seven of the 107 studies, making it the least represented layer of the coordination stack. In addition, 88 studies (82.2% of the core) represent no socio-technical conditions. The value of flexibility depends not only on the capacity to shift, store, or convert energy, but also on the ability to monitor system states, ensure coordination between different actors and energy carriers, verify the…

items.title: Circular Synergy for Sustainable Architecture in Nigeria.
items.source_name: WORLD JOURNAL OF INNOVATION AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY
items.summary_raw: This paper explores the integration of green architecture and circular economy principles in Nigeria, aiming to achieve sustainable development goals. Leveraging Building Information Modeling (BIM), the study examines BIM's role in driving sustainable practices within the Nigerian construction industry. The paper showcases how BIM facilitates lifecycle analysis, facility management, and retrofitting of existing buildings for improved energy performance and circularity. Real-world examples illustrate BIM's potential to enhance building sustainability and operational efficiency. Furthermore, the study emphasizes BIM's contribution to collaborative decision-making and stakeholder engagement. BIM-driven communication tools effectively convey sustainable architecture concepts to diverse stakeholders. Addressing challenges, the paper underscores the need for policy support and capacity building to encourage BIM adoption in green architectural projects in Nigeria. In conclusion, embracing BIM as a catalyst for sustainable architecture and circular economy practices can accelerate Nigeria's transition towards a greener, more resilient, and socially equitable future.

items.title: Agroforestry, Climate Resilience, and Land Degradation in OECD Economies: Roles of Innovation and Finance
items.summary_raw: ABSTRACT Despite the growing prominence of agroforestry practices in environmental research, its specific impact on climate‐induced land vulnerability, land degradation, and territorial carbon dioxide emissions is insufficiently explored in OECD economies. This study investigates how nonlinear effects of agroforestry practices, financial markets, innovation, environmental taxes, along with final consumption expenditure, determine territory‐based carbon emissions in OECD countries over the period 1994–2021. This study applied the second‐generation Driscoll–Kraay technique to analyze the data, while quantile regression serves as a nonparametric approach as a robustness check. The results show that agroforestry has inverted‐U shaped curve underlying that agroforestry in the initial stages may cause land degradation while at the later stages, it supports the climate resilience practices and land restoration in OECD economies. Moreover, financial development exerts heterogeneous effects in both models, suggesting differing channels of support for financial development. Green innovation and environmental taxes significantly reduce territorial carbon emissions, while final consumption expenditure, as theoretically expected, increases it. The results show robustness through nonparametric quantile regression with the role of income. Policy implications emphasize the adaptive framework of financial mechanisms, innovation, and environmental taxation to support agroforestry practices in…

items.title: Income differences in high-carbon activities, climate perceptions and behavioral willingness: an exploratory analysis of a UK survey
items.summary_raw: Introduction Radical actions across all sectors of the economy are necessary to meet stringent carbon emission reduction targets, which requires the widespread adoption of low-carbon technologies as well as significant lifestyle changes. However, carbon emissions are not evenly distributed across households—both globally and within countries—indicating that different income groups have unequal responsibilities for reducing emissions. Policy directed at higher-income households therefore rests on untested assumption that those who contribute more feel more responsible and are more ready to act given their greater resources. Method As an initial step, this exploratory study uses secondary data from a survey conducted in October and November 2023 in the UK, which oversampled higher-income respondents, to examining income-based differences in activities associated with high-carbon consumption, climate perceptions, and willingness to engage in pro-environmental behaviors. Results Results show that higher-income groups are more likely to engage in activities associated with high-carbon consumption, as indicated by their flying, car ownership, and recent purchases of household items. However, income groups in the UK do not differ significantly in their climate perceptions, including concern about climate change, feelings of guilt, or a sense of personal responsibility to take climate action. Higher-income groups also show less willingness to reduce those activities, most clearly…

items.title: Framing of Indonesia's New Capital: Cultural Narratives in Online News Coverage
items.source_name: ADPEBI International Journal of Business and Social Science
items.summary_raw: Purpose – This study examines how Indonesian online news media frame the development of the new capital city, Nusantara, and embed cultural narratives, national identity, and political legitimacy within their coverage. Methodology – Using a qualitative framing analysis based on Pan and Kosicki's model, the study analyzes five purposively selected articles from DetikNews and DetikJatim published during the 2022 ceremonial inauguration. The analysis focuses on syntactic, script, thematic, and rhetorical structures. Findings – The coverage constructs Nusantara as a symbolic national project rather than a purely administrative or infrastructural policy. Four dominant frames emerge: nation-building, cultural symbolism, political legitimacy, and developmentalism. Rituals involving soil and water, the Kendi Nusantara, presidential leadership, and references to Majapahit connect capital relocation with territorial unity, historical continuity, and modernization. Conclusion – Online journalism transforms policy communication into culturally resonant narratives that shape public interpretations of national identity, authority, and development. Novelty – The study extends digital framing research by demonstrating how textual structures and symbolic storytelling jointly legitimize a large-scale development initiative, offering a conceptual explanation of how cultural meaning, political power, and developmental aspirations converge in online news discourse within Indonesia's digital…

items.title: From Agrivoltaics Design to Energy-System Planning: A Critical Integrative Review
items.summary_raw: Agrivoltaics (AV) integrates photovoltaic electricity generation with continued agricultural production on the same land. This critical integrative review examines AV as solar-energy infrastructure, focusing on configuration trade-offs, the translation of land and crop outcomes into energy-system variables, techno-economic boundary conditions, and policy and ownership arrangements for scalable deployment. The review covers the literature from the foundational agrivoltaics work published in 1982 onward and combines searches across multiple academic databases with authoritative institutional sources and backward and forward citation chaining. Eligible sources were English-language studies addressing active agricultural production combined with PV, together with relevant authoritative policy, legal, spatial, and energy-planning sources; conventional PV without continued agricultural activity, duplicate reports, non-verifiable commentary, and studies lacking evidence relevant to the review questions were excluded. Selected studies report land equivalent ratios above 1, although differences in crop type, PV configuration, reference systems, land-area accounting, and temporal boundaries preclude interpretation as a pooled effect estimate. The evidence shows that no AV configuration is universally superior: elevated and tracking systems can preserve machinery access and enable dynamic light management but increase structural and operational burden; spaced systems simplify…

items.title: The Care-ful Work of Climate Litigation: A Study of Women Climate Defenders
items.summary_raw: Climate litigation, often led by women, requires demanding work with little acknowledgement or support. The article argues that this work is a form of caring labour aimed at reproducing human society as well as the environment within which we are enmeshed. Rethinking care as including the environment draws from Indigenous ideas of ‘care for Country’, ecofeminist conceptions of our relationality with the rest of nature, and some versions of social reproduction theory. Broader ideas of care can help to challenge anthropocentricism in our legal frameworks as well as promote improved recognition of caring labour in law. This argument emerges from a study of women climate defenders who engaged in litigation in Australia. The article documents six court cases and discusses the interview responses of the women who led these to consider the following: their motivations for doing this work; their experience of the legal process; the relevance of gender in their work as well as their thoughts on this work as care or ‘care for Country’; and their ideas for improved support for this work. The article suggests that the views and actions of these women inspire future consideration of ways of supporting climate defence while embedding environmental responsibilities in law.

items.title: The electron as ‘chokepoint’: grid connection policy and the infrastructural governance of computation
Wild boar as the state: Wildlife/state of agricultural decline and reproduction at the Hungarian–Slovenian border
items.summary_raw: The article examines a popular story framing the state’s introduction of wild boars into the local environment of the Hungarian-Slovenian borderlands as a purposeful act aimed at harming peasants. By presenting animal agency as the agency of the state (wildlife/state), the narrative projects an image of an insidious state expanding into the local environment under the guise of seemingly natural forces. The article explores how this story resonates differently in neighbouring borderlands, depending on their contrasting political, economic, and ecological histories. In one borderland, it laments the bygone era of peasant agriculture; in the other, where household farming persists, the story helps sustain resistance against the state as a steward of wildlife in the context of peasants’ struggle to secure reproduction. Meanwhile, in this other context, hunters, as state representatives, contest the narrative. They highlight the natural increase in the wild boar population as indicative of their, and the state’s, limited influence on wildlife. Framing the narrative of the wild boar and the state as a purported historical event conveys different moral and political messages in neighbouring borderlands and among various actors; it can be viewed as a framing the past, but it can also apply that past to current boundary work and class struggle.

items.title: Another novel nuclear project gets green light to start construction
items.summary_raw: The United States just cleared another novel nuclear energy project to begin construction. On Monday, the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission approved a joint application by X-energy and Dow Chemical to build four Xe-100 advanced nuclear reactors at a Texas industrial site owned by the Michigan-based chemicals giant.…

items.title: Programmable multistable structures via bioinspired, mechanically guided 4D printing
items.summary_raw: Multistable structures, characterized by rapid shape morphing, instantaneous force amplification, and zero standby power, are pivotal for soft robotics and energy harvesting. However, achieving multistability while systematically controlling the accessible deformation modes remains a significant challenge. Here, we report a bioinspired, mechanically guided 4D printing approach to design and fabricate programmable multistable structures, including octastable and various bistable units, mimicking the growth-induced morphing of plant leaves and fruits. The stability landscapes of these units can be tuned by varying dimensionless geometric parameters and validated through buckling analysis. By integrating multiple octastable units, we demonstrate a compact, 10-cm-scale strip and a shape-morphing metasurface with configuration spaces of over one billion and four sextillion stable states. Furthermore, by modulating the dimensionless geometric parameters of multiunit structures, we identify a transition from bending to folding, enabling the creation of bistable hinges. As proof-of-concept demonstrations, we developed devices for directional droplet routing and mixing, reconfigurable electrical switching, conforming grasping of irregular objects, and programmable mechanical display. This work establishes a versatile framework for the design and fabrication of next-generation reconfigurable morphing systems and programmable flexible devices.

items.title: Elastic tricriticality at the collapse of magnetic order in a valence fluctuating Eu-based compound
items.summary_raw: Spin and charge fluctuations are key for understanding the properties of materials with strongly correlated electrons, but their coupling to the atomic crystal lattice is often assumed to be weak and perturbative. In this work, we demonstrate that at tricritical points (TCPs), that are associated with electronic correlations, a coupling to crystal elasticity is generically nonperturbative. It will modify the tricritical universality class leading to elastic tricriticality , characterized by a compressibility that diverges in a universal manner with the correlation length. To test this scenario experimentally, we use single crystals of EuPd 2 (Si 1− x Ge x ) 2 where, depending on x and pressure, magnetic order collapses due to strong valence fluctuations. First, we confirm the presence of a TCP for x ≈ 0.1 by using complementary probes, in particular, measurements of relative length changes under control of temperature and He-gas pressure. Second, by studying the elastic response, we uncover clear signatures of elastic tricriticality, notably a drastically enhanced compressibility.

items.title: Disruption of the NTCP–EGFR receptor complex as a strategy for selective inhibition of hepatitis B and D virus entry
items.summary_raw: Hepatitis B and D virus (HBV, HDV) enter hepatocytes through a coordinated process mediated by a receptor complex consisting of sodium taurocholate cotransporting polypeptide (NTCP), and host entry cofactors, including epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR). Here, we established an in vitro assay to evaluate the NTCP–EGFR interaction and identified Oxy229, an oxysterol-based compound that disrupted this molecular interaction. Oxy229 selectively inhibited HBV and HDV infection to HepG2-NTCP cells and primary human hepatocytes. Mechanistic analysis revealed that Oxy229 impaired the relocalization of HBV–NTCP complex from the plasma membrane to intracellular vesicles. Notably, Oxy229 did not compromise the physiological functions of NTCP and EGFR, i.e., bile acid transporter and activation of downstream EGFR signaling pathways including Ras–MAPK and PI3K–Akt pathways, indicating selective inhibition of viral entry. Compound derivative analysis identified Oxy283, which acquired dual inhibitory activity against both NTCP–EGFR interaction and NTCP multimerization, resulting in enhanced anti-HBV potency. These findings establish the functional significance of NTCP–receptor complex formation in the HBV/HDV entry and highlight this machinery as a potential target for antiviral intervention.

items.title: Stereodynamical control of a four-atom reaction: HD + OH → D + H 2 O
items.summary_raw: To date, studies of differential steric effect in reactive collisions have been limited to atom + molecule systems. How stereodynamics is affected when the other reactant is also a molecule remains an open question. Here, we present a combined high-resolution crossed-beam scattering and full-dimensional quantum dynamical study of the HD ( v = 1, j = 2) + OH → D + H 2 O reaction, in which the HD molecular axis was initially prepared either parallel or perpendicular to the relative velocity using the stimulated Raman pumping scheme. The OH reactant was unpolarized and in its ground vibrational state, with a rotational temperature of ~85 K in the experiment, and was restricted to the ground rovibrational state in the theory. Pronounced stereodynamic effects are observed in both the backward scattering intensity and the product angular distributions. Detailed analysis of scattering wavefunctions reveals that the initial m = ±2 states access a noncoplanar dynamical transition state, distinct from that accessed by m = 0 ( m denotes the projection of j along the direction of relative velocity). The nonzero dihedral angle, a geometric degree of freedom absent in triatomic reactions, leads to reduced reactivity and enhances sideward scattering for the perpendicular configuration, while leaving the product rovibrational state distributions essentially unchanged. In addition, the alignment of the HD rotational angular momentum is preserved in the rotational direction of the product H 2…

items.title: Homeostatic control of stem cell activity during intestinal regeneration
items.summary_raw: Stem cells proliferate rapidly to maintain tissue turnover during regeneration, yet the mechanisms preventing hyperproliferation remain unclear. Here, we identified nuclear factor Y (NF-Y) as a transcriptional repressor that maintains intestinal stem cell (ISC) quiescence. NF-Y restricts ISC proliferation by occupying the promoters of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) signaling components, including Egfr , Mkp3 , Raf , Ras , and pnt , through regulation dependent on the histone acetyltransferase Nejire (Nej)/p300. Loss of NF-Y enhances ISC proliferation and accelerates tumor progression. NF-Y acts with Nej to restrict Egfr expression and suppress hyperproliferation. Together, these results demonstrate that NF-Y, acting with Nej, serves as a key transcriptional repressive brake that restrains growth-signaling to control stem cell activity under homeostatic and disease conditions.

items.title: Acute degradation of Pumilio proteins reveals a biphasic posttranscriptional regulatory hierarchy in embryonic stem cell fate decision
items.summary_raw: Posttranscriptional regulation is critical for mammalian embryogenesis yet has been underexplored. We previously showed that RNA-binding Pumilio proteins (Pum1/2) are essential for early mouse embryogenesis and embryonic stem cell (ESC) functions. Here, using acute protein degradation systems combined with time-resolved RNA sequencing and enhanced crosslinking and immunoprecipitation, we delineate a two-phase regulatory hierarchy modulated by Pum1/2 in mouse ESCs. The first phase, occurring within 10 h of Pum1/2 depletion, is predominantly stabilization of over 100 Pum1/2-target mRNAs, while the second phase, occurring in subsequent 66 h, propagates to over 1,000 mRNAs mostly through indirect regulatory effects. Functionally, Pum1/2 depletion delays transition from naïve to formative pluripotency and alters expression trajectories of neuroectoderm and germline genes during early differentiation. Mechanistically, Pum1/2 directly repress mRNAs encoding Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 subunits, including Suz12 , thereby potentially constraining H3K27me3 deposition at neuroectodermal gene loci. These findings establish Pum1/2 as biphasic posttranscriptional regulators of pluripotency and lineage balance.

items.title: The highly heat-inducible HspA6 and the thermolabile DnaJB5 are potent regulators of heat shock transcription factor 1 activity
items.summary_raw: In response to proteotoxic stress the central regulator of the heat shock response (HSR) in mammalian cells, Hsf1, trimerizes, binds DNA, and drives transcription of heat shock genes. We previously showed that Hsc70 (HspA8) assisted by its J-domain protein (JDP) cochaperone DnaJB1 dissociates Hsf1 from DNA by monomerizing the trimeric Hsf1 and thereby attenuates the HSR. Whether this feedback mechanism is specific to the HspA8–DnaJB1 pair or instead reflects a broader, isoform- and JDP-selective Hsp70 network controlling Hsf1 remained unresolved. Here, we demonstrate that of all cytonuclear Hsp70s the highly heat-inducible HspA6 is most efficient in monomerizing Hsf1 in the presence of DnaJB1 and of all cytonuclear class A and class B JDPs, only DnaJB1, DnaJB4, and DnaJB5 assist in Hsf1 monomerization. Whereas cooperation of HspA6 and HspA8 with DnaJB1 and DnaJB4 absolutely depends on Hsp70s’ C-terminal glutamate-glutamate-valine-glutamate (EEVD)-motif, cooperation with DnaJB5 does not. Consistent with these data, overproduction of EEVD-deleted HspA8 and HspA6 down-regulate the HSR in HeLa cells. DnaJB5 knockdown reduces HspA8–Hsf1 interaction under nonstress conditions revealing DnaJB5 as major targeting factor for HspA8 binding to Hsf1. On temperature upshift DnaJB5 partially unfolds and partitions into insoluble cell fractions, suggesting it is a thermosensor that allows for increased Hsf1 activity by reducing HspA8’s ability to monomerize Hsf1. During ongoing heat shock…

items.title: VAMP725 and VAMP726 interact with cellulose synthase to support secondary cell wall formation
items.summary_raw: The formation of plant cell walls underpins morphogenesis, growth, and development of all plants. Cellulose is an essential and load-bearing cell wall polymer that is synthesized by Cellulose Synthase (CESA) protein complexes at the plasma membrane. In this study, we reveal that SNARE proteins Vesicle Associated Membrane Protein 726 (VAMP726) and VAMP725 associate with multiple CESA proteins. Consistent with these results, the VAMP726 is codelivered with the CESA proteins to the plasma membrane, and the proteins colocalize at intracellular compartments. We further show that the VAMPs, especially VAMP726, are important for CESA trafficking and sustenance of cellulose synthesis both in growing tissues and in secondary wall producing maturing tissues. Taken together, our study outlines an important intracellular process whereby VAMP proteins facilitate trafficking of CESA complexes during cellulose synthesis.

items.title: RNA and proteins joined up at the origins of life: Persistence is the point
items.summary_raw: What drove nucleic acids (NA) into functional associations with proteins (PR) at the origins of life? We reason from polymer physics and the Central Dogma that the fitness value of cooperating through a division of labor—NA for replication fidelity and PR for functional fitness—is much higher than for either polymer alone. Our model shows a Pareto Front, where NA and PR can bootstrap each other to achieve autocatalytic cooperativity toward biology.

items.title: Host infection selects for sRNA variants that drive bacterial social cheating
items.summary_raw: Single-nucleotide mutations in regulatory small RNAs (sRNAs) represent a largely unexplored route to social cheating during bacterial infection. Here we show that arcZ , encoding a conserved Hfq-dependent sRNA in the plant pathogen Dickeya solani , undergoes recurrent single-nucleotide mutations during potato tuber infection. Five distinct arcZ alleles define a graded series of ArcZ functional impairment in which antifungal and protease activities are progressively reduced while virulence is compromised only in a subset of alleles. All five variants gain a fitness advantage exclusively during coinfection with wild-type arcZ 1 cells. This advantage is strongest when variants are rare and declines as cheater frequency increases, ultimately correlating with reduced total bacterial productivity, the canonical signature of social cheating and a tragedy of the commons. No fitness benefit is detected in vitro . Transcriptomic profiling of five arcZ variants identifies a conserved core of 186 downregulated genes enriched in secreted and diffusible functions. Systematic genetic dissection, supported by quantitative proteomics, establishes BudAB-dependent limitation of tissue acidification as the dominant cooperative public good exploited during infection. Wild-type arcZ 1 cells divert pyruvate flux toward acetoin via the BudAB pathway, maintaining a less acidic tissue environment that sustains disease progression; arcZ variants, which show reduced expression of this pathway, benefit…

items.title: A trefoil knot mimic and multiple pore states define the mechanism of a split-shell Tc toxin
items.summary_raw: Toxin complex (Tc) toxins are among the largest virulence factors secreted by pathogenic bacteria, operating via a sophisticated injection mechanism that translocates cytotoxic effectors into host cells. While most structural and mechanistic studies have focused on fused-shell Tc toxins such as PTC3 from Photorhabdus luminescens , the structurally distinct split-shell toxins remain poorly understood. Here we report cryoelectron microscopy structures of the split-shell Yersinia entomophaga Tc holotoxin (YenTc) in multiple conformational states at resolutions of 2.6 to 3.7 Å. We show that the chitinase subunit YenChi2 is essential for shell expression and stabilizes the N terminus of the shell subunit YenA1 in the prepore state. Our structures also reveal the first trefoil knot mimic in Tc toxins, which serves the dual function of stabilizing the linker domain and holding the two halves of the split shell together. We further describe three distinct pore states: the conventional pore state, an inverted pore state in which the shell rotates 180° around a hinge in YenA2, and a lollipop pore state induced at alkaline pH in which the YenA1-YenChi2 subcomplex fully dissociates from the channel. Strikingly, all three pore states also manifest in the TcA pentamer of P. luminescens PTC3, indicating that they represent a general but previously undescribed feature of Tc toxin pore formation. Taken together, our results establish a mechanistic framework for split-shell Tc toxins and…

items.title: IFITM1-mediated restriction of henipavirus entry is associated with ephrinB2 reorganization and confinement in membrane nanodomains
items.summary_raw: Nipah (NiV) and Hendra (HeV) viruses are prototype henipaviruses (HNV) within the family of Paramyxoviridae . They are highly pathogenic zoonotic paramyxoviruses that cause fatal encephalitis in humans, with case fatality rates of 40 to 70%. These viruses use the receptor-binding protein (G) to engage host receptors ephrinB2 and/or ephrinB3, while the fusion protein (F) drives membrane fusion leading to virus entry and cell–cell fusion. Interferon-inducible transmembrane (IFITM) proteins restrict the infection of many unrelated viruses at virus entry. We show that the knockdown of IFITM1 enhances HNV entry and cell–cell fusion in both human epithelial and endothelial cells, while overexpression of IFITM1 inhibits both. Using single-molecule localization microscopy, we observed that IFITM1 forms nanoclusters on the plasma membrane that are enlarged upon interferon stimulation. IFITM1 clusters spatially co-occur with GM1-enriched, raft-like membrane domains. EphrinB2, a lipid raft resident, organizes into larger and denser clusters when associated with IFITM1, suggesting a preferential partitioning into membrane domains organized and/or influenced by IFITM1. Using single-particle tracking, we further show that lateral diffusion of ephrinB2 on the plasma membrane is confined in the presence of IFITM1. This confinement is not reversed by amphotericin B, nor is IFITM1-mediated NiV restriction. Our data show spatial reorganization and confinement of ephrinB2 within membrane…

items.title: A heavy molybdenum reservoir in Neoarchean seawater tracks extensive iron oxidation
items.summary_raw: The lead-up to the Great Oxidation Event (GOE; between 2.5 and 2.2 Ga) was arguably as consequential as the event itself, yet substantial uncertainties remain regarding the timing and magnitude of oxygen rise in early Earth’s oceans. Heavy molybdenum isotope compositions (δ 98 Mo) in Neoarchean marine sediments have traditionally been interpreted as evidence for adsorption of dissolved Mo onto iron oxyhydroxides [e.g., ferrihydrite; Fe(OH) 3 ] and manganese oxides (MnO 2 ) formed in oxygenated marine environments, implying at least regional surface oxygen accumulation immediately prior to the GOE. Here, we propose an alternate explanation in which these isotopic signatures arose in a largely anoxic ocean. Analyses of Neoarchean banded iron formations (BIFs) deposited at 2.57 to 2.51 Ga reveal a broad range of δ 98 Mo values, which are best explained by the combined effects of Mo adsorption onto primary ferrihydrite, followed by its diagenetic incorporation into Fe(II)-Mo(IV)-sulfides. After accounting for isotopic fractionation during adsorption, we estimate that Neoarchean seawater δ 98 Mo maintained a relatively stable composition between 1.5‰ and 1.6‰. A newly developed Mo isotope mass balance model further indicates that only a minor MnO 2 sink was required to generate these heavy δ 98 Mo values. Instead, the dominant control was likely removal of isotopically light Mo via adsorption to settling ferrihydrite particles in ferruginous seawater. Given the lack of oxygen…

items.title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals organizational properties of the mouse spinal cord and alterations in neuropathic pain
items.summary_raw: The spinal cord integrates diverse somatosensory inputs and executes motor outputs through anatomically and functionally distinct circuits. Here, we employed spatially resolved single-cell transcriptomic profiling of the adult mouse spinal cord to gain insights into the organizational logic of the spinal cord. Our results reveal distinct spatial and laminar distributions of neuronal subtypes, including axial level and sex-specific differences. Many neuronal subtypes exhibit lamina-specific somatic proximities, suggesting potential regionally specific connectivity. Additionally, neuronal subtypes within the dorsal horn exhibit a wide range of predicted cell-cell communication motifs, as assessed by the spatial distribution of neuropeptide- and other ligand-receptor pairs. Finally, we identified several neuronal subtypes with altered transcriptomic states and predicted cell–cell communications in a model of neuropathic pain. This spatially resolved cellular and molecular map of the spinal cord will facilitate the decoding of circuit mechanisms underlying somatosensory and motor functions in health and disease.

items.title: Extracellular vesicles presenting “don’t eat me” signal limit the efferocytic capacity in lung fibrosis
items.summary_raw: Efferocytosis is essential for tissue homeostasis and resolution of inflammation, yet its direct contribution to resolve organ fibrosis remains poorly understood. In idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, a progressive age-driven lung disease, we found profound suppression of efferocytosis coupled with robust production and release of extracellular vesicles presenting functional receptor CD47, a canonical “don’t eat me” mediator. Restoration of efferocytosis contributes to the natural resolution of fibrosis, which is accelerated by CD47 deficiency or alterations in macrophage metabolic responses. In turn, pharmacologic disruption of efferocytic receptors or signaling results in lung fibrosis development and its persistence. While sustained reduction of efferocytic capacity align with fibrosis persistence in aged mice, AMPK activation promotes fibrosis resolution via reducing inflammaging and CD47 bioavailability, thus restoring clearance of apoptotic fibroblast. Importantly, AMPK activation also reprograms macrophages engaging apoptotic fibroblasts toward a fibrosis pro-resolving phenotype by suppressing TGF-β1 and promoting secretion of pro-regenerative hepatocyte growth factor (HGF). Together, these findings link metabolism and immune efferocytic fitness in lung fibrosis resolution and suggest that an AMPK senomorphic pathway has broad therapeutic relevance for fibrotic diseases.

items.title: N-terminal integrity governs heptamer assembly and maturation in a mosquito innexin hemichannel
items.summary_raw: Nonchordate gap junction channels are formed by innexins, yet the structures and subunit assembly mechanisms of insect innexins remain unknown. We determined cryoelectron microscopy structures of AGAP001487, an innexin from the malaria mosquito Anopheles gambiae , reconstituted in lipid nanodiscs. The wild-type protein forms a rotationally symmetric heptameric hemichannel with an ordered N-terminal ring stabilized by intersubunit hydrogen bonds. Whereas deletion of a single N-terminal residue preserves channel activity, removal of two or more residues markedly impairs function. Consistent with these functional defects, the structure lacking two N-terminal residues exhibits disrupted rotational symmetry, extensive N-terminal disorder, pore collapse, and altered pore–lipid interactions. In addition, two-dimensional class averages revealed a minor population of hexameric particles, consistent with a potential assembly intermediate. Together, these structures support a stepwise assembly pathway in which intersubunit hydrogen bonding stabilizes N-terminal ring formation as a maturation step leading to a fully symmetric heptameric channel. Our findings identify N-terminal integrity as a critical determinant of oligomer maturation and channel function and provide mechanistic insight into how defined oligomeric assemblies are established in large-pore channel families.

items.title: The Cybertruck era is over, but America’s electric truck experiment isn’t
items.summary_raw: After barely three years on the road, Tesla is planning to kick the Cybertruck to the curb after flagging sales. Elon Musk announced on Friday that the company would wind down production next year to make room for the production of Cybercabs, the robot taxis Tesla hopes will reshape transportation. In its short lifespan, the Cybertruck managed to become a top candidate for the most polarizing vehicle on the road — ever. Critics called it a “ MAGA hat on wheels ” and compared it to a dumpster — a resemblance that may have fooled some hungry raccoons that once chewed on the vehicle’s rear vault . It’s already being declared “ one of the greatest flops in automotive history ,” on par with Ford’s 1957 Edsel. But the polygonal, supposedly bulletproof truck did appeal to a certain demographic. “It’s the kind of vehicle, as a kid, you imagine for the future,” said Dan Krassner, executive director of the American EV Jobs Alliance, an advocacy organization working to end the partisan divide over electric vehicles. He’s a Republican and a wrestling fan, and noted that some of his favorite pro wrestlers drove Cybertrucks, including the married WWE superstars Seth Rollins and Becky Lynch, along with The Miz and Liv Morgan (though the latter has said it was the “ worst investment ” she ever made). items.title: 2 years after Mexico relocated their climate-ravaged community, residents struggle to adapt
items.summary_raw: It’s 3 a.m. and the beach in El Bosque, in southeast Mexico, is humming with small talk and laughter as Viviana Velázquez eases out of her hammock and dashes to the shoreline to greet a boat returning with the night’s catch. Velázquez, 38, and her 13-year-old daughter, Marlene, help the tired fishermen unload the ice boxes and heave a plastic crate full of bonito to the cooperative to be weighed. The captain pays Velázquez for her help in fish. She saves a couple to fry for breakfast and cashes in the rest for 50 pesos, the equivalent of about $3, and heads back to her hammock, where some friends are eating pastries while catching up on the past week’s dramas. This work is known locally as garrulear . For decades it was an important source of income, food, and bonding for women in El Bosque, a small fishing community in the state of Tabasco located on a narrow peninsula sandwiched between the Gulf of Mexico and the Usumacinta River. It is one of the things that Velázquez misses most since sea level rise forced residents to leave. “In El Bosque I would garrulear every day, but then the sea took everything,” said Velázquez, as she settled back into a hammock. “Now I’m stuck inside most of the time; it’s too far to come here often.” El Bosque became the first community in Mexico to be recognized as displaced by climate change in 2023. By then, coastal erosion and flooding from storm surge had already damaged or swept away more than half of the hundred or so homes in the area…

items.title: A Delphi Study on Mapping Motivations and Barriers of Pakistan’s Digital Participation in Climate Activism
items.source_name: Lahore Institute for Research and Analysis Journal
items.summary_raw: This study examines the barriers and enablers of digital participation in climate advocacy in Pakistan, a country ranked among the most climate-vulnerable nations globally yet lagging in public engagement with climate action. The research applies the Delphi method within the framework of Actor-Network Theory (ANT) to explore how socio-cultural, technological, and structural factors shape digital activism in the context of climate change. Twenty-three experts from fields as diverse as climate advocacy, digital communication, sociology, and cultural studies were brought together in a three-round iterative process to reach consensus on the key barriers and strategies. The findings include major barriers such as low awareness, socio-economic priorities overshadowing environmental concerns, limited internet access, and algorithmic biases that reduce the visibility of climate content. Identified enablers are religious and cultural framing, localized storytelling, and influencer-led campaigns to mobilize diverse audiences. Non-human actors, such as algorithms on social media, were found to play a very critical role in shaping the effectiveness of digital advocacy networks. The research integrates insights from experts and offers actionable recommendations for enhancing digital climate engagement, including targeted policy interventions and culturally resonant advocacy strategies. This article contributes to the growing body of literature on digital activism in the Global South and…

items.title: Integrating Nigerian Indigenous Climate Indicators with Regional Climate Forecasts: Framework Development and Retrospective Evaluation
items.summary_raw: Regional climate models (RCMs) for West Africa exhibit systematic biases in boundary-layer processes and convective initiation, particularly during monsoon onset and cessation. This study develops and retrospectively evaluates a computational framework for encoding indigenous climate taxonomies from Nigeria's three major ethnolinguistic groups—Hausa, Yorùbá and Igbo—as structured metadata interoperable with numerical boundary-layer datasets, aiming to refine RCM performance and develop accessible climate-smart agricultural interfaces. The study employed a multiphase computational and mixed-methods design: a PRISMA 2020 systematic review to identify and document indigenous climate indicators; linguistic and computational encoding of these indicators as structured metadata; development of a four-layer hybrid architecture integrating boundary-layer data, taxonomy encoding, a fuzzy-logic and Random Forest fusion engine, and a multilingual agricultural interface; retrospective computational validation against ERA5 and CHIRPS data for three agro-ecological zones (Kano, Ibadan, Enugu) over 2010–2020; and stakeholder evaluation with 48 farmers.
