items.title: Justice and the Clean Energy Transition to 2080: Exploring Lessons from Jordan
items.summary_raw: Abstract Expanding clean energy does not settle the politics of transition. It leaves open who benefits, who bears the costs, and who can shape consequential decisions. In Jordan, renewable expansion unfolds amid energy import dependence, fiscal constraints, reliance on external finance, concentrated electricity governance, and severe water scarcity. This article systematically reviews 111 publications on Jordan’s energy and climate transition from 1988 to 2026, organizes them into six empirical pillars, and assesses distributive, procedural, and recognition justice using predefined evidence criteria. The synthesis identifies recurring barriers to benefiting from the transition, fragmented governance with uneven decision authority, the allocation of financial risks through market and contractual rules, and external dependence. Even where policies or technologies are formally available, income, housing, tenure, and location affect households’ ability to benefit. Participation does not necessarily confer equivalent influence, and external resources can expand transition capacity while shaping bargaining and policy choices. Water-energy interdependence is well documented, but its consequences for affected groups are less consistently assessed. Among the publications, 87 recommend policies or other measures, 52 report or evaluate measures or enabling conditions, and only 28 do both, limiting conclusions about which interventions work. Three propositions concerning distribution…

items.title: To What Extent Has Congestion Charging Contributed to Sustainable Urban Environmental Governance? Evidence from London and Stockholm
items.source_name: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
items.summary_raw: This paper examines the progress of congestion charging in promoting sustainable urban environmental governance in London and Stockholm. A comparative case study of traffic demand, environmental results, equity and acceptance, and long-term institutions. Both schemes reduced the amount of traffic entering the paid area significantly and permanently altered people's travel behaviour. A drop in demand did not result in a reduction of long-term congestion or air pollution because both were also influenced by capacity, growth, fleet structure, weather and traffic diversion. The schemes achieved stability through different paths: London was led by politics and administration; Stockholm was a trial run by the public and a referendum. Equity effects were determined by car dependence, alternatives and revenue utilisation. Congestion charging will thus have a relatively small and uneven effect. It is recommended that one of the first devices to be used for demand-fluctuation regulation is selected to reduce congestion and pollution.

items.title: Higher warming leads to a larger zero-emissions commitment
items.summary_raw: Nature Climate Change, Published online: 10 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02789-5 Scientific grounds for a net-zero policy assume near-zero committed warming over a few decades after CO2 emissions cease. A modelling study suggests that if prior peak temperatures rise above 2 °C before cessation of CO2 emissions, committed warming increases, making it harder to stabilize global warming.

items.title: Beyond ecological miscommunication: a system theory approach to climate litigation
items.summary_raw: The increasing number of lawsuits against European carbon majors has sparked interest among legal scholars. However, the literature has paid little attention to the sociological dimension of climate litigation. This paper makes two contributions. First, it develops a systems-theory Framework to analyse key social dynamics that emerge between social systems at stake in corporate climate litigation, including science, law, economics, politics, media, and organisations (NGOs). Second, this paper investigates the overlooked key role of NGOs in climate litigation. Findings from 16 qualitative semi-structured interviews with lawyers and members of NGOs involved in corporate climate litigation over loss and damage indicate that NGOs ease systemic buondaries for three reasons. First, NGO’s climate litigation campaings augment ecological irritation between social systems. Second, NGOs’ operational structures are coupled with a plurality of social systems’ codes, which bring different systems into collaboration. Third, climate litigation supported by NGOs requires the practice networking among different NGOs and expert affine to diffferent social systems. The increase in resonance, coupling- and network-oriented characters of NGOs’ climate litigation campaigns redefines Luhmann’s key conceptual tools, such as structural coupling, the relationship system-environment (ecological communication), as well as his description of organisation as a forum of interdependence interruption (…

items.title: A further acceleration of clean energy is needed for global CO2 emissions to peak and decline
items.summary_raw: Abstract Global fossil fuel CO 2 emissions have grown 0.8% per year on average between 2019 and 2025. Here we project a decrease of 0.4% in 2026, probably as a short-term response to the energy shock triggered by the Iran conflict. Electric vehicles and solar and wind power offset about 64–79% of increasing emissions from demand growth through 2028; acceleration in clean technology deployment is needed to guarantee emissions peak and subsequent decline.

items.title: Coal power lives longer next to data centres
items.summary_raw: Nature Climate Change, Published online: 10 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02769-9 Data centres are among the world’s fastest growing electricity consumers. An analysis of more than 9,000 facilities worldwide links the artificial intelligence-era expansion of data centres to delayed coal plant retirements and around 2 Gt of additional carbon dioxide emissions.

items.title: Exploring marine conservation futures to inform systematic conservation planning
items.summary_raw: Marine conservation must advance towards global biodiversity targets despite significant climatic and geopolitical uncertainties. We present an expert-informed scenario framework to support systematic conservation planning in marine environments in the face of such unpredictable conditions. Through a six-step process involving an expert workshop and a survey of 85 respondents, climate change and international politics, governance and legislation were identified as the most relevant and uncertain drivers of marine conservation futures amongst the fourteen drivers considered. Their contrasting states were combined into four qualitative scenarios, ranging from effective climate mitigation and international cooperation to inadequate climate action and geopolitical conflict. We propose ways to translate these scenario narratives into conservation planning options by linking them to spatial decision-support tools and analytical workflows, considering biodiversity distributions, ecological connections amongst areas, climate risks, socio-economic costs and other effective area-based conservation measures. Two proposed analytical approaches illustrate how these considerations could be combined under different scenarios about the future. The resulting conservation priorities would provide information for ecosystem-based marine spatial planning by identifying biodiversity objectives and spatial requirements for consideration alongside other marine uses. The proposed framework provides…

items.title: Ideology through Trade Policy: Corpus- Assisted CDA of Biden's Discourse
items.summary_raw: This paper examines the discursive construction of U.S. trade policy during Biden administration by applying corpus assisted tools with Critical Discourse analysis (CDA) approach. This study analyses the official document of United States Trade Representative (USTR) and President's trade policy agenda. For methodological considerations, the study adopts a mixed methods explanatory sequential design in which the quantitative corpus data are accumulated and analyzed first by AntConcsofware, then followed with qualitative analysis for deeper understanding to the quantitative results. Because of the limitation of scholarly attention to provide sufficient understanding for the ideological constructions in American trade policy, this study is directed by the following research questions: what lexical patterns describe Biden's trade policies in USTR? How the framings of trade policies are justified? whatare the key ideologies identifiedfrom the qualitative analysis and guidedby corpus results?. The qualitative CDA analysis is drawn on eclectic model of van Dijk's (1998) ideological square, Reisigl and Wodak' (2009) Discourse Historical Approach (DHA) argumentative topoi, and Entman's (1993) framing model. The study reveals that American trade policy during Biden administration is constructed with the ideologies of trade liberalism, moderate protectionism, competitive authoritarianism, interconnected institutionalism, and inclusivism. These ideological representations are reflected…

items.title: Does Digital Technology Enhance New Quality Agricultural Productivity? A Quantitative Meta‐Analysis
items.summary_raw: ABSTRACT This study employs meta‐analysis to assess the effect of digital technology on new quality agricultural productivity, defined as a systemic construct driven by technological innovation and factor reallocation and encompassing output, efficiency, and green performance. Based on 853 estimates from 48 studies, all effect sizes are converted into partial correlation coefficients. The results show a small positive average effect that remains robust across publication‐bias and sensitivity tests. The positive effect does not vary significantly across digital technology types, productivity measures, transmission mechanisms, region, or analytical scales, but is influenced by climate and environmental risks, temporal contexts, and econometric methods. Climate risk significantly strengthens the contribution of digital technology, particularly in the 2010s, whereas this effect was relatively weak in the 1990s. No significant differences emerge across technology types under climate risk, suggesting that coordinated digital systems may enhance agricultural climate resilience more effectively than individual technologies. This study integrates fragmented microlevel, regional, and cross‐country evidence within a comparable framework, distinguishes average from conditional effects, and incorporates climate risk into research on new quality agricultural productivity.

items.title: Green Innovation and Environmental Policy Stringency: Heterogeneous Drivers of Sustainable Energy Transition in OECD Countries
items.summary_raw: Achieving Sustainable Development Goal 7 (SDG-7) requires not only technological progress but also effective environmental regulation. Although previous studies have examined green innovation and environmental policy separately, less is known about how these two drivers are jointly associated with different dimensions and stages of sustainable energy transition. This study investigates the heterogeneous relationships of green innovation, proxied by public support for R&D in low-carbon energy technologies, and environmental policy stringency (EPS) with sustainable energy transition, across 27 OECD countries during 2002–2020. Sustainable energy transition is captured through three dimensions of SDG-7: electricity access, renewable energy deployment, and energy efficiency. The empirical strategy combines conventional panel estimators, GMM robustness estimates, and panel quantile regression, allowing both average relationships and heterogeneity across the conditional distributions of the SDG-7 outcomes to be examined. The results show that electricity access is already near-universal across the OECD sample, whereas substantial cross-country differences remain in renewable energy deployment and energy intensity. Baseline estimates indicate that the green innovation proxy is positively associated with renewable energy use and energy intensity, whereas higher EPS is associated with greater renewable energy use and lower energy intensity. The quantile estimates reveal substantial…

items.title: System-level impacts of landscape scenicness on onshore wind deployment in a decarbonized European energy system
items.summary_raw: Abstract Onshore wind is pivotal to Europe’s decarbonization, yet its expansion increasingly faces social constraints due to landscape impacts that are rarely captured in energy system models. This study presents a Europe-wide integration of landscape scenicness, which is used as a proxy for potential landscape impact, into a calibrated, multi-sector energy system model that explores policy interactions with enhanced capacity-factor granularity. Building on a machine-learning–based scenicness dataset linked to wind resource assessment, and an enhanced representation of wind technologies with fine capacity-factor granularity, we quantify how landscape scenicness preservation affects onshore wind deployment and system-wide outcomes across 27 European Union member states. Results show that moderate scenicness protection has limited impacts, while stringent protection disproportionately removes high-capacity-factor wind sites, particularly in mountainous and coastal regions. This reduces the number of potential low-cost wind sites and induces techno-economic substitution toward solar photovoltaics in the model. A reduction in onshore wind capacity intensifies competition among uses of clean electricity, including direct electrification, hydrogen, and other renewable synthetic fuels. The presence or relaxation of intermediate EU climate and energy policy targets has a stronger effect than scenicness constraints alone. These findings demonstrate that coordinated policy design…

items.title: Low-carbon city pilot policy, carbon emission reduction effect of agricultural inputs, and transmission pathways: evidence from a quasi-natural experiment at the prefecture level in China based on multi-period DID
items.summary_raw: Introduction Low-carbon city pilot policies constitute an important institutional practice for advancing the green and low-carbon transition of agriculture and achieving the “Dual-Carbon” goals. Scientific assessment of the agricultural emission-reduction effects of this policy is critical for land and food security. Methods Based on prefecture-level panel data of China spanning 2005–2024, this paper adopts a multi-period staggered Difference-in-Differences (DID) model to systematically examine the impacts of low-carbon city pilot policies on carbon emissions associated with agricultural inputs, and provides associational evidence on the transmission mechanisms. Given that the conventional two-way fixed-effect multi-period DID may yield potential bias under strong heterogeneity, this study further employs the Callaway-Sant’Anna staggered DID (CS-DID) to estimate the dynamic treatment effects for different cohorts. Multiple robustness strategies including PSM and placebo tests are also applied to validate regression results and improve the credibility of causal inference. Results The study finds that low-carbon city pilot policies significantly reduce regional Agricultural input-related carbon emissions mainly through three pathways: optimizing agricultural factor allocation, forcing the low-carbon transformation of agricultural industrial structure, and improving agricultural energy-use efficiency. Heterogeneity exists in policy effects: western cities achieve the strongest…

items.title: The Children's Climate Vulnerability Index: An Integrated Approach to Assessing Climate Risk—Evidence From India
items.summary_raw: ABSTRACT Children are particularly vulnerable to climate‐related risks due to their biological sensitivity, their dependence on societal systems, and their limited ability to adapt to the stressors posed by the environment. This study assesses the climate risk and the resulting vulnerability of children at the state level in India with the Children's Climate Vulnerability Index (CCVI). Drawing on the IPCC vulnerability framework, the index combines measures of household‐reported and perceived climatic and environmental exposure, child‐specific sensitivity, and adaptive capacity. The CCVI is applied to four Indian states—Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Himachal Pradesh, and Uttarakhand—that represent different climatic regimes and socioeconomic contexts. Results show substantial variation in children's climate vulnerability despite similar levels of exposure; sensitivity is the main driver of vulnerability in all states. Health, nutrition, and education‐related sensitivities consistently outweigh the impact of climatic hazards, while adaptive capacity has limited power to offset these pressures. By linking vulnerability patterns to child development outcomes, the study shows that children's climate risk is shaped more by developmental and institutional conditions than by hazard intensity alone. The findings underscore the need for child‐focused, multi‐sectoral adaptation strategies that combine action with health, nutrition, education, and social protection policies.

items.title: Climate distress at a moral crossroads: how solastalgia conditions divergent consumer responses
items.summary_raw: Introduction Climate-related distress can support responsible consumption or coincide with affect-driven escape, yet the moral processes underlying these divergent responses remain unclear. This study develops and tests a dual-route framework in which moral disengagement (MD) and moral obligation (MO) link climate-change anxiety (CCA) and eco-grief (EG) with affective impulsive buying (AIB) and eco-conscious behavior (ECB), while solastalgia (BS) conditions key emotion-to-moral-processing associations. Methods An explanatory sequential mixed-methods design combined a cross-sectional survey of 582 adult consumers in Türkiye with semi-structured interviews conducted approximately 1 month later with 26 participants. Survey data were analyzed using PLS-SEM, and interview data were examined through codebook thematic analysis. Results CCA was positively associated with MD and MO, whereas EG was positively associated with MO and negatively associated with MD. MD was positively associated with AIB, while MO was positively associated with ECB. The corresponding indirect associations were significant. BS strengthened the CCA–MD association and weakened the EG–MO association, with significant moderated indirect associations in the expected directions. The qualitative findings clarified these relationships through patterns of rationalization, perceived agency, reparative action, affective consumption, and place-based stewardship. Discussion The findings challenge accounts that assign…

items.title: Reading the Currents: Deconstructing Messages and Meanings of Water in Informational Picturebooks
Policy bundling and the political economy of climate policymaking
items.summary_raw: Climate action has been stymied by a challenging political economy: climate policies can impose salient, short-term costs in exchange for uncertain, long-term benefits. Public support for many climate policies has, as a result, remained uneven. We use conjoint experiments in 10 of the world’s largest carbon-emitting countries to investigate the effects of policy bundling – linking one contentious policy to other programs – on public support for climate action. We find remarkable consistency across diverse political and economic contexts: linking climate policy to some progressive economic and social programs expands coalitions of support, notably without reducing support on the political right. Achieving the Paris Climate Agreement’s goals will require every country to navigate contentious domestic climate policy conflicts; we find that policy bundling offers a broadly applicable strategy for strengthening public coalitions in favor of a contentious policy.

items.title: Early evidence links data centre exposure to coal power retirement timelines
items.summary_raw: Nature Climate Change, Published online: 10 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02794-8 Data centre expansion may slow the coal-fired power plants phase-out, complicating decarbonization pathways. This study finds that coal units exposed to post-2020 data centres have lower retirement risks and their potential lifetime extensions could cause large additional CO2 emissions.

items.title: Strategic Opportunities and Key Challenges for China's Marine Energy Resource Development under the Framework of the 15th Five‑Year Plan
items.summary_raw: The 15th Five‑Year Plan period represents a critical window for China's transition from a maritime nation to a maritime power. This paper, guided by the outline of the 15th Five‑Year Plan and related policy documents, employs a combination of policy text analysis and industrial empirical analysis to systematically explore pathways and strategies for the efficient development and utilization of marine energy resources. The study finds that the 15th Five‑Year Plan provides a clear top‑level design for marine energy development, with three major strategic opportunities emerging: the "100‑million‑kilowatt" target for deep‑water offshore wind drives leapfrog industrial growth, with China's exploitable deep‑water wind resources exceeding 1.2 billion kilowatts and key technologies such as floating wind turbines having achieved major breakthroughs; deep‑water oil and gas have become the core replacement area for reserve and production increases, with the South China Sea containing 35 billion tons of oil and gas resources, and China having systematically mastered the full suite of exploration and development technologies in the deep‑water domain; the large‑scale utilization of marine energy opens a new track, aiming for an installed capacity of 400,000 kilowatts by 2030, with overall levels entering the world's first tier. At the same time, challenges cannot be ignored: deep‑water technologies and equipment face "bottleneck" risks, with high dependence on foreign core components…

items.title: NGO Inc or Guardians of the Just Transition? Navigating Diverging Narratives on Civil Society in EU Corporate Sustainability Negotiations
items.summary_raw: This article examines how civil society organisations are framed and regulated in recent EU corporate sustainability regulation, with a particular focus on the 2025 Omnibus I proposals. By investigating the Omnibus I proposals, the article finds two opposing framings of NGOs: on the one hand, an individualising tendency that views civil society actors as representing their own specific interests and on the other hand a collectivising tendency where civil society is seen as representing public interest and the environment at large. These opposing framings are part of a broader tendency across EU regulatory instruments relevant for civil society actors, which the article evidences through an analysis of the EU Civil Society Strategy and the Multiannual Financial Framework. Finally, the article identifies future research opportunities to analyse potential implications of these framings for EU corporate sustainability governance: a lack of coherence, a more fragmented corporate sustainability legal landscape characterised by normative ambiguity, and a changing understanding of public and private governance in EU corporate sustainability frameworks.

items.title: Comparative Life Cycle Assessment of Spodumene Processing Routes for Battery Grade Lithium Hydroxide Production in Australia, China and Finland
items.summary_raw: Abstract The increasing demand for lithium-ion batteries has intensified the need for sustainable and resilient supply chains for battery-grade lithium hydroxide monohydrate (LHM). This study presents a cradle-to-gate Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) of three hard-rock spodumene-based LHM supply routes: the conventional Australian–Chinese route (BASE), integrated Australian production (I-AUS), and integrated European production in Finland (I-FIN). The functional unit is 1 kg of battery-grade LiOH·H₂O at the refinery gate. Fifteen environmental impact categories were assessed, with emphasis on acidification, eutrophication, global warming, land use, freshwater consumption, and cumulative energy demand. I-FIN exhibits the lowest impacts across all categories, with a Global Warming Potential (GWP) of 10.21 kg CO₂-eq/FU, 22% and 34% lower than I-AUS and BASE, respectively. Compared with BASE, I-FIN reduces Freshwater Consumption (FWC) and Cumulative Energy Demand (CED) by 38% and 37%, respectively. Conversion/refining is the main environmental hotspot, contributing approximately 40–45% across most categories. Monte Carlo analysis indicates low uncertainty. Sensitivity analysis identifies ore grade, beneficiation recovery, and thermal-energy supply as key parameters, with lower-carbon thermal energy reducing GWP by up to 16%. Overall, integrated regional production, efficient beneficiation, soda-leaching conversion, and low-carbon energy can substantially improve the environmental…

items.title: Integrating TPB and UTAUT to explain renewable energy adoption intentions in rural Terengganu, Malaysia: The role of facilitating conditions and policy awareness
items.summary_raw: The transition to renewable energy technologies (RETs) is essential for achieving Malaysia’s sustainable development and carbon-reduction goals. Despite various national initiatives, adoption rates in rural communities remain modest. This study develops and empirically tests an integrated behavioural framework that combines the Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB) and the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) to explain intentions to adopt renewable energy in rural Terengganu, Malaysia. A structured questionnaire survey was administered to 200 rural household decision-makers across the Kemaman and Dungun districts. Data were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) with 5,000 bootstrapping resamples. The structural model explains 54.8% of the variance in intention (R2 = 0.548), demonstrating moderate explanatory power, with satisfactory in-sample predictive relevance (Q2 = 0.443) and acceptable model fit (SRMR = 0.061). Perceived Facilitating Conditions (β = 0.357, p < 0.001) and Perceived Behavioural Control (β= 0.284, p < 0.001) emerged as the primary direct predictors of adoption intention, with Perceived Facilitating Conditions demonstrating the largest direct effect (β = 0.357, p < 0.001) and the largest effect size (f² = 0.138), classified as a small effect. Subjective Norms (β = 0.155, p = 0.004) and Awareness of National Energy Policy (β = 0.111, p < 0.001) also significantly influenced adoption intention, while…

items.title: Estimation of carbon dioxide emissions using liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) in some Libyan cities as an alternative fuel
items.summary_raw: قيّمت هذه الدراسة استخدام غاز البترول المسال كوقود بديل للبنزين في قطاع النقل، مع التركيز على الجوانب البيئية والاقتصادية وإمكانية تطبيقه في بعض المدن الليبية. يُعتبر غاز البترول المسال وقودًا أنظف نسبيًا، إذ يتميز بانخفاض انبعاثاته من الغازات الضارة مقارنةً بالبنزين. تضمن الجانب العملي للدراسة مقارنة انبعاثات ثاني أكسيد الكربون الناتجة عن استخدام البنزين وغاز البترول المسال في عدد من المدن الليبية ذات الكثافة المرورية العالية، وهي: طرابلس، بنغازي، مصراتة، الزاوية، سبها، الخمس، وطبرق. حُسبت الانبعاثات بافتراض أن كل مركبة تقطع 100 كيلومتر يوميًا، وذلك بمقارنة استهلاك البنزين وغاز البترول المسال والانبعاثات الناتجة عن كل منهما. أظهرت النتائج أن استخدام غاز البترول المسال يُقلل انبعاثات ثاني أكسيد الكربون بنسبة 22% تقريبًا مقارنةً بالبنزين، حيث انخفضت الانبعاثات من حوالي 15.525 كيلوغرامًا من ثاني أكسيد الكربون إلى 12.1 كيلوغرامًا لكل 100 كيلومتر لكل مركبة. أشارت الدراسة أيضاً إلى أن التحول الجزئي لما يصل إلى 25% من أسطول المركبات يمكن أن يحقق انخفاضاً ملحوظاً في الانبعاثات داخل المدن الليبية. وخلصت الدراسة إلى أن غاز البترول المسال يمثل خياراً عملياً وتدريجياً للحد من التلوث البيئي وخفض استهلاك الوقود التقليدي في ليبيا، لا سيما في ظل وفرة موارد النفط والغاز المحلية.

items.title: Spatial Spillover Effects of Supply Chain Digitalization on Synergies between Pollution Reduction and Carbon Mitigation: Evidence from China
items.summary_raw: Promoting synergistic governance of pollution reduction and carbon mitigation (PRCM) constitutes a core task for China’s green transformation. As a major digital‑driven initiative, the supply‑chain digitization pilot policy (SCD) holds promise for advancing environmental governance, yet its spatial spillover effects on PRCM remain under‑explored. Using panel data of 237 Chinese cities from 2011 to 2023, this study measures urban PRCM performance and adopts a spatial Durbin model (SDM) to explore SCD’s direct and indirect impacts on PRCM, considering geographic and economic-geographic proximity. The results show PRCM has significant positive spatial autocorrelation; SCD significantly improves local PRCM and exerts positive spatial spillovers to neighboring cities under the economic-geography weight matrix; its promotion effect is most obvious in eastern and western cities, with significant spillovers across regions under the economic-geography matrix. These findings provide insights for cross-regional collaborative environmental governance in the digital era.

items.title: A Child Changes More Than Diapers: Does Parenthood Reshape Trust in Local Government Officials?
items.summary_raw: ABSTRACT Becoming a parent changes household priorities, time horizons and exposure to public institutions, but its consequences for political trust remain uncertain. Using a staggered difference‐in‐differences design, this study finds that first childbirth is followed by higher trust in local government officials. Event‐study tests find no evidence of differential pre‐trends, and the result remain stable in robustness tests such as alternative clustering, a stacked DID estimator, pregnancy‐based treatment timing, placebo tests and controls for province‐specific shocks and trends. The increase is smaller among respondents who perceive more serious integrity or social‐security problems, larger among men and stronger when the child has health insurance or other family members report high trust. The gender pattern is consistent with evidence that first childbirth reduces women's, but not men's, employment probability. These findings highlight parenthood as a consequential life‐course event for institutional attitudes and show that the associated change in political trust varies with the perceived quality and visibility of public support.

items.title: Utilization of Nuclear Technology in Supply Chains: A Review of the Literature
items.summary_raw: Background. Nuclear technology has strategic potential to enhance the safety, quality, traceability, and resilience of modern supply chains. However, existing studies remain fragmented across industrial sectors, highlighting the need for an integrative synthesis of its contributions to supply chain management. Aims. This study aims to identify, classify, and analyze nuclear technology applications across supply chain activities, focusing on their potential benefits, implementation challenges, and relevance to Indonesia. Methods. We conducted a narrative literature review using a targeted literature search and thematic synthesis of scientific publications and reports from national and international institutions published between 2014 and 2025. Result. The findings identify six major application domains: (1) food irradiation to improve food safety and extend product shelf life; (2) isotope analysis for product traceability and authenticity verification; (3) radioisotope tracers for industrial process monitoring and energy supply chains; (4) non-destructive testing to maintain logistics infrastructure integrity; (5) radiation sterilization in pharmaceutical and healthcare supply chains; and (6) radiation detection technologies to strengthen international trade security. The synthesis indicates that these applications can potentially support quality assurance, risk mitigation, and operational reliability. Nevertheless, implementation remains constrained by investment costs…

items.title: Research on Social Justice Issues and Governance Paths in Urban Climate Resilience Construction
items.source_name: International Journal of Education and Social Development
items.summary_raw: With a focus on the social equity issues in the construction of urban climate resilience, this paper employs the analytical system of environmental justice and climate equity, draws upon domestic and foreign experiences in urban climate adaptation, and identifies the main problems in social equity at the core of resilience construction. Research has found that the inequity is manifested in five ways: spatial clustering of vulnerable groups and a mismatch in resilience resources; concealment of fairness issues through technical governance paths; lack of voice for disadvantaged groups in community participation; deficit in fairness of adaptation fund allocation; and neglect of fairness dimensions in governance system design. The five types of problems are not independent; rather, they are linked together and work in concert to produce an institutional reproduction of vulnerability. Based on the above analysis, the following paths have been proposed: differentiation of resilience planning, participation-based governance mechanism, fairness-oriented fund allocation system, decision-making framework with fairness assessment, and multi-party collaborative governance network. Transferring the concept of social equity from a secondary consideration to an essential component of resilience-building is necessary to address the conflict between efficiency and fairness in urban climate governance.

items.title: Assessing the Role of Agroforestry in Mitigating Climate Change and Enhancing Food Security in Nigeria
items.source_name: IIARD INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF GEOGRAPHY AND ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT
items.summary_raw: Climate change poses significant challenges to agriculture in Nigeria, threatening food security and livelihoods. This research assesses the role of agroforestry in mitigating climate change impacts and enhancing food security in Nigeria. Through a systematic literature review and analysis of case studies, the study explores the diverse applications and benefits of agroforestry practices across different agroecological zones in Nigeria. Findings reveal that agroforestry systems offer sustainable solutions by sequestering carbon, reducing greenhouse gas emissions, and improving soil fertility. Case studies illustrate successful agroforestry initiatives, including alley cropping, agro-silvopastoral systems, home gardens, and agroforestry parklands, showcasing enhanced agricultural productivity, resilience, and food security. Recommendations are provided to promote the adoption of agroforestry practices, including policy support, capacity building, research, community engagement, partnerships, monitoring, and scaling up successful models. Implementing these recommendations can harness the potential of agroforestry to address climate change and food insecurity, fostering sustainable agricultural development in Nigeria.

items.title: Bridging technology and justice: reconsidering reverse osmosis for just and sustainable water systems in coastal Bangladesh
items.summary_raw: Salinity intrusion in coastal Bangladesh has reduced the reliability of conventional drinking-water sources and encouraged the expansion of reverse osmosis (RO) systems. We examine RO here not simply as a desalination infrastructure but as a socio-technical water service whose outcomes depend on access, governance, energy, infrastructure, and environmental management. Direct non-participant field observations were undertaken in April-May 2025 and March-April 2026 across Khulna, Satkhira, and Bagerhat, which were documented through location-specific photographs and the researcher’s personal retrospective memories arranged around access and affordability, functionality and maintenance, gendered challenges, energy resilience, and environmental risks. These observations are interpreted through water-justice and socio-technical transitions perspectives. Justice is operationalized as distributive justice (who receives benefits and bears costs), procedural justice (who participates in decisions and accountability), and recognition justice (whether differentiated needs are acknowledged). The evidence shows that RO can provide valuable potable water, but benefits are constrained by distance and user costs, seasonal shifts between rainwater and RO, weak lifecycle maintenance, private or project-dependent management, grid-electricity vulnerability, and poorly governed concentrate disposal. A Justice-Centred Climate-Resilient Desalination Framework (JCCRDF) has been proposed that links…

items.title: Framing and Sentiment Shifts in Indonesian Online News Coverage of Forest and Land Fires 2025-2026
items.summary_raw: Background Forest and land fires (karhutla) are a recurring annual ecological crisis in Indonesia that consistently attracts mass media attention, yet how media construct the causes of and responsibility for such events can shift over time. This study analyzes shifts in framing and sentiment of forest and land fire coverage in Indonesian online media between 2025 and 2026, and identifies patterns of geographic distribution and the most frequently quoted actors in each period. Method This study uses dictionary-based content analysis on 19,343 online news articles (9,502 from 2025; 9,841 from January–August 2026) drawn from a media monitoring database, after removing duplicates and articles found on audit to be unrelated to the topic. Articles were classified into six frames adapted from Entman’s model, and differences between years were tested using chi-square and Cramer’s V. Results Framing shifted significantly (chi-square = 400.29; df = 6; p < .001; Cramer’s V = 0.144). Solutions/mitigation was the dominant frame in both years but declined from 52.0% to 47.7%, while natural disaster/climate rose from 24.9% to 32.7%. Corporate negligence declined from 4.9% to 2.4%, and the already-marginal governance failure frame declined further to 0.4%. Health/humanitarian impact rose from 5.1% to 8.7%. Sentiment also shifted more negative (23.2% to 27.4%; chi-square = 57.36; df = 2; p < .001). Coverage intensity declined in East Kalimantan (−25.8%) and North Kalimantan (−36.6%), and…

items.title: Sub-ice thermal gradients strongly influence winter depth use of an iconic cold-water fish
items.summary_raw: In a thermally stratified lake, freshwater fish select habitats that align with their thermal preferences. While most studies of dimictic lakes have focused on habitat selection during summer stratification, less attention has been given to winter when inverse thermal stratification occurs with water temperatures between 0 to 4 °C. Our results show that winter thermal stratifications vary considerably among lakes. Much of the variation in winter depth use by the cold-water predator, Lake Trout ( Salvelinus namaycush ), can be explained by the depth of the 2 °C isotherm. Selection ratios further support preferential use of this thermal boundary after accounting for habitat availability. Larger, shallower, and windier lakes tend to exhibit colder mean temperatures near 0 °C and deeper isotherms, typically within the 1 to 2 °C range. In contrast, deeper or more sheltered lakes maintained warmer temperatures close to 4 °C and a shallower 2 °C isotherm. Using multiyear acoustic telemetry of Lake Trout from 11 different lakes, we found that in warmer lakes with depth-averaged temperatures above 2 °C, Lake Trout used thermal habitat averaging 2.6 ± 0.6 °C, which occurred in relatively shallow depths (0.1 to 11.3 m). In contrast, in the one large, shallow lake studied, where maximum water temperatures were below 2 °C, Lake Trout occupied the deepest waters during winter (16.8 to 26.4 m) and experienced average temperatures of 1.5 ± 0.4 °C. Applying our model to 877,927 Canadian and…

items.title: A signal convention in natural chimpanzee communication
items.summary_raw: Human language relies on conventional signals that are arbitrary, stable, and socially transmitted. Whether other animals exhibit meaning-based communicative conventions is virtually unknown. Using a quasi-experimental design, we investigated this in chimpanzee unvoiced calls (UCs), such as acoustic raspberries, known to show usage variation. We collected audio and contextual data in 91 chimpanzees (0 to 55 y), across eight wild and captive groups that differed in the presence or absence of adult role models. Communities with role models emitted UCs in one dominant context, which remained stable over years and from first utterances in development (1 to 2 y old). In contrast, groups without role models displayed highly variable, unstable UC usage across contexts and years. This contextual variation could not be explained by age or by a shared emotional valence, and individuals could use different UC forms within the same context, suggesting a decoupling between the signal form and usage. Together, these findings provide evidence that chimpanzee UCs meet key criteria for a signal convention: arbitrary signal–usage mappings, social transmission, and stability within communities. These findings demonstrate that conventionalized communication is not a uniquely human feature but can also emerge through social learning mechanisms in other animals’ natural communication.

items.title: Host and anatomical filters prevent microbiome convergence in avian scavengers
items.summary_raw: How host-associated microbiomes assemble under intense environmental microbial exposure remains a central question in microbial ecology. Vultures represent a unique natural system because these species differ markedly in feeding ecology and carcass use. We characterized bacterial communities across four anatomical niches (facial, buccal, tracheal, and cloacal) in 155 individuals spanning all four European obligate vulture species (subfamily Gypaetinae: Gypaetus barbatus, Neophron percnopterus, and Aegypiinae: Aegypius monachus and Gyps fulvus ) and the facultative scavenger Milvus milvus . Microbiome composition was jointly structured by host species and anatomical niche, with host identity explaining more variation than anatomical compartment and a significant interaction indicating that interspecific differentiation depended on body site. Each niche supported distinct bacterial assemblages and core microbiomes: Cloacal communities were enriched in anaerobic gut-associated taxa, whereas facial and tracheal communities contained more environmental and respiratory-associated bacteria. Host-specific taxonomic signatures persisted within anatomical niches despite recurrent exposure to the same carrion-associated microbial pool. Age further influenced community composition, whereas sex had little detectable effect. The facultative scavenger showed the same broad anatomical compartmentalization observed in obligate scavengers, although taxonomic signatures differed among species…

items.title: History-dependent droplet friction driven by contact-line aging
items.summary_raw: The motion of liquid droplets on solid surfaces is commonly described by contact-line friction, which is generally assumed to increase monotonically with instantaneous velocity. However, such a velocity-only description cannot explain why static droplet friction can exceed dynamic friction or why contact-line friction can become velocity-weakening. Here, we demonstrate that contact-line friction depends jointly on sliding velocity and contact history. Using self-assembled alkylsilane monolayers as molecularly tunable substrates and ionic liquids as low-volatility model liquids, we observe pronounced history-dependent strengthening of contact-line friction on solid-like monolayers, manifested as time-enhanced static friction and velocity-weakening dynamic friction. Both effects are progressively suppressed as the surface is tuned toward a more liquid-like state with a lower density of pinning defects, either by reducing the monolayer chain length or by increasing temperature. We attribute this behavior to nanoscopic contact-line aging, whereby contact-line segments thermally fluctuate and progressively occupy interfacial defects, leading to a progressive increase in contact-line pinning. An aging-based model quantitatively captures the history-dependent onset friction and the low-velocity friction dynamics in our system, while similar logarithmic strengthening across diverse liquid–substrate systems suggests broader applicability of the constitutive framework. These findings…

items.title: A Nasca-period perinatal burial reveals cyclopia associated with trisomy 13 in southern Peru
items.summary_raw: Cyclopia, is an extremely rare congenital condition resulting from severe disruption of early brain and facial development and is typically lethal before or shortly after birth. We examined two infants buried together in a Middle Nasca-period cemetery in Jauranga, southern Peru. One infant, JA13A, exhibited a single median orbit and other skeletal features diagnostic of cyclopia, whereas JA13B showed no comparable congenital variations. Ancient DNA revealed an extra copy of chromosome 13 in JA13A, identifying trisomy 13 as the likely cause. The two maternally unrelated individuals were interred together in a ceramic vessel, a mortuary treatment well documented for Nasca children. By integrating skeletal, genomic, and archaeological evidence, this case provides a view of a severe congenital condition and its mortuary treatment in a past society.

items.title: Belonging to a group with shared ideology leads preschool children to resist revising their beliefs despite disconfirming evidence
items.summary_raw: Shared beliefs can bring people together but may motivate prioritizing group affiliation over facts supported by evidence. Indeed, affiliation with a group whose membership is tied to shared beliefs (i.e., ideology-based groups) has led adults to endorse and maintain false beliefs. We demonstrate that this resistance to revise beliefs that form the basis of group membership has its origins in childhood. In three studies, 4- to 5-y-old children ( N = 192 ) endorse a claim about a novel causal system and subsequently join a group that shares their endorsement. Children randomly assigned to a focal Belief-contingent condition learn that their membership in the group is based on this claim, framed as a shared belief. We contrast this with conditions where group members hold the same shared belief, but this belief is not a condition for group membership (Experiments 1, 2, and 3), and where group members hold to the same claim framed as a “guess” (Experiment 2). After joining a group, children see evidence that their initial endorsement was incorrect and then have an opportunity to revise based on the new information. Only when group membership was contingent on the shared belief did children hold on to (and act on—Experiment 3) their initial incorrect endorsement. These findings suggest that the affiliative power of ideology has developmental roots; even in our earliest years, affiliative motives override truth-seeking and rationality. Thus, our early-emerging motive to identify…

items.title: A replaceable soma enables negative senescence in harvester ants
items.summary_raw: Most vertebrates and insects undergo senescence: as they age, their rate of mortality increases while reproduction declines. We present data from a 34-y study on 3,285 colonies of known age in the western harvester ant, Pogonomyrmex occidentalis, that show the reverse pattern, negative senescence, in which mortality decreases and reproduction increases with age. Theoretical models have identified indeterminate growth and a lack of reproductive cost to growth as the key traits favoring the evolution of negative senescence. Ant colonies continue to grow throughout their lifetime, leading to older colonies being larger on average. We found no evidence of a tradeoff between colony growth and reproduction: growth and reproduction were positively correlated, a synergism that may favor continued investment in growth. Harvester ants occupy a temporally variable environment that shapes investment in reproduction. At the population level, greater reproduction in 1 y does not lead to higher numbers of new colonies in the following year. Environmental unpredictability decouples reproduction from recruitment and selects for an extended reproductive lifespan, a trait that parallels changes in aging. We discuss the features that harvester ant colonies share with other organisms to identify functionally homologous mechanisms for avoiding senescence, as well as those traits that are specific to highly eusocial species.

Signaling mechanism of the transmembrane energy receptor Aer
items.summary_raw: The Escherichia coli aerotaxis receptor Aer is a bacterial chemoreceptor that senses intracellular redox changes via an N-terminal PAS domain bound to a flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD) cofactor. Distinct from canonical methyl-accepting chemotaxis proteins (MCPs) such as Tar/Tsr, Aer lacks a periplasmic ligand-binding domain and adaptive methylation, transmitting conformational signals laterally from the PAS domain to the HAMP domain and the methylation helix-like cap (MHL-cap) of the kinase control domain (KCD). To elucidate the Aer signaling mechanism, we determined cryoelectron microscopy structures of full-length Aer in oxidized flavin quinone (kinase-on) and reduced semiquinone (kinase-off) states. Structural comparison reveals redox-linked rearrangements of the FAD-binding pocket, reorientation of PAS–HAMP interactions, and strikingly altered MHL-cap stability. PAS–MHL-cap interactions in the oxidized state compress the receptor and stabilize the proximal KCD helices, whereas reduction disrupts these contacts, increasing KCD flexibility. To probe distal effects on KCD architecture, we performed nanodisc reconstitution and pulse dipolar ESR spectroscopy on spin-labeled positions along the four-helix bundle. Distance distributions indicate redox-dependent changes in helix separation, particularly at the C-terminal MHL2 region, consistent with PAS-driven loosening of KCD packing in kinase-off states. These data support a model in which FAD redox chemistry reorganizes…

items.title: The decision to stop “counting” explains numerical underproduction in primates
items.summary_raw: Sequential numerical production requires generating a target number of actions, but the mechanisms governing the termination of counting sequences are unclear. We trained two rhesus macaques to produce instructed numerosities by generating the corresponding number of actions in response to sign numerals or dot arrays. Although action sequences were controlled for temporal parameters, both monkeys performed accurately across both stimulus formats. However, their performance accuracy showed a systematic asymmetry: underproduction occurred more often than overproduction, contrary to predictions from perceptual numerosity judgments governed by Weber–Fechner scaling. This asymmetry was mirrored in reaction times, with longer latencies for underproduced sequences and shorter latencies for overproduced ones. A stochastic accumulation-to-bound model in which a decision variable evolves across counting steps and triggers termination when a threshold is reached can account for both accuracy and reaction-time patterns. These results provide evidence for a sequential stopping process that contributes to numerical production, relating counting behavior to general principles of decision formation.

items.title: Loss of DUSP2–RPA signaling enhances virtual memory T cell–mediated innate-like antiviral immunity
items.summary_raw: Virtual memory CD8 + T (T VM ) cells are antigen-inexperienced cells with rapid effector potential, but how their differentiation and antiviral activity are regulated remains unclear. Here, using an autoantibody-based screening strategy, we identify the phosphatase DUSP2 as a key regulator of T VM cell responses. Dual-specificity phosphatase 2 (DUSP2) deficiency enhances CD8 + T cell–dependent antiviral immunity and promotes the expansion of a highly activated CD44 super-high T VM subset. Upon viral challenge, these T VM cells respond rapidly without antigen recognition and display enhanced effector and cytokine programs, supporting an innate-like mode of antiviral immunity rather than conventional antigen-specific recall. Mechanistically, DUSP2 interacts with the replication protein A (RPA) complex to regulate RPA2 phosphorylation and chromatin association. Disruption of the DUSP2–RPA axis promotes R-loop accumulation and increases chromatin accessibility, which in turn activates Eomesodermin (EOMES)-associated transcriptional programs, eventually promoting T VM cell differentiation. T cell–specific deletion of RPA1 phenocopies these effects, leading to spontaneous T VM cell accumulation and rapid effector-like responses upon viral challenge. Together, our findings establish a DUSP2–RPA–R-loop axis that restrains T VM cell development and innate-like antiviral immunity.

items.title: Structural basis of hypervariable region 1 dynamics on HCV envelope glycoproteins in immune evasion
items.summary_raw: The hypervariable region 1 (HVR1) of the hepatitis C virus E1E2 glycoprotein plays a crucial role in immune evasion through rapid mutation and shielding of conserved neutralizing epitopes. Despite its important role, the structural properties of HVR1 remain poorly understood, particularly how its conformation influences shielding mechanisms and receptor recognition. To date in all published E1E2 or E2 structures, the C-terminal part of HVR1 (394 to 411) remains unresolved. Using neutralizing antibody (nAb) RM1-38, which targets C-terminal HVR1 (residues 399 to 409), we investigated the folding, positioning, flexibility, and shielding function of the RM1-38 epitope, or antigenic site 399 (AS399), on HVR1 by X-ray crystallography and negative-stain electron microscopy (nsEM). The crystal structure of RM1-38 Fab with the HVR1 AS399 peptide, combined with mutagenesis analysis, delineated the molecular basis of its strain-specific recognition and neutralization. nsEM and competition enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay revealed that HVR1 exhibits pronounced conformational flexibility even in the presence of other nAbs bound to E1E2. Virus neutralization assays using a combination of RM1-38 and broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) demonstrated antagonistic effects of RM1-38 with the bnAbs. Furthermore, RM1-38 reduced E1E2 binding to cells expressing the scavenger receptor SR-BI, an HVR1-dependent receptor, but did not affect binding to CD81 tetraspanin. Together, these findings…

items.title: Rapid vaterite-mediated shell repair for acid-induced damage in a deep-sea mussel
items.summary_raw: Mollusks are able to secrete and repair the most diverse and complex calcareous tissues in the animal kingdom, yet the detailed molecular mechanisms of these biomineralization processes, especially for the deep-sea calcifiers, remain to be elucidated. Here, using an in situ experiment, we report a repair mechanism for acid-induced shell damage via biologically mediated vaterite formation in the deep-sea cold-seep mussel Gigantidas haimaensis . Interestingly, the mussels secreted and recrystallized amorphous calcium carbonate into vaterite to seal the acid-induced dissolution porosities within 30 h. Calcium and nucleation substrates were potentially supplied by the mantle, including calcium-binding proteins and hydroxyapatite. Calcium then reacted with readily available carbonate in the extrapallial space, whose precipitation can be promoted by the nucleation substrates. This rapid repair mechanism is likely an advantage in the habitat of these mussels, which are characterized by pulsed acidification events from the seeping fluids. Furthermore, our finding expands our understanding of the diverse biomineralization mechanisms by which mollusks maintain their protective shells.

items.title: Generating interesting scientific ideas using knowledge graphs and LLMs: Evaluations with 100 research group leaders
items.summary_raw: The rapid growth of scientific literature makes it increasingly challenging for researchers to identify novel and impactful ideas, especially across disciplines. Modern AI systems offer new opportunities for scientific ideation, but how compelling are AI-generated ideas, and how can their quality be improved? Here, we introduce SCIMUSE , which generates personalized research ideas using a knowledge graph of 58 million papers and a large language model (LLM). A central focus of this work is to understand how interesting these ideas are. Therefore, we conducted a large-scale evaluation in which more than 100 research group leaders—spanning the natural sciences to the humanities—rated over 4,400 personalized ideas according to their level of interest. Overall, expert ratings were modest (mean 2.40 on a 5-point scale, most common rating 1), while 24.9% of ideas were rated 4 or 5. We find that supplying concept pairs selected using the knowledge graph does not improve expert-rated interest over a titles-only GPT baseline. High-citation-predicted pairs even showed a weak tendency (1.94 σ ) toward lower interest than random pairs. Nevertheless, graph features can be used to control properties of ideas, and, using this unique evaluation dataset, we show that idea interest can be predicted with both a supervised neural network based on graph features and a zero-shot ranking approach based on an LLM. Our work provides an AI methodology for generating scientific ideas and a large-scale…

items.title: Leaf hydraulic and photosynthetic traits mediate forest-scale resource use efficiencies across the continental United States
items.summary_raw: Temperate forests play a critical role in global carbon cycling and other ecosystem services, yet their resilience to climatic stresses remains uncertain. We combined physiology, community composition, flux data, and modeling to test a functional trait-based approach to predict forest ecosystem processes. For eight U.S. forests spanning broad precipitation and temperature gradients, we scaled up key leaf functional traits—maximum carboxylation velocity of Rubisco ( V c , m a x ), maximum leaf hydraulic conductance ( K l , m a x ), and turgor loss point (that is, wilting point, π t l p ) to predict gross primary productivity, light-use efficiency, standard and intrinsic water-use efficiency (WUE and iWUE), and their sensitivities to soil drought. In multiple regressions, ecosystem processes were strongly associated with community-weighted mean (CWM) trait values: enhanced productivity was linked with high V c , m a x ¯ , K l , m a x ¯ and π t l p ¯ , whereas high WUE and iWUE were linked with low K l , m a x ¯ and high π t l p ¯ . The CWM functional traits also influenced the sensitivity of ecosystem processes to soil moisture. A causal role of functional traits in driving ecosystem processes alongside climate was supported by parameterizing the LM4.1 vegetation model with CWM functional traits. This study highlights the important role of functional traits in determining forest responses to climate-driven water stress at a continental scale.

items.title: Millennial-scale variability in Greenland dust provenance during Dansgaard–Oeschger events of the last glacial period
items.summary_raw: Greenland ice-core records show an approximately 15-fold increase in dust concentration during cold stadial periods compared to warmer interstadial periods in the last glacial period (LGP). While multiple regions including East Asian deserts and the Sahara have been suggested as potential source areas (PSAs) for Greenland dust, millennial-scale variability of their relative contributions associated with Dansgaard–Oeschger climatic fluctuations during the LGP remains poorly constrained. To address this, we investigate high-resolution (~800 y) Pb and Sr isotopic, mineralogical, and geochemical records from the North Greenland Eemian Ice Drilling ice-core samples covering the entire LGP. We found that the Pb and Sr isotopic compositions, kaolinite-to-chlorite ratios, and chemical index of alteration values were higher during stadials than during interstadials. Comparison with PSAs suggests that East Asian deserts remained the dominant contributors to Greenland dust throughout the LGP, but contributions from the Sahara increased during stadial intervals. This shift likely reflects climate-driven changes in atmospheric circulation patterns responsible for transporting dust to Greenland. Our findings provide insights into the relationship between dust cycle dynamics and abrupt climate changes on millennial timescales during the LGP.

items.title: Realizing environmental benefits through the diffusion of smart farming innovations

Active and passive crowding pathways drive topological and mechanical divergence in myoblasts
items.summary_raw: Cell crowding is closely associated with many physiological processes, yet our understanding of crowded tissue organization has been developed largely in polygonal epithelia, leaving intrinsically anisotropic cell collectives comparatively poorly understood. Using C2C12 myoblasts, we investigate this problem by decoupling the final crowded state from the pathway taken to reach it, comparing active crowding, arising from cell proliferation during incubation, with passive crowding, imposed directly through high-density seeding. Unlike polygonal epithelia, crowded myoblast monolayers do not undergo epithelial-like kinetic arrest: cell motion is strongly suppressed, yet local rearrangements persist and packing remains structurally irregular. However, the two crowding pathways generate distinct collective states, differing in nematic order and junctional coupling. By contrasting these states, we reveal a close interplay among cell geometry, intercellular coupling, tissue-scale nematic order, and force transmission. This mechanical coordination ultimately shapes physiological function, preserving sensitivity to topographical cues and promoting efficient, spatially organized myogenic fusion. These findings broaden the physical framework of collective organization in active matter and establish key mechanical principles for in vitro tissue engineering.

items.title: Rare recovery of reassortants between contemporary clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 viruses and human influenza A viruses in vitro
items.summary_raw: Influenza A virus (IAV) pandemics can arise when animal-derived and human-adapted IAVs exchange genome segments; however, whether contemporary clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 viruses can generate viable reassortants with human IAVs is unclear. Here, we tested the reassortment potential of two clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 viruses with human-adapted H1N1 and H3N2 IAVs using a biosafe reassortment system. Across multiple coinfection conditions, we genotyped 2,698 plaque-purified viral clones and recovered 20 reassortants (0.74%). Polymerase assays identified human IAV subunits, particularly H1N1 PA or H3N2 PB2, that increased H5N1 polymerase activity. Thus, contemporary clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 viruses can reassort with human IAVs, but factors beyond polymerase compatibility may limit their recovery.

items.title: Targeting of STEAP3 by a selenium D–π–A photosensitizer that activates ferroptosis
items.summary_raw: Resistance to apoptosis limits the efficacy of many cancer therapies. Photodynamic therapy (PDT), with its spatial precision, offers a promising strategy by engaging nonapoptotic cell death pathways, such as ferroptosis. However, the direct molecular targets of most photosensitizers remain undefined. Here, we introduce a class of selenium-containing D–π–A photosensitizers (PDSe-1 to PDSe-11) and identify PDSe-8 as a lead system with advantageous photophysical properties and potent, hypoxia-tolerant phototoxicity (IC 50 = 53 nM). PDSe-8 elicits a concentration-dependent switching of cell death programs. Low doses trigger apoptosis through p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling, whereas higher doses activate ferroptosis. Competitive chemoproteomics reveals the metalloreductase STEAP3 as a direct molecular target of light-activated PDSe-8 underlying this switch. Upon photoirradiation, PDSe-8 photodegrades STEAP3 in glioblastoma cells, which in turn activates p53, impairs the SLC7A11–GPX4 antioxidant axis, and drives lethal lipid peroxidation, ultimately leading to ferroptotic cell death. This mode of action results in potent antitumor efficacy against U87MG glioblastoma both in vitro and in vivo. This work establishes STEAP3 as a key molecular target for photodynamic therapy and proposes a mechanistically defined selenium photosensitizer that overcomes cancer apoptosis resistance by inducing ferroptosis.

items.title: Coevolution of social network structure and life history in toothed whales
items.summary_raw: Toothed whales offer a 34 My-long natural experiment for the evolution of complex mammalian societies. However, quantitative comparative analyses of social structure in these species are lacking. Here, we draw on existing social network analyses to compare social structure across toothed whales. We consider published measures of two social network traits across all toothed whales: modularity ( Q ), which captures divisions or “cliques” in a social community, and social differentiation ( S ), which estimates how much whales vary in their relationships—whether they associate equally with others or form special bonds with specific individuals. Combining these with a recently published database of life history traits, we applied phylogenetic multilevel models with the objective of exploring the origins of social network structure. We identified 98 measures of modularity and 89 measures of social differentiation from 23 toothed whale species. Social network structure was more similar among closely related species (showing strong phylogenetic signal), despite substantial intraspecific variability. Toothed whales with longer lifespans and larger bodies tended to form more modular social networks, as did those where males were proportionally larger than females. Similar but weaker patterns were found between life history traits and social differentiation. Results from causal coevolutionary models provide preliminary evidence that social structure has been both a leader and follower…

items.title: Intensification of compound wind drought and heatwave events under climate change
items.summary_raw: Compound wind drought and heatwave (WDHW) events, defined as the co-occurrence of low wind speeds and high temperatures, pose growing risks to future power system stability. Yet their future evolution and underlying physical drivers remain poorly constrained. Using daily output from 27 downscaled CMIP6 models (~25 km), we identify a widespread intensification of these compound events over global land areas. Across the low- to high-CO 2 scenarios, global event frequency is projected to increase by 100 to 750% by 2100, with event duration lengthening by 80 to 300%. Mechanistically, this intensification is mainly driven by thermodynamic warming and widespread wind stilling, and further amplified regionally by enhanced climate variability and strengthened wind–temperature coupling associated with poleward jet streams. Applying an emergent-constraint framework that links observed historical trends to future projections can reduce intermodel variance by 10 to 40% at both global and regional scales. These results provide a physically grounded assessment of future compound WDHW risks, with direct implications for climate-impact assessment and energy-system planning.

items.title: Isotopically heavy carbon in the core
items.summary_raw: Constraining the origin of Earth’s carbon requires knowing the isotopic composition of the core—a geochemical signature long presumed to be beyond observation for the planet’s largest carbon reservoir. Here, we report high-precision δ 13 C measurements from Hawaiian plume melt inclusions entrapped before significant degassing and sampling distinct mantle sources. Melt inclusions from shield-stage lavas, interpreted to sample the plume’s central axis, inferred to be rooted in the core–mantle boundary thermal boundary layer, converge toward a primary δ 13 C signature of –1 ± 2‰. In contrast, melt inclusions from rejuvenated-stage lavas, derived from entrained mantle at the plume’s periphery, record a normal mantle source signature of –7 ± 2‰. We interpret the uniquely 13 C-rich shield-stage signature as the isotopic fingerprint of carbon exchanged from the core into the mantle. Our results point to 13 C-rich carbonaceous chondrites as the primary source of Earth’s carbon.

items.title: A monstrous El Niño has arrived. Here’s what it means for where you live.
items.summary_raw: A monster is growing in the Pacific — not the kraken, but something far scarier and deadlier. El Niño is a natural phenomenon in which a band of warm water forms every three to five years off the coast of South America. It raises ocean water temperatures by just a few extra degrees for typically nine to 12 months and ends up injecting an extraordinary amount of energy into the sky. It’s already the strongest El Niño on record , and it might not even peak for about another month or two. “Those are actually really big changes for the ocean,” Art Miller, a climate scientist at the Scripps Institution of Oceanography, told Grist in September. “The ocean has a lot of heat content — 1,000 times more ability to hold heat than the atmosphere — so slight changes in the ocean surface temperatures can actually do a lot for the atmosphere.” While scientists are still trying to figure out how climate change might be influencing El Niño, some research suggests that rising temperatures have led to stronger El Niño events. At the very least, we can use this event’s temporary warming to imagine what the climate will look like by default in two decades, as planetary temperatures continue to rise. The effects of the current El Niño will be global, and they will be severe. Scientists have estimated that the additional heat alone could kill around 450,000 people worldwide. Drought is gripping some places, like the Amazon rainforest , while extreme rainfall hits others, like the Greater Horn of…

items.title: 5 ways to prepare for El Niño’s extreme weather this winter
items.summary_raw: You may have heard about El Niño — the natural, recurring phenomenon that releases heat from the ocean into the atmosphere, influencing temperature and precipitation around the world. Its effects will differ this fall and winter depending on where you live, but heavy rainfall, flooding, and snowfall are some of the most likely impacts. There’s a lot of information available on navigating extreme weather, so we came up with five things you can do to prepare right now, from packing an emergency kit and bookmarking your local National Weather Service page to knowing how to stay safe around floodwaters. Read Next A monstrous El Niño has arrived. Here’s what it means for where you live. Grist staff 1. Sign up for local emergency alerts Your city or county has an emergency management department, which is part of the local government. Emergency managers are responsible for communicating with the public about disasters, managing rescue and response efforts, and coordinating among various agencies. They usually have an SMS-based emergency alert system, so sign up for those texts now. Some also have an app you can download. If you’re having trouble finding your local department, you can search for your state or territory here — but it’s easier to type your city or county name followed by “emergency management” into Google to quickly find the closest agency in your area. In larger cities, emergency management is often a standalone agency; in smaller communities, fire chiefs or sheriffs…

items.title: What to expect as world leaders gather for COP31
items.summary_raw: World leaders convene in Antalya, Turkey, on Monday for the United Nations’ 31st Conference of the Parties, or COP31 , after another year of deadly climate disasters. Forest fires in Canada , Indonesia , and Brazil impacted millions of people. Heat waves contributed to more than 50,000 deaths in Europe. Floods prompted by the collapse of a melting glacier killed more than 1,500 people in Nepal and caused nearly $5 billion in damages. And things may only get worse. This will be the first COP since the U.N.’s sobering report on the inevitability of breaching 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) of global warming. That temperature target was a focal point for climate ambition even before the landmark 2015 Paris Agreement , with scientists warning that exceeding that benchmark could push the planet past dangerous tipping points , triggering climatic changes that may be impossible to reverse. Despite the urgent need for action, few expect COP31, co-hosted by Turkey and Australia, to produce another breakthrough like the Paris Agreement or COP28’s call to transition away from fossil fuels . “There’s a whole bunch of decisions that have to be taken, but none of them on their own is going to make headlines,” said Kaveh Guilanpour, vice president of international strategies for the nonprofit Center for Climate and Energy Solutions. This is in part due to the nature of the negotiations. This year’s event is being referred to as an “implementation” COP, where countries will…
