items.title: Mytho-ecological isomorphism: a study of marine restoration through mythological narratives
items.summary_raw: Nature is understood as a part of human life through sacred narratives to sustain the environmental resources. When nature is exposed to environmental disturbances such as climate change, it adapts to these imbalances and restructures itself to maintain a stable state. This article employs the idea of ‘isomorphism’ to investigate self-regulation and transformation of marine ecology through mythological narratives. By drawing on Eugene Odum’s idea of ‘Homeostasis’ and Sterling and Eyer’s ‘Allostasis’, the self-regulation and transformation process of the marine system is explored in the paper. The marine ecosystem undergoes internal self-regulations naturally to sustain equilibrium despite minor fluctuations reflecting ‘homeostasis’. However, when environmental disturbances such as coral bleaching, rise in ocean temperature, etc., exceeds the ecological resilience, the ecosystem reorganizes the structure itself and continues to function without collapsing, reflecting the ‘allostatic’ state. ‘Homeostatic’ and ‘Allostatic’ self-regulatory functions find narrative parallels in Greek and Hindu mythological traditions. Mythological marine narratives often portray the disrupt symbolic orders, reorganise divine authority and restructure the system, reflecting restoration and transformation of the systematic order. The mythological marine narratives and the marine ecosystem restoration exhibit binary oppositions, presenting conflicting forces within a single ecological system. The…

items.title: A Comparative Review of Pollutant Fate and Climate Implications in Constructed and Natural Wetlands
items.source_name: International Journal of Natural Resources and Environmental Studies
items.summary_raw: Wetlands remove nitrogen, phosphorus and organic pollutants, yet the same biogeochemical processes also release carbon dioxide (CO2), methane (CH4) and nitrous oxide (N2O); improving water quality and affecting the climate are therefore two sides of one system. The comparison between constructed and natural wetlands in this review covers pollutant fate and greenhouse-gas effects together, and it also asks whether their evidence bases are comparable at all. A structured search of Web of Science and Scopus gave 60 candidate papers (2007–2026); 29 of them were kept as the core evidence base (14 focused mainly on constructed wetlands, 11 mainly on natural wetlands, and 4 on both), and they include laboratory and pilot experiments, field and long-term monitoring, modelling studies, reviews and bibliometric analyses. The paper gives a narrative comparison and does not claim to be a systematic review or a meta-analysis. Both wetland types remove pollutants through the same basic processes, such as sedimentation, adsorption, plant uptake and microbial transformation; the difference between them is one of emphasis and not of kind. Constructed wetlands are managed systems and remove about 60% of total nitrogen and 64% of total phosphorus, but they may emit N2O; natural wetlands store more carbon, but they are a source of CH4. Critically, the two types are usually reported with different indicators, units and system boundaries, so they cannot be ranked by a single removal efficiency…

items.title: Informality and the Business Environment as Drivers of Carbon Emissions: The Moderating Role of Environmental Regulatory Quality
items.summary_raw: ABSTRACT A low‐carbon transition cannot succeed while a substantial share of business activity remains beyond the effective reach of regulation. This study examines how informality and the business environment shape carbon emissions and whether regulatory quality conditions the environmental consequences of informal production. The analysis uses an annual panel of 145 economies over 2005–2020, combining data from the World Development Indicators and World Bank. Informality is measured using dynamic general equilibrium and Multiple Indicators Multiple Causes estimates, while nine disaggregated business‐environment dimensions capture firm entry, infrastructure, finance, taxation, trade and commercial institutions. Standard negative binomial regression constitutes the principal estimator, with Poisson regression, alternative informality measurement and income‐group estimations used for robustness. The results show that informality is consistently associated with lower aggregate CO 2 emissions, with the relationship strongest in low‐income economies and weakest in high‐income countries. This apparent environmental advantage reflects the small‐scale, labour‐intensive and capital‐constrained nature of informal production rather than inherently cleaner business practices. Most business‐environment indicators are associated with higher emissions, particularly in lower‐ to middle‐income economies, suggesting that enterprise expansion and energy demand may outpace the diffusion of…

items.title: Understanding pre-owned electric vehicle purchase intentions: An extended Theory of Planned Behavior approach
items.summary_raw: The electric vehicle (EV) market is expanding rapidly owing to environmental concerns that accelerate the shift toward sustainable transportation. Pre-owned EVs can widen adoption by offering a cost-effective alternative; however, they combine the traits of both new EVs and conventional used cars, creating decision complexities that remain understudied. To address this gap, we extend the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) with EV-specific benefit and risk and test the model using survey data from 347 licensed South Korean drivers with EV experience who plan to purchase vehicles. Our structural equation modeling shows that attitude ( β = 0.624), subjective norm ( β = 0.221), and perceived behavioral control ( β = 0.180) significantly enhance the intention to buy pre-owned EVs, with attitude being the strongest factor. Moreover, the proposed extended Theory of Planned Behavior accounts for 62.2% of the variance in pre-owned EV purchase intentions Users’ attitude grows with perceived benefit and declines with perceived risk. Critical motivation is the leading source of perceived benefit, whereas financial risk is the dominant perceived risk. The extended TPB framework provides evidence for clarifying how intrinsic motivations and EV-related risks shape consumer perceptions and ultimately purchase intention in the secondary EV market. Practically, policymakers and marketers should stress the environmental and symbolic merits of used EVs, supply transparent battery health metrics…

items.title: Research on the relationship between online public opinion and investor sentiment: from the perspectives of correlation and spillover effects
items.summary_raw: This study investigates the relationship between online public opinion and investor sentiment. Utilizing textual analysis and professional indicators, we construct an online public opinion index and an investor sentiment index. We then delineate their correlation and spillover effects under both “static and dynamic” and “normal and extreme” conditions. Findings reveal a consistently positive correlation and spillover effects across all scenarios. Investor sentiment frequently exhibits stronger outward spillovers in the estimated system. Furthermore, these interactions exhibit heterogeneity during bull and bear markets. Notably, the study identifies a structural breakpoint in these effects during the COVID-19 pandemic. These results provide evidence of the dynamic linkage between public opinion and market sentiment.

items.title: Patient safety climate in vaccination rooms from the perspective of vaccinators in Minas Gerais, Brazil: a cross-sectional study
items.summary_raw: Vaccination is a major strategy for preventing vaccine-preventable diseases; however, immunization errors remain a patient safety challenge. Evidence on the patient safety climate in vaccination services is limited, particularly from nursing professionals responsible for delivering and supervising these activities. This study aimed to analyze the patient safety climate and associated factors as perceived by nursing professionals working in vaccination rooms in Minas Gerais, Brazil. An analytical cross-sectional study was conducted with nursing professionals from vaccination rooms in 95 municipalities in Minas Gerais, Brazil, selected according to population size. Data were collected using the Brazilian version of the Safety Attitudes Questionnaire – Short Form, administered electronically. Descriptive and inferential analyses included nonparametric tests and correlation analyses. Effect sizes were estimated for statistically significant differences, adopting a 5% significance level. A total of 647 nursing professionals participated; 91.8% were women and 58.9% were nursing technicians or assistants. The mean Safety Attitudes Questionnaire score was 78.1 (SD = 10.3; 95% CI: 77.3–78.9), indicating a positive safety climate, although close to the cutoff of 75. Job Satisfaction had the highest score (86.9; SD = 15.7), whereas Perceptions of Management (70.7; SD = 17.2) and Stress Recognition (64.2; SD = 28.2) were below the cutoff. items.title: Evidence‐Based Learning for Climate Action: A Mixed‐Methods Intervention on Climate Change Hope and Water Footprint Behaviour
items.summary_raw: ABSTRACT To advance Sustainable Development Goal 13.3, geography education must strengthen human capacity and adaptive resilience through sustained climate action. This study investigates an Evidence‐Based Learning (EBL) intervention's impact on ninth‐graders' climate change hope and water footprint behaviour in Türkiye. Adopting a mixed‐methods design, the research integrated quasi‐experimental data ( N = 60) with qualitative insights from youth in the water‐stressed Mediterranean basin. Results indicate that EBL yielded modest but statistically significant initial gains in climate hope ( p = 0.005, d = 0.192) and encouraged positive within‐group trends for pro‐environmental actions, thereby supporting awareness and mitigation capacity (SDG 13.B). Theoretically, identifying a potential ‘sleeper effect’ in enacted habits and a shift towards ‘agency‐based hope’ illustrates how structured inquiry enables students to transcend eco‐paralysis through meaning‐focused coping. Engaging with ‘virtual water’ effectively helps translate intangible environmental concerns into tangible personal agency. These findings offer a framework for restructuring geography curricula and enhancing institutional capacity to foster proactive climate citizenship, advocating for evidence‐based inquiry over alarmist narratives to ensure global sustainability.

items.title: V Turecku začíná klimatická konference COP31. Jak zpomalit globální oteplování a omezit jeho dopady?
items.summary_raw: Od 9. do 20. listopadu se v turecké Antalyi koná 31. klimatická konference OSN (COP31). Zástupci států budou jednat o snižování emisí skleníkových plynů, financování klimatických opatření a přizpůsobování se dopadům klimatické změny. Přestože investice do klimatických opatření rostou, globální emise CO₂ zůstávají na rekordně vysokých hodnotách. Na nutnost řešit především příčiny klimatické změny, nikoliv pouze její následky, upozorňuje v rozhovoru pro Seznam Zprávy také Miroslav Trnka. Dopady klimatické změny se totiž neprojevují jen rostoucími teplotami a častějšími extrémy počasí, ale také postupným zhoršováním podmínek pro zemědělství a lesnictví, změnami dostupnosti a kvality vody či rostoucími ekonomickými škodami. Ochrana klimatu se tak stále výrazněji propojuje také s energetickou bezpečností, ekonomickou konkurenceschopností a dlouhodobou stabilitou společnosti. Celý článek je k dispozici zde.

items.title: The Economics of Agri-Food Supply Chain Resilience: Pandemics, Climate Shocks and Global Disruptions
items.summary_raw: Agri-food supply chain resilience has become a central economic concern as disease outbreaks, climatic extremes, trade restrictions and geopolitical disruptions expose interdependencies between production, processing, logistics, markets and household food access. Yet operational continuity alone is an incomplete measure of resilience: firms may recover output while consumers face unaffordable diets, workers lose earnings and costly buffers transfer risks between regions or supply-chain tiers. This critical narrative review examines how shocks propagate through agri-food systems, why decentralised incentives may diverge from social welfare, and which private and public responses are supported by credible evidence. Peer-reviewed empirical studies, theoretical analyses, simulations and substantive reviews published from 2004 to 4 September 2026 were assessed through targeted scholarly discovery, bibliographic verification and thematic appraisal, with earlier conceptual antecedents considered where necessary. The synthesis distinguishes covariate from localised shocks, physical scarcity from purchasing-power failures, and short-term recovery from economically and environmentally sustainable adaptation. Pandemic evidence indicates heterogeneous disruptions: substantial losses for particular workers, farmers and perishable-product channels coexisted with adaptive capacity in other markets. items.title: Can intelligent transportation steer towards a low-carbon future?
Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Designing Country-Specific Climate Mitigation and Sustainable Development Pathways
items.summary_raw: This study compares six machine-learning models for predicting per-capita CO2 emissions in a panel of 118 countries over 2000–2020 and uses SHAP to examine the fitted XGBoost model. The test sample comprises 2019–2020. XGBoost achieved the lowest test RMSE (0.475) and highest R2 (0.324), indicating limited to moderate predictive fit. GDP per capita had the largest means absolute SHAP value (0.2821), followed by the country effect (0.0361). Renewable-energy associations differed across observations and should not be interpreted as a uniform emissions reduction. Country profiles and four descriptive clusters illustrate possible areas for policy review; SHAP contributions are predictive associations, not causal effects or evaluated policy impacts.

items.title: Optimal scenario design for climate emulation
items.summary_raw: As deep learning for physical systems continues to grow in popularity, efforts to improve generalizability have primarily focused on designing architectures that embed physical constraints. However, for machine-learning surrogate climate models (emulators), we show that the low structural diversity in existing scenarios commonly used to generate training data places a ceiling on predictive skill. Here, we examine whether training datasets themselves can be optimized to improve generalization. We introduce a method to create datasets that produce emulators capable of generalizing to new, structurally different scenarios absent from the training data. We use a differentiable simple climate model (SCM) to calculate the sensitivity of emulator loss to perturbations in the training data, iteratively updating the training data to maximize emulator skill. For an SCM, an emulator trained on one scenario optimized in this fashion outperforms an emulator trained on six standard Scenario Model Intercomparison Project (ScenarioMIP) pathways. We achieve this higher predictive skill despite training on a smaller dataset, finding that our emulator successfully isolates distinct physical behaviors of different climate forcing agents (e.g., greenhouse gases vs. aerosols) without single-forcing runs. We then demonstrate that scenarios optimized using an SCM, when used to drive an intermediate-complexity climate model, produce a training dataset that yields a more skillful emulator than…

items.title: Archival and palaeoenvironmental documentation of extreme climate events reveals generational amnesia in collective memory
items.summary_raw: Collective memory shapes how societies respond to extreme climate events, yet long-term evidence on how the collective memory of such events becomes perceptually biased over time is lacking. Here, we utilise four centuries (1470-1900) of climatic archives from northern China, along with tree-ring-based hydroclimate reconstructions, which are validated against instrumental observations of Wet/Dry Index (1901-2000) to fill the gap. We find that historical records reveal systematic, non-random mismatches, where severity assessments are often biased toward recent experience rather than absolute climatic anomalies. Correlations between historical and natural records increase when the natural series is re-standardised using 20-40-year sliding windows, reflecting a generational offset. A heuristic agent-based model reproduces this pattern, suggesting that generational amnesia is sufficient to explain the offsets in perception of environmental change. We argue that historical archives carry a generational imprint of perceptual bias, in which the severity of climate extremes is judged against recent lived experience rather than long-term climate variability. This has implications for bias-aware corrections for risk assessment, adaptation, and paleoclimate reconstruction.

items.title: Do Information and Communication Technologies Promote Climate‐Smart Irrigation in Sub‐Saharan Africa?
items.summary_raw: ABSTRACT Irrigation is vital for climate resilience and food security in Sub‐Saharan Africa (SSA), yet its expansion remains constrained by climatic and structural barriers. Although information and communication technologies (ICTs) offer opportunities for climate‐smart irrigation, evidence across diverse SSA remains limited. Using panel data from 20 SSA countries (2000–2023), this study employs fixed‐effects (FE) and dynamic system–GMM (Generalized Method of Moments) estimators to examine the ICT–irrigation relationship, accounting for persistence and potential endogeneity. The findings reveal that ICT effects vary by technology and income level. Internet access consistently promotes irrigation development, particularly in low‐ and upper‐middle‐income economies, potentially by reducing information gaps and improving water management. Conversely, mobile phone penetration does not automatically generate irrigation gains and is negatively associated with irrigation development in lower‐middle‐income economies. Complementary conditions are also crucial: Electricity access and agricultural capital support irrigation development, whereas higher rainfall is associated with lower irrigation intensity, reflecting reduced reliance on irrigation. These findings reveal a development gradient in digital benefits, demonstrating that connectivity alone cannot drive irrigation expansion. Policies should therefore prioritize rural internet access alongside electrification, irrigation…

items.title: Exploring Pragmatic Strategies in English Media Discourse on Energy: A Scoping Review
items.source_name: Journal of Language Teaching and Research
items.summary_raw: This scoping review examines pragmatic and linguistic strategies employed in English-language media discourse on renewable energy in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, with implications for critical media literacy. A corpus of 450 media articles published between 2022 and 2024 was analyzed using a pragmatic framework focusing on speech acts, modality, hedging, stance markers, and framing strategies. Quantitative findings reveal that declaratives constitute 68% of evaluative statements, interrogatives 12%, and directives 20%. Epistemic modal expressions appear in 35% of predictions concerning renewable energy outcomes, while deontic modals account for 42% of prescriptive statements. Hedging devices are identified in 18% of evaluative claims, functioning to mitigate epistemic commitment. Positive stance markers are present in 54% of the articles, compared to 21% for negative stance markers. Qualitative analysis further demonstrates that media texts deploy face-saving strategies and nationalist discourse framing to construct renewable energy as both a civic obligation and a national strategic vision. The findings highlight how pragmatic language choices shape ideological positioning and public attitudes in media narratives. This scoping review contributes to the growing field of media discourse analysis and offers practical implications for integrating authentic media texts into language teaching curricula, developing learners' pragmatic competence, and fostering critical discourse…

items.title: Research on Stability of Carbon Fiber Lining for Artificial Caverns with Compressed Air Energy Storage
items.summary_raw: Compressed air energy storage is a large-capacity, long-term physical energy storage technology. With the advantages of safety, environmental protection and long life, it is moving from demonstration to large-scale commercial application driven by policy support and global energy transformation. Aiming at the problem of structural stability of underground caverns in CAES, the existing research mostly focuses on the mechanical response of unreinforced lining under cyclic internal pressure and in-situ stress field. However, there is a lack of systematic comparative analysis on the long-term dynamic stability of lining reinforced with carbon fiber-reinforced polymer under different cavern burial depths, cavern radii and surrounding rock grades. In this paper, an analysis model considering elastic–plastic mechanical behavior and stability theory is established, and the improvement effect of CFRP reinforcement on the mechanical properties of a cavern lining is systematically evaluated. Firstly, based on the complex variable function method and elastic–plastic theory, the analytical solutions of stress-displacement field of surrounding rock-lining structure under reinforced and unreinforced conditions are derived, respectively. By introducing the CFRP constraint effect, the correction formula of the maximum allowable cyclic internal pressure amplitude to maintain the dynamic stability of the structure is proposed. The accuracy of the numerical simulation is verified by the…

items.title: Recovery Without Reward: How Leadership and Policy Shaped the 2024 Queensland Election
items.summary_raw: ABSTRACT Queensland's political culture boasts a predilection for ‘strong’ leadership and ‘pragmatic’ policy where voters value decisive leaders while also rewarding governments capable of delivering ‘material’ economic outcomes. In the context of that culture, this article argues the 2024 Queensland election—producing a result very different from that long expected—came after substantial fluctuations in major party public opinion support between 2022 and 2024. It also argues Labor premier Steven Miles's social media campaign was a driver in his government's minor recovery, and that leadership approval did not translate directly into party support. Last, the article argues that crime, despite being a highly salient issue before and during the 2024 campaign, was nonetheless outweighed by ‘material’ economic concerns. Once again, Queensland voters' preference for pragmatic policy outcomes is confirmed.

items.title: Beyond tolerance: Distinct pathways shape human attitudes toward wildlife conflict
items.summary_raw: Abstract Human–wildlife conflict is driven by socio‐economic factors that are often overlooked or unaccounted for by most conservation plans and policies. These include social attitudes like tolerance of and opposition to wildlife which act and operate through distinct pathways rather than along a single continuum. Here, we distinguish these as two related but distinct attitudinal dimensions of human responses to wildlife conflict. Tolerance reflects attitudinal acceptance of wildlife conservation and coexistence despite conflicts, while opposition reflects support for lethal control and/or hunting as an attitudinal response toward wildlife‐related problems. Using household survey data ( n = 412) from the mid‐hills of far‐western Nepal and multi‐model inference, we found that acute shock due to livestock loss reduced tolerance but did not increase opposition, whereas crop loss reduced tolerance and increased opposition. Household financial capacity acted as a buffer against both reduced tolerance and increased opposition, while spatial proximity showed no effect. These findings reveal asymmetric pathways that challenge uniform approaches to conflict mitigation and point toward conflict‐type‐specific, equity‐based coexistence strategies.

items.title: Teachers’ Personal Aggressiveness and Its Correlation with Attitudes Toward School Conflict
items.summary_raw: The school environment is a complex phenomenon, which is not immune to conflict and aggression. Teachers’ attitudes toward aggression largely depend on their psychological profile. These attitudes were assessed based on teachers' responses to conflicts between students, their methods of signaling their attitudes, and their personal levels of aggression. The study sample consisted of 5,086 school teachers (94% female). Clustering was followed by a one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) and post-hoc multiple comparisons (Tukey or Games–Howell method). The resulting six clusters represented distinct attitudes toward student aggression and conflict mediation: undefined, emotionally undefined, passive, actively responsive, actively restrained, and indifferent. These attitudes correlated differently with such indicators of aggression as a propensity for physical aggression, anger, and hostility. The findings may be used to improve professional training programs for preventing destructive behavior in schools.

items.title: System-level value of carbon capture and utilization under emission caps, power-sector decarbonization, and industrial electrification: A spatial optimization analysis for Japan
items.summary_raw: Carbon capture and utilization (CCU) can supply low-carbon fuels to hard-to-abate sectors, but its value depends on conditions across the energy system. Existing studies have not identified when CCU creates system-level value while jointly considering spatial matching of CO 2 sources with utilization and storage sites, multi-resource competition, and endogenous price and demand responses. We embed price-responsive industrial demand in a spatially explicit electricity–fuel–CO 2 optimization model for 46 of Japan’s 47 prefectures. We evaluate the system-level value of CCU, the difference in optimal objective values with and without CCU, across 1331 scenarios combining 11 levels each of the emission cap, power-sector decarbonization, and industrial electrification. Their interactions explain 74.9% of the variation in CCU deployment. CCU has positive value in only 7.4% of scenarios, reaching about 1.66 trillion USD where a stringent emission cap coincides with low-carbon electricity. Improving the electricity consumption coefficient of synthetic-fuel production by 20% enlarges the positive-value region by only about 0.7 percentage points. Positive value requires a grid carbon intensity below about 0.109 t-CO 2 /MWh, just inside the bound set by the electricity needed for synthetic-fuel production; this boundary hardly depends on calibration or structural assumptions. Read as a long-run cross-sectional screening under the modeled conditions, the results show that CCU is not a…

items.title: Causes of Decline in Support for Joining the European Union in Serbia. Socio-Political Analysis
items.summary_raw: In this article, the author analyzes the support for joining the European Union in Serbia, trying to determine the key causes that influenced the decrease in support for European integration in Serbian society. The main causes of the decline in support for joining the European Union are the long duration of Serbia’s European integration process, insufficient cooperation with the Hague Tribunal, different understanding of the status of Kosovo and Metohija, and cultural factors, which are additionally emphasized by the current conflict between Russia and Ukraine. Serbia applied for membership in the European Union in December 2009, and received candidate status in March 2012. However, only two of the 35 chapters have been closed so far, so it is clear that Serbia has not advanced far on the path of European integration. This was also contributed to by the stagnation in the admission of new members. After the accession of 10 countries in 2004 and the admission of Romania and Bulgaria in 2007, in the last 16 years only Croatia has become a member. The reason the decline in support for European integration occurred is mainly due to the weakening of the soft power of the European Union and the reduction of its internal cohesion. In public opinion polls which were conducted during the last few years, one of the reasons for the decline in support for the European Union is the prevailing attitude of Serbian citizens that in the process of accession to the European Union it will be…

items.title: Heading with beheadings. Warring narratives in Mexico between the State and Drug-Trafficking Organisations (2006-2012)
items.source_name: Entreciencias diálogos en la Sociedad del Conocimiento
items.summary_raw: Purpose: This article analyses how competing narratives advanced by the Mexican State and drug-trafficking organisations were constructed and represented on newspaper front pages and across cultural industries during Felipe Calderón’s presidency (2006–2012), framing criminal violence as Mexico’s most serious problem. Methodological design: The study adopted an interdisciplinary qualitative design combining narrative analysis and cultural studies. Nearly 5,000 front pages from La Jornada and Milenio, published between January 2006 and December 2012, were reviewed through the newspapers’ digital archives. A corpus of 1,663 relevant headlines was identified, coded by keyword and thematic category, and analysed chronologically alongside selected cultural products. Results: Front-page coverage of drug-related violence increased sharply between 2006 and 2010 and declined from 2011 onwards. The federal government promoted a punitive narrative through speeches, media displays of detainees, and collaborations with television producers. Criminal organisations countered through narcomessages, executions, and public displays of bodily violence that asserted territorial power and challenged State authority. Research limitations: The analysis is confined to the 2006–2012 period, two national newspapers, and a purposive selection of cultural products; it therefore does not represent the full range of regional media coverage or cultural production. Findings: Although positioned as…

items.title: Jaká bude letošní zima? A proč bude její průběh důležitý pro zásoby vody v Česku?
items.summary_raw: Zda nás čeká mírná zima, nebo výraznější mrazy a sněžení, zatím nelze spolehlivě předpovědět. Sezonní předpovědi pro střední Evropu jsou zatíženy značnou nejistotou. Dlouhodobý trend je však zřejmý. V důsledku klimatické změny ubývá v Česku dnů se sněhovou pokrývkou i mrazových dnů. Stále větší část zimních srážek přichází v podobě deště a sníh se v krajině udrží kratší dobu. Zásadní otázkou nadcházející zimy tak bude doplňování zásob podzemních vod, které jsou aktuálně v řadě oblastí výrazně podprůměrné a na některých místech se blíží historickým minimům. Právě zimní období a začátek jara jsou pro doplňování těchto zásob klíčové. Výpar i spotřeba vody vegetací jsou nízké a voda ze srážek má větší možnost vsakovat se do půdy. Významnou roli přitom může sehrát postupné odtávání sněhové pokrývky. Na nejistotu sezonních předpovědí i dlouhodobé změny charakteru českých zim upozorňuje v rozhovoru pro Seznam Zprávy také Miroslav Trnka. Celý článek je k dispozici zde .

items.title: All IPCC AR6 regions are close to their 1.5 °C- and 2 °C-equivalent warming limits
items.summary_raw: Global temperatures have averaged 1.2 °C above pre-industrial levels over the past decade, yet regional warming patterns and remaining warming budgets under Paris Agreement limits remain uncertain owing to insufficient historical observations. Here we quantify and attribute warming across all IPCC Sixth Assessment Report (AR6) regions since pre-industrial times using a Bayesian framework combining multi-model simulations with observations, enabling robust estimates in data-sparse regions. Regional warming is already pronounced. By 2025, attributed regional warming had reached about 90–94% of the levels expected at 1.5 °C global warming and 65–76% of those expected at 2 °C. Attribution confidence is the highest in tropical regions, including much of Africa, where low internal variability enables robust results. Attributed warming is the greatest in northern high-latitude regions, exceeding 2.5 °C. Greenhouse gases dominate, partially offset by aerosol cooling. These results reveal that current warming is already indistinguishable from a 1.5 °C world, highlighting the shared urgency of adaptation across all regions. Climate targets are set for global temperatures, but what they mean regionally is less clear. Here the authors quantify the amount of human-induced warming in individual IPCC regions and find that, by 2025, they had reached 90–94% (65–76%) of their expected warming levels at the 1.5 °C (2 °C) global warming thresholds.

items.title: Fatores psicológicos sobre a intenção de produtores de leite em intensificar o uso de Inseminação Artificial no rebanho
items.source_name: Revista em Agronegócio e Meio Ambiente
items.summary_raw: Brazil’s low average milk productivity reflects family-based systems with limited technological adoption and socioeconomic barriers. An online questionnaire was administered to 100 dairy farmers in nine Brazilian states to investigate artificial insemination (AI) adoption. Regression and structural equation modeling were used to analyze relationships among socioeconomic and productive variables, the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) constructs, Attitude (ATT), Subjective Norm (SN), and Perceived Behavioral Control (PBC), and the Intention (INT) to intensify AI use in the herd. Despite its bias toward younger, digitally connected farmers, the sample represents an emerging segment. INT decreased with age (r = ?0.33). ATT (mean 4.68/5) and SN (mean 4.38/5) were significant positive predictors. Education and association membership were not directly associated with INT but may influence it indirectly through ATT and SN, highlighting the role of family members, technicians, and cooperatives. Thus, extension strategies should strengthen ATT by demonstrating the genetic and economic benefits of AI, and SN by promoting the exchange of experiences among farmers in associations and technical events. These actions may help expand AI adoption in dairy farming and narrow the gap with beef cattle farming.

items.title: KNOWLEDGE, ATTITUDES, AND ADOPTION READINESS FOR RESPONSIBLE FISHING AMONG FISHERS IN THE BANDA ISLANDS, MALUKU
items.summary_raw: Environmentally responsible fishing requires gear and operational practices that maintain selectivity, reduce unwanted catch and habitat impacts, comply with management rules, and remain feasible for fishers. This study aimed to describe self-reported knowledge, attitudes, and perceived adoption readiness for environmentally responsible fishing practices among the surveyed tuna handline and mini purse seine fishers in the Banda Islands and to compare scores between the two groups. A cross-sectional quantitative survey was conducted in June–July 2025 using purposive sampling. The sample comprised 51 fishers, including 18 tuna handline fishers and 33 mini purse seine fishers. Sixteen of 20 questionnaire items met the item-validity criterion (r > 0.33), and each retained variable had Cronbach’s alpha above 0.70. Item responses were summarized descriptively, and the two independent groups were compared using Mann–Whitney U tests. Knowledge did not differ significantly between tuna handline and mini purse seine fishers (U = 313.0, p = 0.757, rank-biserial r = 0.054). Mini purse seine fishers had higher attitude scores (U = 191.0, p = 0.037, r = 0.357 and perceived-adoption-readiness scores (U = 179.0, p = 0.020, r = 0.397. Combined item means nevertheless remained modest: knowledge ranged from 1.96 to 2.59, attitudes from 1.98 to 3.38, and perceived adoption readiness from 2.25 to 2.80. The findings indicate group differences in perceptions and enabling conditions, not verified…

items.title: Data centres asymmetrically exacerbate energy burdens through wholesale price increases and regressive grid cost shifting
Regional climate change approaches Paris limits
items.summary_raw: Nature Climate Change, Published online: 09 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02797-5 It has been surprisingly difficult to calculate how much warming different regions of the Earth have experienced since pre-industrial times. Now, research shows that in most land regions, the temperature thresholds that governments agreed to in Paris to keep below are already dangerously close.

This narrative review explores the clinical and public health impacts of these shifting paradigms, highlighting the urgent need to address Neglected Tropical Diseases and to adopt a global "One Health" approach to mitigate future health threats.

items.title: The Current State of Global Climate Policy: How to Improve Regional Cooperation
items.summary_raw: This paper provides an update on the current state of climate policies and proposes a policy framework that can improve regional cooperation. Global greenhouse gas emissions will continue to rise to 2050 under current policies, according to projections from the G-Cubed multi-country model. We evaluate an approach to international climate cooperation to substantially reduce greenhouse gas emissions designed to sustain participation: national policies implemented through domestic institutions; a common reference carbon price adjusted for national emissions intensities; free allocation of carbon bonds, which transfers wealth to households and firms while the policy continues; and a safety valve that caps carbon prices at an agreed, negotiated level. This is based on the Hybrid/CALM framework of McKibbin and Wilcoxen (2002b) and McKibbin (2020). We compare three scenarios of halving greenhouse gas emissions from all sectors (except LULUCF) from 2023 emissions by 2050, with carbon pricing beginning in 2027: (i) a uniform national reduction target met with country-specific carbon taxes; (ii) a common US dollar carbon tax in all countries; and (iii) a common reference price adjusted by emissions-intensity multipliers, which illustrates the price differentiation in the Hybrid/CALM approach. Emissions outside the Middle East and North Africa, which is exempt from pricing, fall by about 49 percent from 2023 levels by 2050 in all three scenarios. A Hybrid/CALM mechanism narrows the…

items.title: Building a Canadian Industrial Strategy: Adaptive Governance for Integrated Energy and Economic Policy
items.summary_raw: Abstract What one influential Science Council report said in 1979 could still be said today: “Canada has had an industrial policy… [but], Canada has not had a coherent industrial strategy” (Science Council of Canada, 1979). Canada has long offered supports for specific industries yet has not developed an integrated set of complementary measures to achieve strategic objectives. Institutional, cultural, and economic barriers continue to push against holistic approaches in favour of fragmented sectoral policies that can be dominated by strong incumbents. We argue that the net‐zero transition and geopolitical imperatives alike require a strategic approach that confronts these challenges directly by treating decarbonization, energy security, and economic competitiveness as a single integrated project. We outline how to do effective industrial strategy despite the multiple barriers, presenting recommendations for state capacity development, adaptive governance institutions, and effective policy mechanisms most likely to advance a geopolitically resilient transition in Canada.

items.title: Climate change and health through “primary care physicians’ eyes”: a qualitative study
items.summary_raw: BACKGROUND: The revised European Definition of General Practice acknowledges primary care physicians' (PCPs) role in integrating environmental concerns and planetary health into daily practice, and strengthening community climate resilience and literacy. Data on PCPs' perceptions regarding their role in the climate crisis are scarce. AIM: To explore how PCPs perceive climate health impacts, conceptualize their role and define their professional priorities regarding planetary health and sustainability. METHODS: PCPs with at least one year's work experience were recruited through a national professional network. Purposive sampling captured diversity in gender, various levels of work experience, region (urban, semi-urban, rural, and island) and work settings (public and private). Semi-structured individual interviews were conducted remotely and recorded. Thematic analysis was used. FINDINGS: Fifteen PCPs participated. Though few were unconvinced, almost all recognized climatic change and its impact on their community's health: increased morbidity and mortality from extreme weather, more respiratory, infectious diseases and chronic conditions, encumbered mental health, and lower food quality. Our findings indicate conflicting viewpoints over PCPs' role in the climate crisis, with most regarding themselves as advocates for climate resilience and sustainability of medical practices as well as educators of their community. Chronic fatigue, ill-preparedness, and perceived state…

items.title: How Can a Circular Economy for Sustainable Tourism be Assessed? Evidence From an Ecological Resort in Taiwan
items.summary_raw: ABSTRACT Climate mandates pressure the tourism and hospitality industry to decarbonize rapidly, making circular economy implementation in fragile destinations an immediate priority. Hotels usually focus inward on building efficiencies. Ecological resorts, however, must operate within natural environments, a difference requiring a specialized framework that bridges natural resource assessment with stakeholder collaboration to reduce environmental degradation. We thus developed a circular framework tailored for forest eco‐resorts via a mixed‐methods design using three distinct panels. We ran a fuzzy Delphi survey to refine the indicators, used the analytic hierarchy process with 25 experts to weight them, and assessed practical field performance via 79 employee responses. This process yielded 52 indicators spanning seven subcategories. The conservation of natural resources scored the highest weight (0.0514), followed closely by the installation of water‐saving equipment (0.0433). The quadrant distributions demonstrated that destinations must first implement advanced technical strategies for robust wastewater treatment to anchor macrolevel circularity before behavioral programs can mature successfully. These indicators, ultimately, offer a robust assessment instrument for sustainable development throughout the eco‐resort sector.
